### Agent surface (Base-delivered)

#### BASE-AGENT-001 — One MCP door per seed

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every seed, hosted or self-hosted, serves one remote MCP endpoint at `/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. It speaks the current revision (2026-07-28) and accepts 2025-11-25 clients through the twelve-month deprecation window. It implements `server / discover`, tools, resources and prompts. Lists are deterministic and carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope: "private"`. Roots, Sampling and Logging are not served.

**Acceptance.**
1. `server / discover` returns the supported versions, capabilities, `serverInfo` and instructions.
2. A 2026-07-28 request works with no handshake, and a 2025-11-25 client completes `initialize` and lists the same tools.
3. An unsupported version returns `UnsupportedProtocolVersion`.
4. Two `tools / list` calls return the same order, with cache fields.
5. A foreign Origin returns 403, and a header and body method mismatch returns `HeaderMismatch`.
6. An oversized body returns 413 with no effect.

#### BASE-AGENT-002 — The seed's jobs are tools, through the UI's own actions

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Each Core job a person does in the product is a tool. Where one is not, the Agent surface says why: it runs on a device, it is a person's interactive screen, it belongs to a connector or the import door, or it is an installation fact. Risk is never the reason: a risky job is a tool with its class (BASE-AGENT-006). Tools are named `<seed>.<area>.<verb>` and declare input and output schemas and truthful annotations. Each calls the same server action as the UI, so validation and authorization are written once, and the seed's embedded agents use the same registry. A business refusal returns `isError` with the seed's stable error code.

**Acceptance.**
1. The Core clause ids in each tool's `_meta`, with the not-a-tool reasons that `server / discover` serves, cover every Core clause in the contract, and no reason is risk; the harness and `rer check` fail on a gap.
2. Each tool's fixture result validates against its `outputSchema`.
3. Read tools declare `readOnlyHint`; tools that can carry destructive declare `destructiveHint`, and tools that can carry external declare `openWorldHint`.
4. A refusal returns the same error code the UI gets for the same action.
5. The UI action and its tool, on the same fixture, give the same record state and the same audit event type.
6. The seed's embedded agents appear in the audit as calls to the same tools.

#### BASE-AGENT-003 — Records are resources

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Each primary record type has a URI template, and tools return `resource_link`s to the records they touch. A read returns exactly the fields the caller's role sees in the UI. File bytes count against any byte budget on the grant. A record the caller cannot open reads as not found, identical to a missing id. Text from customers, imports or files carries an untrusted marker in `_meta`.

**Acceptance.**
1. `resources / templates / list` names every record type in the Agent surface.
2. Reads as two roles return exactly what the UI shows each.
3. An out-of-scope id and a missing id give identical responses.
4. A write's `resource_link` reads back the new state.
5. Bytes over budget return `budget_exhausted` and no partial content.
6. Customer-sourced text carries the untrusted marker.

#### BASE-AGENT-004 — Business identity and short-lived, audience-bound tokens

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** The door is an OAuth 2.1 resource server. Its RFC 9728 metadata names the authorization servers this installation trusts. That is the paired Business when Business provisioned it, verified with the owner-claim trust the installation already holds for its import door; otherwise it is the seed's own sign-in. Access tokens are RFC 9068 JWTs with `aud` set to the seed's canonical MCP URI, `sub` the sponsoring person, `act` the agent (RFC 8693) with its specialist, scopes per tool family, and a lifetime of 15 minutes or less (5 by default). The policy scopes rules on the sponsor, agent and specialist the token names. The consent behind the tokens can last longer and is revocable. Tokens travel only in the Authorization header, and there is no passthrough.

**Acceptance.**
1. An unauthenticated call returns 401 with `resource_metadata`, and the metadata names the trusted servers and scopes.
2. A Business token for this seed works, and the same token sent to a sibling seed returns 401.
3. An expired token returns 401, and a token with a lifetime over 15 minutes is refused.
4. A read-only token calling a write tool returns 403 `insufficient_scope` with every needed scope in one challenge.
5. A token in a query string is refused and not logged.
6. Revoking consent in the seed or in Business refuses the next call within 60 seconds.
7. After unpairing, Business tokens are refused and the seed's own sign-in still works.

#### BASE-AGENT-005 — An agent acts as a person in a role, never more

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every call is authorized as the sponsoring person's current role and access (BASE-ACCESS-004), intersected with the grant's resources, actions and budget. A grant only narrows. No call widens the calling agent's own authority. A call that would widen its own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the company policy or Pause, is refused with `self_escalation`, whatever the policy says; narrowing its own grant is allowed. Other access and security changes are ordinary actions in the access and security classes. An agent never acts after its sponsor is suspended. Anything an agent reads (records, files, emails, imports, other seeds' results) is data and cannot change its scope, its targets or a call's class.

**Acceptance.**
1. For each role fixture, every tool's allow or deny through MCP equals the UI's for the same action.
2. A one-folder, read-only grant holds, and widening through arguments is refused.
3. Downgrading the sponsor changes the next call's result, and suspending the sponsor returns 401.
4. Calls that widen the agent's own grant or its sponsor's role, or change the policy or Pause, return `self_escalation` and change nothing, even under a policy with every class autonomous; dropping a scope from its own grant runs.
5. An injection fixture yields no out-of-grant call and no change of class: record text asking for a wider action, or claiming that a recipient is internal.

#### BASE-AGENT-006 — Every action declares its risk class

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Classes come from the fleet list in RISK-POLICY.md: standard, external, money, commitment, accounts, gated, access, security, destructive, sensitive and live. In the registry, each tool declares the classes it can carry and a server-side classifier that decides them per call from the arguments, current records and, for gated, the provider's answer. The classifier also supplies each class's facts: the measure (items, recipients, amount and currency, people or records), the counterparty (internal, known, new or public), the direction for access, the provider and step for gated, and the data kind for sensitive. A classifier never reads a flag, label or claim supplied by the agent or by record text. A seed cannot add a class; it proposes one for the fleet list.

**Acceptance.**
1. Every tool in `tools / list` carries its possible classes in `_meta`, equal to the Agent surface table.
2. For each tool, fixture calls cover every class it can carry, and the computed classes and facts equal the fixture's expected values.
3. An argument or record text asserting a class or a confirmation (`internal: true`, `confirmExternal: true`) leaves the computed classes unchanged.
4. Money calls carry amount and currency, external calls their counterparty and recipient count, access calls their direction, and destructive calls their item count.
5. No tool in `tools / list` declares a class outside the fleet list, and `rer check` fails on one.
6. A refused call's audit row still records its computed classes.

#### BASE-AGENT-007 — The company's policy decides, at one chokepoint

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every agent door calls one decision function: MCP, the integration API with agent tokens, and the seed's embedded agents. It evaluates the call's classes against the company's policy, as above. The seed ships no dispositions and fills no gap with one: agent access opens only under a complete policy that setup has asked for (RISK-POLICY.md), and before then every agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing. *Autonomous* runs the call. *Review* runs it and adds it to the review feed. *Approval* saves a pending action with server-computed facts and returns `input_required`, with a URL-mode elicitation to the seed's approval page and a pending handle. Each person the rule names approves the exact saved revision in a signed-in browser, and changed inputs need a new approval. The retried call returns the result and a receipt. A rejection returns `approval_rejected`, and a lapse past the wait the rule sets returns `approval_expired`. *Blocked* returns `policy_blocked`, naming the class, rule and revision.

**Acceptance.**
1. The Base harness runs each tool under each disposition for every class it can carry, and sees it run, run and enter the review feed, wait with no effect, or be refused.
2. Before setup is complete, the setup page lists every class the seed's tools carry with examples and no answer pre-selected, an agent call returns `policy_unset` with the setup link and changes nothing, and an incomplete revision cannot be confirmed; a `*` rule completes it, and a tool an upgrade adds with an unanswered class appears in `tools / list` once that class is answered, while the other tools keep running.
3. Under "money autonomous up to $500, approval up to $10,000, blocked above", calls of $400, $600 and $20,000 run, wait and are refused; a per-day cap sends the call that crosses it to the next rule.
4. A call carrying two classes takes the stricter disposition.
5. An approval shows server-computed facts and an expiry, returns the URL elicitation and a handle, and completes once after the named approver approves; a changed input needs a new approval, and a rejection or lapse leaves no effect.
6. The same call through MCP, the integration API and an embedded agent gets the same decision.
7. A policy change applies to the next call within 60 seconds, and the audit cites the new revision.
8. A policy document with a bad signature or another Business's id is rejected, and the door keeps the last valid revision.

#### BASE-AGENT-008 — Truthful attribution

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every agent act is recorded and shown as `"<agent> for <person>"`, and mail and messages an agent sends outside name it that way as their sender. An approval, a review mark, a confirmation (a warning dialog, a typed-field confirmation, a delivery confirmation), a decision or a signature attributed to a person comes only from that person's signed-in session. When an agent does the equivalent act, the record names the agent, and the act carries its own class; a binding decision or a signature is commitment. Agent doors ignore arguments that stand for a person's confirmation. No tool solves a bot check, or enters a person's own password or 2FA code at an outside service. A provider step that demands a person goes to a person, whatever the policy says; the gated class marks such steps before they run.

**Acceptance.**
1. An agent call carrying a person-confirmation flag is classified and decided exactly as without it.
2. Approving, marking reviewed or answering a policy question with an agent or device token returns 403 and changes nothing.
3. A form-mode elicitation "accept" never completes an approval.
4. Where an agent's decision, signature or field confirmation runs without a person, it reads `"<agent> for <person>"` in the record, the activity view, exports and any certificate, never as the person's own act.
5. After a person approves an agent's prepared action, the record shows the person as approver and the agent as preparer.
6. Activity and exports at 1440 and 390 show `"<agent> for <person>"` for every agent act.
7. Mail an agent sends to an outside address names `"<agent> for <person>"` as its sender.

#### BASE-AGENT-009 — Every agent action is audited with its class and decision

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Extending BASE-OPS-005, each call that reads private data or changes anything records the agent client, name and specialist, and the run or task id (`traceparent` when sent); the sponsoring person, the grant, the tool and the targets; the classes and their facts, and the policy revision and rule; the decision (autonomous, review, approval, blocked, unset or self_escalation) and the outcome (done, refused, pending or failed); the approval or review id and person, and the idempotency key. For a period, the seed's Agents page shows actions by class and decision with the notable ones, the review feed (Mark reviewed, Flag, and Undo where reversible), pending approvals, steps waiting for a person and setup questions. Business shows the same across seeds.

**Acceptance.**
1. One write leaves a complete audit row.
2. Refused, pending, unset and self-escalation calls are audited.
3. The Agents page's counts by class and decision equal the audit rows on a fixture week.
4. The review feed lists exactly the calls decided as review; Mark reviewed records the person, and Undo restores a reversible one.
5. Filtering by agent or class lists only those rows, and export includes every field.
6. Removing the agent keeps its rows and its name.
7. The Agents page works at 1440 and 390 with no serious or critical axe findings.

#### BASE-AGENT-010 — Agents can follow changes

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** The seed emits a typed event for every record change and for every approval, review and policy decision. Each event carries a stable id, a type, the record URI, the actor (a person, or an agent acting for a person) and a time. Events never carry secrets or more than the subscriber may read. Agents can read events three ways: `subscriptions / listen`, an `events.list` tool with a cursor, and signed webhooks from Base `integrations` using the same ids. Every channel delivers at least once and filters by access at delivery.

**Acceptance.**
1. A subscribed record changed in the UI produces a notification within 10 seconds.
2. `events.list` returns the same event id the webhook carries.
3. Replaying from a cursor returns the same ids in order.
4. After access is revoked, no channel delivers events about that record.
5. A failed webhook is visible and replays without duplicate effects.
6. `approval.pending`, `approval.decided`, `review.flagged` and `policy.adopted` carry the class and decision and nothing the subscriber may not read.

#### BASE-AGENT-011 — Limits are policy, and Pause stops everything

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Business limits are rules in the company's policy: per-call and per-day thresholds on any class's measure, such as money moved, outside recipients or items destroyed; spend caps on provider cost (models, SMS, email) per seed, specialist or agent, which setup asks with the classes; "no cap" is an answer. Tools with provider cost declare an estimate before they run, and an exhausted cap returns `budget_exhausted` before any partial effect. The seed's capacity limits (request rate, body and byte sizes) protect the installation: they bound rate and size, never daily business volume, are documented and are not policy. A grant carries budgets only when the person granting it sets them. A **Pause agents** control in the seed, and Pause all agents in Business when paired, refuses every agent token within 60 seconds until a person resumes; browser sessions and devices keep working.

**Acceptance.**
1. A rate overrun returns 429 with `Retry-After`.
2. A per-day cap of three outside recipients sends the fourth to the rule that applies past the cap.
3. An exhausted spend cap returns `budget_exhausted` with no partial effect and shows the spend.
4. Under the answer "no cap", a spending call runs and its spend shows in usage; a call that spends nothing is unaffected by any cap.
5. The usage view shows calls, decisions by class, money moved and provider spend per agent.
6. Pause and Pause all agents each stop the next call within 60 seconds, and resume restores access.
7. An agent token cannot resume.

#### BASE-AGENT-012 — Writes are idempotent and conflict-safe

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** Every mutating tool requires an idempotency key and takes an optional expected revision. The same key with the same arguments returns the first outcome for at least 24 hours; the same key with different arguments returns `idempotency_conflict`; a stale revision returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision. Long work returns a job handle and a status tool, with no dependence on the Tasks extension.

**Acceptance.**
1. Two calls with one key give one effect and equal results.
2. A retry with a new JSON-RPC id and the same key, after a dropped stream, returns the recorded outcome.
3. The same key with different arguments returns a conflict and no effect.
4. A stale revision returns a conflict naming the current revision.
5. A job handle used by another person's token reads as not found.

#### BASE-AGENT-013 — Manifest, docs and the conformance journey

*Tier:* Agent surface

**Requirement.** `server / discover` instructions and an on-site `/docs/agents` page are generated from the action registry. The page lists tools by job, with each tool's classes, the test that adds each computed class, its scopes, resource templates, event types, capacity limits and error codes, and the specialist role. `prompts / list` carries the specialist's jobs. Base ships the conformance journey, a harness that `rer verify` runs against `rer dev` and seeds run in CI. It is an MCP client; a signed-in test person takes a person's steps (setup answers, approvals, review marks, resume) through the URLs the door returns, and the same browser leg runs the UI-parity actions and the page checks at 1440 and 390. It runs every acceptance point of BASE-AGENT-001 to 012 and of the seed's SURFACE clauses under two company policies: *all autonomous* (`*`), and *held* (standard review, every other class the seed declares approval, which the test person grants), plus the single-class variants a point names. A point that names no disposition passes under both.

**Acceptance.**
1. The docs list exactly the names in `tools / list` and `resources / templates / list`.
2. Each tool's classes, and the test behind each computed one, are documented.
3. The harness fails on any of: a tool without a schema; an effect under approval or blocked, or before setup is complete; a computed class that differs from its fixture; a flag that changes a class or completes a person's step; a role-parity mismatch; a wrong-audience token being accepted; a duplicate effect on retry.
4. Every acceptance point runs under both policies, every decision matches the policy in force, and under all autonomous no call waits for a person or is refused by policy.
5. A stranger agent given only the seed URL completes the specialist journey through MCP.

### Agent surface

**Specialist: Triage engineer.** It keeps the business's application errors captured, grouped, owned and tied to verified repairs, acting for the person who sponsors it.

Inherits BASE-AGENT-001 to BASE-AGENT-013. The company's policy decides every call; this section presets none.

**How Spool computes each class.**
- *standard*: reads of issues, events, packets, outcomes, releases, reports and the audit; triage, assignment, comments, priority, saved views, grouping proposals, grouping corrections and rules (each undone by undo or a rule-version rollback), alert rules and snoozes, release, deployment, repair and suspect records, tracker tickets in the business's own tracker, reproductions in the isolated runner, a draft fix in a private repository, member notification settings, a legal hold or a longer retention window, code mappings, and exports to the person asking. A reversible internal action keeps standard when another class is added. Facts are the item count.
- *external*: anything that reaches or exposes data to someone outside the business: an invitation or identity-visibility grant to a person or service outside the business, a reply to an end user's feedback, an alert or resend to a destination outside the business's own workspaces and domains, a draft fix, merge, comment or tracker ticket in a public repository, a tracker ticket exposed outside the business, trace context forwarded to an outside provider, source-fetch requests to an outside origin and evidence sent to an outside model provider. Facts are the recipient count and the counterparty: *known* for a person, service, reporter, destination, repository, provider or origin already on record, *new* otherwise, *public* for a public repository.
- *money*: a budget, cap, plan or overage change, a raised artifact storage cap and a paid longer retention window. Facts are the USD amount and the payee.
- *commitment*: accepting the billing partner's terms. Facts are the document and the counterparty.
- *accounts*: installing a provider application (a GitHub App, a GitLab application, a Slack, Teams, PagerDuty, Jira or Linear app, a Vercel or Netlify integration) at an outside service. Facts are the provider.
- *gated*: a provider's consent screen in a person's own account, and card entry at the billing partner's hosted checkout. Facts are the provider and the step.
- *access*: organization members, teams, roles, project keys, agent grants, identity-access roles and the verified successor handoff during owner erasure. Facts are the people and whether the change widens or narrows.
- *security*: server-side scrubbing rules, the identity policy, the commit author and message sharing choice, allowed domains, sign-in, SSO, SCIM and MFA settings, replay consent and masking, source-fetch secret headers, project credentials, and provider credential connection, rotation and revocation, including tracker credentials. Facts are the setting.
- *destructive*: project, end-user and owner erasure, irreversible conversion of retained identity from keep to hash or drop or from hash to drop, a shortened event or replay retention window and the cutoff it runs, a removed alert destination and replay references irreversibly removed on disconnect. Facts are the item count.
- *live*: inbound filters, project item limits, DSN key rate limits, event or replay sampling, spike protection, billing budgets or caps that change intake, loader settings, check-in routes, detector thresholds, a release ordering rule that changes intake or regression, promoting an evaluated agent-runtime candidate and merging a fix into the branch the buyer deploys from, including an authorized resend of that merge. Facts are the project and the setting.
- Spool stores no health, ID, bank, card or payroll numbers, because SDK-003 and ERR-003 scrub them before storage, so it declares no sensitive class.

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-DATA-004, BASE-AGENT-004, BASE-AGENT-005 · *Rules:* D-1 · *Register:* R-18

**Requirement.** Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Claude can consume the same permissioned CLI/MCP packet, source/release links, gaps and current repair observations. Read-only diagnosis never silently acquires repository write or production authority. The named agent clients themselves are register row R-18.

2. Cross-project, mutation and prompt-injection requests are refused.

#### AI-002 — Generate and test the smallest reproduction

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-011 · *Register:* R-1

**Requirement.** An agent combines sanitized occurrence, exact release/build/symbol/source artifacts, breadcrumbs, trace/replay and the input its grant allows to construct and minimize a deterministic reproduction. It tests competing causes and records counterexamples, failing input, environment and unsuccessful attempts in an isolated budgeted runner for each supported runtime/mobile target. No production credentials/network access are inherited; repository scope and dependency/network policy come from the agent's grant, which the agent never widens itself, and its cost stays within the company's spend caps. Unsupported, not reproduced, failed and reproduced remain distinct.

**Acceptance.**
1. For a real captured failure chosen for reproduction, the runner yields a minimal failing case and a competing-cause experiment.
2. Malicious telemetry, timeout and missing-artifact cases each end in their named state.
3. Repeated against the fixed release, the failure no longer reproduces.
4. A failed setup never becomes a not-reproduced success.

#### AI-003 — Minimal code repair as a tested pull request

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-007 · *Rules:* D-1, D-3 · *Register:* R-10

**Requirement.** From a reproduction and a repository grant, an agent prepares the smallest source change and regression case, compares candidates, runs the buyer's relevant tests/type/build/security checks in isolation and opens a draft GitHub PR or GitLab merge request with failing-before/passing-after evidence, changed files, risks and unresolved cases. A trigger rule that starts an investigation stays within the grant's scope and the company's spend caps. Writing to the provider and merging are calls with their classes (a draft branch or pull request is standard, or external in a public repository; a merge is live), which the company's policy decides; the agent never widens its own repository scope, and deployment stays the buyer's own CI/CD. Prompt content cannot authorize changes or bypass CI.

**Acceptance.**
1. A scoped repair yields a real source patch and a regression case that fails before and passes after.
2. One draft PR or MR opens.
3. Cancelling, expiring or revoking between steps leaves durable results, with no unauthorized write and no duplicate branch.

#### AI-004 — Prove the released repair from live rates

*Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-3 · *Register:* R-19

**Requirement.** Once a fix is merged and deployed and its success criteria are set, an agent links the fix commit to actual deployed cohorts and exercises the failing customer flow. Compare before/after failure rates against observed comparable traffic, confidence/minimum exposure, adoption, sampling, old releases, capture loss, retention and grouping changes. Require the reproduction to pass and live evidence to support improvement; continue a bounded watch and reopen/escalate recurrence. Quiet or missing telemetry is inconclusive, never success. Show the exact denominator, window, counterexamples and reasons; the engineer may stop or revise criteria without rewriting observations. A buyer's live production traffic is register row R-19.

**Acceptance.**
1. With a fix deployed to only part of traffic and known healthy and failing flow exposure generated, the rate comparison shows its denominator, window and counterexamples.
2. Old-version errors and capture gaps make the verdict inconclusive.
3. With coverage restored the criteria are reached, and a later recurrence reads recurred.
4. The recurrence raises one accountable follow-up.

#### AI-005 — Explain grouping proposals before applying

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-AGENT-007, BASE-AGENT-008 · *Rules:* D-4

**Requirement.** An agent compares stack, release, route and trace variants, proposes split/merge/rule changes and shows exact affected events, counterexamples, ownership and alert/rate/repair-verification effects. Applying or rejecting a proposal is a grouping correction in the standard class, and the company's policy decides whether an agent's proposal is applied alone or waits for a person to preview it and apply or reject it; undo preserves immutable originals and prior decisions. A person who decides a proposal is the owner until TEAM-001 supplies project roles. Agent proposals are labelled "proposed by agent <alias>". CTX-001 inherits trace-variant comparison for AI-005 before completion. The model cannot silently rewrite a group, suppress alerting or manufacture better repair results.

**Acceptance.** Given deceptively similar and rebuilt failures:
1. The agent's proposal shows exact affected events and counterexamples.
2. It shows the rate and alert differences.
3. After the owner rejects one proposal, nothing changes.
4. After the owner approves another, it applies.
5. Undoing it preserves the immutable originals and leaves a grouping-change coverage gap.

#### AI-006 — Prevent related failures from recurring

*Tier:* Core · *Rules:* D-1

**Requirement.** An agent mines accepted fixes, rejected hypotheses, production recurrence and the repository code its grant covers for shared violated invariants. It proposes reusable regression/property tests, identifies other affected call sites with evidence and counterexamples, and watches later releases for that invariant. Related-code guesses remain hypotheses. A new repository or service scope is a grant a person widens, never the agent itself; adding a test or a patch is a call with its class, which the company's policy decides; budgets, stop controls and known false positives stay visible.

**Acceptance.**
1. After a repair is accepted, a related failure introduced at another authorized call site yields the inferred invariant and a failing regression case.
2. A false positive is rejected and stays visible as known.
3. After a person approves a scoped patch, it lands with the person as approver and the agent as preparer.
4. Later recurrence is observed, and the agent's scope never widens on its own.

#### AI-007 — Agent-runtime failure diagnosis and evaluated improvements

*Tier:* Core

**Requirement.** For applications using LLM agents, correlate the model/tool spans the buyer's capture policy allows, latency, token/cost and sanitized failures with the application issue. ## Boundaries

- Spool owns error/crash records, release health, error-linked traces/replay, triage and the repair-verification loop. Mobile SDKs, native symbolication, provider applications, billing and heavy sandbox workers are required engineering, not reasons to reduce this scope.
- General work planning remains [Vector](https://github.com/just-every/run-vector), and rotations, SMS/voice escalation and incident response remain [Oncall](https://github.com/just-every/run-oncall) or PagerDuty. TRACK-001 and ALERT-002 connect those products; Spool does not recreate their broader job.
- For monitoring and observability, see RunEditRun’s sibling [Porthole](https://github.com/just-every/run-porthole). Whole-platform infrastructure APM, general log warehousing, product analytics and model-evaluation suites remain connected services such as Datadog, Splunk and PostHog. CTX-001/002 and AI-007 still require the diagnosis context the error buyer needs; these boundaries do not exclude it.
- Scheduled-job and heartbeat monitoring is [Uptime](https://github.com/just-every/run-uptime)'s product; SDK-024 forwards Sentry SDK check-ins to the buyer's connected Uptime heartbeat.
- Cloudflare is the bounded intake/control plane, not a requirement to run native symbolication, replay processing or persistent sandboxes inside request execution. Use declared isolated worker/storage providers with quotas, custody, portability and erasure coverage; SDK-011's attachment, minidump, profile and replay items and SRC-004's source maps and debug files stream there rather than being held in request memory, and the request-size limits SDK-011 publishes still bind. SDK-002, SDK-011, GOV-002 and AI-002 retain the full obligation.
- Production deployment remains the buyer's own CI/CD action, after the buyer's own review; Spool does not deploy. Telemetry and model suggestions authorize nothing. Replay/raw requests/identity are opt-in with preview and redaction; no blanket claim of perfect secret removal or legal compliance is made. Health/payment data requires buyer-approved agreements and controls before capture, rather than an implicit assurance.
- Local deletion cannot remove already downloaded archives, delivered messages or remote-provider copies; show the limits and partner deletion path. ERASE-001 defines the exact offline-journal and backup limits: already downloaded archives, delivered mail, remote provider and identity-provider records, `OWNER_EMAIL` and alert destination configuration (`ALERT_DESTINATIONS`), D1 Time Travel and backups, and raw database imports lie outside the local fence, erasure reports these limits rather than claiming their deletion, and a brand-new store given only an older archive has no later journal and cannot recognize the erasure.
- No unlimited-ingest or complete-capture claim is permitted; GOV-003 and SRC-004 publish the limited figures a buyer buys (retention, retained volume, sustained intake rate and artifact capacity), and no lower undisclosed cap may stand in for them.
- Expanded category clauses supplement the published clauses' bounded guarantees; they do not turn the current single-owner implementation into a scope boundary.
- Incumbent names identify switching obligations, not claims about their current plans or feature availability.

run-spool.com · Part of Just Every · MIT licensed

Watch the full demo · 51 seconds


Each error traced to the exact line in your original source.


A fixed error that comes back is flagged as a regression in its release.

# Spool · See exactly what broke Spool catches JavaScript, Python and Go errors, groups repeats into issues, and maps JavaScript stacks back to your original source. Download an evidence packet for a fix, give an agent evidence access and inert grouping-proposal submission to one project, and see when a resolved error comes back in a later release. One owner can keep several projects separate, export private evidence and restore it into a fresh copy. Public source: [just-every/run-spool](https://github.com/just-every/run-spool). The latest tagged Spool release is [v0.7.9](https://github.com/just-every/run-spool/tree/v0.7.9). The clone instructions below use `main`, which may be ahead of that tag; the tagged release has its own instructions. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). Licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Run Spool on your computer without a Cloudflare account or mail provider, or deploy it to your own Cloudflare Worker and D1 database. The [first-release jobs and verification requirements](ACCEPTANCE.md) describe what to expect. ## Run it on your computer macOS, Linux or Windows with WSL2. git is required; rer brings Node and pnpm. One line, as on the [Run page](https://run-spool.com/run), installs rer, clones Spool and starts it: ```sh curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh -s -- dev just-every/run-spool ``` The installer puts rer in `~/.local/bin` and leaves your shell profile unchanged. For the `rer` commands below, add it to this terminal's PATH: ```sh export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" ``` Repeat that line in each new terminal, or use `~/.local/bin/rer` wherever this guide says `rer`. `~/.local/bin/rer cli path` shows optional shell-profile setup for future terminals. The installer’s printed restart and stop commands also work after this PATH step. Already have Node 22 or later? `npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-spool` does the same. To start it again later, run `cd run-spool && ~/.local/bin/rer dev`. To run the tagged release instead, use `git clone --branch v0.7.9 https://github.com/just-every/run-spool.git spool && cd spool && rer dev` in place of that line. Its dependencies and instructions are those shipped with that tag. `rer dev` installs everything, prepares a local owner and prints a link that opens Spool signed in. First start uses `owner@run-spool.test` for the `run-spool` folder above, without asking for an email, even when input is piped. Another folder name produces `owner@.test`; existing setup keeps its owner. To choose your own email before first start, run the install line with `setup` in place of `dev` instead, then `cd run-spool && ~/.local/bin/rer dev`. Explicit setup asks for missing required answers in an interactive terminal. With non-TTY input, put JSON such as `{"OWNER_EMAIL":"you@example.com"}` in `.rer/local/setup-answers.json`, an ignored private file with mode `0600`, then run `rer setup --answers .rer/local/setup-answers.json --non-interactive` from the Spool checkout. The answers path must be relative and contained inside that checkout; absolute paths, traversal and symlinks are refused. Piping an email alone is not a setup answer. Saved answers are reused. To replace the temporary dev owner's address later, stop dev first and supply `OWNER_EMAIL` through that file. Keep addresses and secrets out of shell arguments. See [installation](docs/getting-started.md) for the file procedure. Setup prepares private settings and the database, claims or preserves the owner, opens the local owner without email and stops its temporary app; run `rer dev` afterwards. It creates no sample project and sends no real email. For older state, follow [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md#existing-installation-recovery). `rer dev` opens signed in as the owner. Open the private `RER_OPEN` link printed on this computer; its `#rer-dev=` fragment carries this checkout's owner gate. Keep the link and gate private. Local development reads **Spool Dev**; `rer demo` reads **Spool Demo** and adds sample data in disposable state. Mail is silently suppressed in dev and demo; no mailbox viewer is needed. With rer dev v2 (using the rer version pinned in [package.json](package.json)), an ingest key created in dev works directly from your app against local Spool, and a deploy key works from your local build, without the owner gate. Allow your browser app's exact origin in Capture. Dev agent keys still need the gate for evidence and inert proposals: privately extract the `rer-dev` fragment value as `SPOOL_DEV_KEY` for the local agent CLI, as shown in [the agent guide](docs/WITH-YOUR-AGENT.md#local-agent-access). Never give the gate to a browser app. Every dev-minted key is refused by deployed Spool; create fresh keys there. Private archives exclude all project grants. A fresh installation opens `/setup`. Create the first project, copy its once-shown ingest key, add the SDK with the shown install line and init, use **Send test error** to check ingestion from Spool itself, then choose **Continue to workbench**. Replace a lost key in Settings. To restore existing evidence instead, choose **Restore a private archive** before creating a project. Register the app's release/build before sending its errors; the setup test registers the release/build shown on that screen. Stop dev with `~/.local/bin/rer dev --stop` (or Ctrl+C in the foreground) before deploy, verify, reset or transfer. Your owner, projects and evidence stay on this computer for the next start. [RUN-LOCALLY.md](RUN-LOCALLY.md) describes preview, idle timeout and server capacity. `rer describe` lists supported maintenance commands and flags. Export before reset and import only into an empty destination. Export includes private maps and browser-origin policy but excludes sign-in sessions, project keys, outbox and temporary state. Run setup if the destination has no owner and create new keys after restoring. Browser restore is available from `/setup` before the first project and Settings thereafter. For CLI import of a browser download, first run `chmod 600 /path/to/spool-private-archive.jsonl`; see [the transfer procedure](OPERATIONS.md#data-movement-and-retention). Reset removes only its displayed local inventory and preserves source, exports and deployment records. ## Upgrade an existing installation Back up first: export a private archive (Settings → **Download private archive**, or stop dev and run `rer export --output exports/spool.rer`). Keep the original checkout, database and private settings. For the latest tagged release, run `git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.7.9`, then `rer dev`. To keep following `main`, run `git pull --ff-only` and then `rer dev`. Hosted installations update with `rer deploy` from the original deploying checkout, retaining its private settings, generated secrets and deployment receipt; follow [the hosting update procedure](docs/HOSTED.md#update-to-a-newer-spool). Those commands apply any migrations missing from the installed version. This `main` checkout includes migrations through `0099`; a tag applies the migrations shipped with that tag. Existing projects, evidence, triage states, grouping rules, inbound filters, alert rules and project keys are preserved. No reset or restore is needed for an upgrade. Older native private archives can also restore into a fresh, empty current installation. See the [release record](RELEASE.json) and [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). ## Managed hosting Spool uses the rer version pinned in [package.json](package.json) and supports RER Managed mail for sign-in links and email alerts. Managed Configure supplies and hides the mail settings: no mail-provider account or copied API key is needed. Free and Assisted self hosting keep their existing provider choices and sender setup; see [the hosting guide](docs/HOSTED.md#managed-mail). ## Run it on your Cloudflare account Follow [the hosting guide](docs/HOSTED.md) to configure your account and email sender. Stop local dev with `rer dev --stop`, then run `rer deploy`. Open `/sign-in` on the printed hosted address and request an email link. If you cannot receive mail, `rer signin --env-file .rer/deploy/production.env --environment production` prints a private, one-use owner link using the hosting guide's private settings file, the same Cloudflare credentials and original deploying checkout; it expires within 15 minutes. To remove it, export anything you need and run `rer deploy --remove --yes` from the original deploying checkout, retaining its private deployment record and using the same account credentials. The default environment is `production`; add `--environment ` for another environment. Removal deletes the Worker and its database. The hosting guide also covers updates and restoring archives. `rer deploy --dry-run` builds and validates the package locally without deploying or contacting Cloudflare. It prints the plan and names the inputs a real deploy still needs. A successful dry run exits 0 even when those inputs are missing; it does not establish that a real deploy is ready. ## Capture protocol Spool's own SDK, [`@just-every/spool`](packages/sdk/README.md), is the way to send errors. For browser capture without Node.js or npm, download `/errors-capture.js` from your Spool installation, serve it with your app and follow the [browser-helper setup](docs/capture.md#browser-capture-without-nodejs-or-npm). Or install the SDK and initialise it once with the project's endpoint and ingest key: Run this in **your application’s repository**, with [Node.js and npm](https://nodejs.org/en/download) installed and available on PATH. The Spool installer’s private Node runtime runs Spool itself; it does not put Node or npm on your shell’s PATH for your application. ```sh npm install @just-every/spool ``` As of 2026-11-12, this installs SDK 0.1.0, the published npm version. SDK 0.2.0 remains owner-held and unpublished. Ordinary error capture and map upload work with 0.1.0; exposure measurement (`client`, `anonymousClient()` and `exposure()`) and the Vite/Rollup upload-count message require 0.2.0. The Spool app release does not publish or upgrade the SDK. See the [SDK release notes](packages/sdk/CHANGELOG.md). ```js import { init } from '@just-every/spool'; init({ endpoint: 'https://spool.example.com', project: 'web-app', ingestKey: 'YOUR_INGEST_KEY', release: 'web@1.4.0', build: 'b1907' }); ``` The browser SDK captures errors and unhandled rejections and can attach the last 20 explicit, scrubbed breadcrumbs. Use `@just-every/spool/node` for Node and `@just-every/spool/worker` for Cloudflare Workers. The package also includes `npx spool-sourcemaps` and the Rollup/Vite plugin at `@just-every/spool/vite` for uploading maps that match your build. Setup, Capture and Settings show the install line and init for your project. Allow your app's browser origin before connecting it; **Send test error** runs inside Spool and does not check that external origin. Follow [the capture guide](docs/capture.md) for browser permissions, local key scopes, release registration and map upload. Pages without a bundler can use `/errors-capture.js`. ### Already using Sentry? Point your DSN here Each project can issue a Sentry DSN for supported JavaScript, Python and Go exception reports. Spool scrubs the selected error fields and discards unsupported telemetry. [Switching from Sentry](docs/SENTRY-SWITCHING.md) covers supported intake, map tooling and the optional organization-export importer. The importer has been qualified with synthetic fixtures; a real organization export still needs reconciliation. This does not establish feature parity or a completed migration. ## Operating limits and privacy Spool is intended for bounded error evidence. Each project retains at most 10,000 occurrences and admits at most 120 new occurrences per minute; recorded rejections can reduce the remaining admission budget. The issue list and its filters cover the latest 100 groups, and packets include the latest 10 occurrences. Maps are private uploads. The upload service and current checkout CLI accept flat or indexed V3 maps up to 1 MiB each. The published npm SDK 0.1.0 CLI and the prepared-map picker on **Releases** accept only flat V3 maps up to 256 KiB. There is no lifetime map count; all paths respect the optional project artifact-storage byte cap. The larger/indexed CLI support is in the unpublished 0.2.0 source, not npm 0.1.0. Spool never fetches source URLs. Ingest requests are limited to 32 KiB, 30 frames and 20 breadcrumbs. The SDK and server scrub common emails, tokens and passwords, but free text can contain personal data those patterns do not recognize. Inspect event and packet previews. There is no durable offline queue, automatic retry or guaranteed unload flush; errors lost before reaching Spool are unknown. Firefox and Safari stack parsing is implemented but has not been tested in those browsers. See [supported languages](docs/SUPPORTED-LANGUAGES.md) for exact Python and Go support and symbolication limits. Private archives include source maps and exclude sign-in sessions and project credentials. Browser restore accepts up to 16 MiB; use the streaming CLI for larger archives. Older native v1 and v2 archives remain supported. Retention and project erasure cannot remove copies you already exported elsewhere. See [data movement and retention](OPERATIONS.md#data-movement-and-retention) and [project erasure](docs/PROJECT-ERASURE.md). Optional project alerts cover new issues, regressions in later releases and spikes in received events. Add, edit and test email destinations from **Alerts → Rules**, then select one in a rule ([steps](docs/ALERT-WEBHOOKS.md#manage-email-destinations)). Email alerts require a configured provider; signed webhooks require a separately installed service that enforces destination restrictions. Provider submission does not prove recipient delivery. Local mail is suppressed. See [alerts](OPERATIONS.md#per-project-alerts) and [webhook setup](docs/ALERT-WEBHOOKS.md). The [triage guide](docs/triage.md) explains issue links, mapped stacks and first capture. You can record repair checks and the release that shipped a fix; Spool reports recurrence or explains why the available capture and exercise evidence is inconclusive. It does not infer that a fix worked just because no new error arrived. ## Develop and verify After `rer install`, run `npm run test:setup --` once to install this checkout's Chromium browser for verification; repeat after changing the Playwright version. Stop dev, then run `rer verify` to build, typecheck and exercise the application, sign-in, capture, maps, triage and restore flows. These commands run locally and never deploy. [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md) describes the verification requirements and remaining limits. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md) cover source maintenance and recovery. A passing local check does not establish mail delivery, a live provider integration or large-instance economics.

# HappyToHelp target product contract

Target edition · 17 October 2026 · US-first, USD. HappyToHelp is a complete customer service help desk and AI support agent for a US SMB support lead switching from Zendesk, Intercom (with Fin), Help Scout or Freshdesk. It owns the job from customer intake through a shared operational queue, self-service and live business context to an authorized resolution and continued customer recovery. Decagon, Sierra and Pylon set the agent/procedure and B2B-channel baseline; the target goes further with verified repair and obligations that survive handoffs.

## Product target

HappyToHelp is the complete help desk and AI support agent a US SMB support lead buys instead of Zendesk, Intercom (with Fin), Help Scout or Freshdesk; Decagon, Sierra and Pylon set the agent and procedure baseline it must also meet.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Category | Customer service help desks and AI support agents |
| Incumbents a buyer switches from | Zendesk, Intercom (with Fin), Help Scout, Freshdesk (agent baseline: Decagon, Sierra, Pylon) |
| Up-and-comers it must also beat | Decagon, Sierra, Pylon |
| First buyer | A US SMB support lead, costs in USD, moving a Zendesk, Intercom, Help Scout or Freshdesk help desk |

The primary journey: Set up the workspace, bring in support history, connect customer channels, triage and assign requests, resolve them with knowledge and permitted actions, then verify recovery and follow up.

## How to read this contract

- This follows the RER contract standard.
- Core, Agent surface and Later are reported separately.
- Done means every acceptance outcome has recorded proof.
- Field proof records real-world qualification separately.
- ACCEPTANCE.md, docs/CLAIMS.md and summary counts are generated from this file.

## Door rules

- **D-1.** Support identity. Linking customers supplies staff context only; it grants no customer-side access, merge or send authority. Each customer continues to use their own verified session.
- **D-2.** Support recovery. A provider acknowledgment, closed engineering issue or completed command is not customer recovery; record the separate observation.

### Retained product and operating guarantees

#### NATIVE-001 — Native owner installation

**Requirement.** The owner can inspect the operating description before dependency installation; setup preserves this edition’s native owner and selected bindings. Local setup exits with no app running; dev prints a private entry address that enters as the real local owner through the rer dev v2 boundary, preserving native sessions, roles and passwords. Reset is explicitly confirmed and local; export/import preserve supported native data with documented exclusions. Deployment dry-run makes zero outbound requests and explicitly reports that fact. A separately and explicitly started read-only provider preflight uses the owner's scoped Cloudflare token with owner consent to read the account's Workers subdomain and the Worker's settings and secret names (three GETs for an existing Worker); it sends no mail and changes no resources. Dry-run and preflight are independent steps, neither a mock of the other. The delivered runtime requires no original checkout or PHP service. Details are in [the support protocol guide](docs/contract/support-protocols.md).

**Acceptance.**
1. Use a clean checkout through rer describe/check, locked installation, setup, dev, verify, reset and export/import; preserve owner/data/settings and refuse unconfirmed destructive work.
2. For deployment dry-run, assert zero outbound requests and an explicit no-outbound report without provider credentials.
3. As a separate acceptance point, explicitly start the read-only provider preflight with owner consent and the owner's scoped token; assert only the three expected Cloudflare GETs for an existing Worker, no mail and no mutations, and refuse missing credentials or consent.
4. Prove the runtime works independently of the original checkout; separately qualify remote provisioning.

#### IDENTITY-002 — Retained native password identity

**Requirement.** Preserve native password sign-in, first-owner setup, the accepted owner experience and prior account/workspace data with the maintained Base command mechanisms. Retain this edition's authentication and native owner setup. A second factor for these native accounts is required by IDENTITY-003; it adds to native passwords and never replaces them. Supersedes `BASE-ACCESS-001` for native password identity under RL-1.

**Acceptance.**
1. Complete native password setup, login, recovery and workspace re-entry, then upgrade with prior owner credentials and data intact; configured providers must not replace native identity.

#### IDENTITY-001 — Scoped authority

**Requirement.** Owner setup, registration, login/recovery, project switching, membership and widget admission establish native identity. Provider configuration never substitutes for user authority. The public widget key and origin are not a secret: visitor, registration and project-creation requests are bounded by D1-backed limits (the documented admission limits) and refused with HTTP 429 and `Retry-After`. A stored widget session serves only the visitor identity the host page supplies now (its identifier, else its email in any letter case, else anonymous); an unsigned sign-in carries the browser's anonymous conversation over, unverified; and `h2h('shutdown')` ends the browser's widget sessions.

**Acceptance.**
1. Through native session and widget routes, deny cross-tenant, blocked/deleted and revoked access; prove public admission returns 429 with Retry-After when limited and provider configuration conveys no actor authority.
2. In one real browser against the emitted Worker and the built widget, prove that account switches, sign-out, emulated pages and signed identities never send, read or render another visitor's session or conversation; that sign-in carries the anonymous conversation over and a returning signed-in visitor gets its own back; and that `h2h('shutdown')` removes the widget and forgets the browser's sessions in every state.

#### FIRST-RUN-001 — A useful first workspace

**Requirement.** First-run setup is one screen: the owner's email, a password, the website and, only where the server requires one, the private setup token. Missing names and colors are derived and every derived value can be changed. A completed installation leads the owner to a workspace that is already set up, whose Setup page lists only what cannot be done for them (an AI service key, the widget on their website and, with a hosted email provider, a verified sending domain), leads with the widget, lets the owner skip any of them for now, and shows everything else under "What we've set". Every workspace created by first-owner setup, signed-in workspace creation or email-verified registration, and never a demo workspace, is provisioned in one step: a starter assistant as its default visitor assistant, a reply-by-email mailbox when the installation holds the installation’s inbound-email credential, and mail sent from the installation sender until the workspace's own domain is verified. The starter assistant’s visitor replies carry external, and its internal preparation standard; the company’s policy decides each call once a provider key and complete policy exist, within that policy’s AI spending limits; with no key no assistant is assigned to a new conversation, it stays with the team and the AI page and Setup say a key is missing. The first-run Create workspace action may send one welcome email to the owner; an uncertain send is never replayed. Ordinary workspace creation leads with the widget snippet; Advanced retains the server secret and verification examples. Empty inboxes offer installation, a link to Setup and a demo. Workspace headers follow workspace switching. Visitor headers retain the operator's display name.

**Acceptance.**
1. Run fresh first-owner setup and signed-in workspace creation to Setup and an installable widget; inspect derived editable name/color, starter assistant, mailbox/sender, skip/Advanced controls and mobile headers.
2. With no model key a new visitor stays with the team; with a configured provider exercise the capped starter.
3. A workers.dev hostname must not become a business name.

#### LOCAL-MAIL-001 — Rer dev mail

**Requirement.** Trusted local development configuration uses the rer dev v2 development transport: it validates and suppresses visitor and teammate mail, reports `development`, stores no messages and exposes no mail viewer. It sends no external email. The local owner enters automatically through the dev boundary; native password identity, ordinary hosted email-link confirmation and prior stored data are retained. Production has no local dev surface. Missing credentials or failed remote delivery never select a local substitute.

**Acceptance.**
1. Enter through rer dev v2; send visitor and teammate mail and prove development suppression without storage, viewer or external send; refuse forged and production dev entry and never substitute suppression for a failed hosted provider.

#### CONVERSATION-001 — Durable transcript

**Requirement.** Customer, operator, generation, import and administrative writers preserve stable message/command identity, revision/frontier, attachment ownership and final-reply admission atomically. Competing or repeated writes cannot admit two incompatible final replies. Owner/admin contact erasure removes message content while keeping identity, revision and frontier, so erased transcripts stay coherent.

**Acceptance.**
1. Race visitor, operator, model and import writers through conversation routes with duplicate and lost responses; admit only compatible final replies.
2. Erase a contact through the owner door and verify coherent identity/revision/frontier with content removed.

#### DELIVERY-001 — Live delivery and recovery

**Requirement.** Persist before broadcast; reconnect/outbox replay and socket authorization recover committed messages after reload, disconnection or process wake. Provisional AI deltas never become durable final answers until guarded admission succeeds.

**Acceptance.**
1. Disconnect/reconnect widget and operator sockets after persisted writes, restart the runtime and recover the same committed messages/attachments; unauthorized replay is denied and superseded AI deltas never become final replies.

#### UI-001 — Existing editable experience

**Requirement.** Reuse the original React dashboard, transcripts/drafts/suggestions, settings and Shadow DOM widget; preserve useful desktop/mobile flows, attachment display, collector/privacy controls and errors. Native routing and transport use the configured application origin.

**Acceptance.**
1. Use the native dashboard and separately installed widget at 1440 and 390 pixels with realistic conversations, attachments, drafts, errors and workspace switching; retain the approved desktop/mobile navigation and configured-origin transport.

#### MOVE-IN-001 — Reviewed history import

**Requirement.** Current workspace owner/admin reviewers privately upload, inspect per-kind plans, source-located omissions, rejections, conflicts and publication changes, then explicitly apply bounded, resumable imports of conversations, contacts, tags, saved replies and articles. Preserve source identities, timestamps, private notes and publication state; reject unsupported meaning rather than inventing it. Recheck current role and workspace authority for apply, resume and whole-import undo. Retain immutable source custody and conflict-safe reversal journals. Imports and undo send no mail, widget messages, model requests, assignment or connection notifications; imports are excluded from Reports. Native tag controls enforce workspace scope. RL-2 requires exact business-state repeat/undo equality, including contacts, conversations, messages, private notes, tags, source links and every other imported business table. Only platform counters/sequences, audit history and import journals are excluded. Synthetic 1,000-conversation datasets for Zendesk and Help Scout qualify this local flow.

**Acceptance.**
1. Through Move in, exercise all five kinds, source custody, per-row omissions/rejections/conflicts, current-role denials, inert apply/resume/repeat/undo and exact business-state equality for synthetic 1,000-conversation Zendesk and Help Scout datasets; counters/sequences, audit and journals are the only named exclusions.

#### OUTCOMES-001 — Resolution feedback and provenance

**Requirement.** Current original visitor sessions may rate a closed resolution with thumbs up/down and an optional comment up to 1,000 characters. Changes retain history; reopened cycles cannot receive the previous resolution's rating. Operators retain access to each past resolution's latest feedback after reopening; visitor eligibility and report denominators remain tied to the current cycle. Erasure removes rating comments. Confirmed operator-sent drafts establish assisted outcomes, otherwise confirmed human replies establish human outcomes. AI requires a complete visible answer history without a person handoff; missing evidence remains unknown. Status, assignment and cancellation transitions recheck current authority atomically.

**Acceptance.**
1. Close, rate, rerate, reopen and close again via widget/operator routes; prevent previous-session/cycle feedback, retain old-cycle operator visibility, redact erased comments and verify human/assisted/AI/unknown attribution from actual visible answers.

#### REPORTS-001 — Workspace calendar reports

**Requirement.** Native conversations created in the workspace IANA calendar range with at least one persisted message form the cohort; Move in and legacy imports are excluded. First visitor-to-visible-answer response and creation-to-first known-resolution durations use median and nearest-rank p90. Each conversation contributes its latest closed cycle once to outcome and satisfaction rates. Reopened conversations leave those denominators. Aggregate queries return bounded data; CSV streams every matching conversation with formula-safe cells. Empty widget conversations stay durable but are excluded from Reports and its analytics CSVs. A separate step-up guarded JSON export includes all workspace conversations, messages, private notes and attachment names across dates and imports; attachment bytes stay in the portable backup.

**Acceptance.**
1. Compare Reports and formula-safe CSV to hand-calculated response/resolution median and p90, latest-cycle outcome and satisfaction cohorts across DST and tenants, including more than 10,000 rows and excluded imports/reopened cycles.

#### CONNECTIONS-001 — Workspace integrations

**Requirement.** Owner/admin tokens have explicit scopes, optional expiry, one-time display, hashed storage and durable audit. Bearer-only API calls have no CORS, per-token limits and native guarded writes. Contact erasure fences API identity restoration and pending event payloads. Native events commit tenant-bound webhook and Slack intents; historical import apply and undo do not emit them. Slack projects bounded native visitor text through Base escaping. The owner-authorized ordinary HTTPS exception retains redirect refusal, bounded requests/responses and literal-destination checks instead of DNS pinning (RL-3). See [the full transport exception](docs/contract/support-protocols.md).

**Acceptance.**
1. Issue, use, expire and revoke each scoped show-once token; exercise native API operations, erasure fences, signed events and Slack escaping.
2. Refuse redirects/unsafe literal destinations and over-limit traffic; preserve timeout, streamed bounds, uncertain 500 without replay and bounded 429 behavior under the recorded HTTPS override.

#### ACTIVATION-001 — Observed owner setup

**Requirement.** An owner sees the durable, project-scoped eight-step list on the Setup page; the genuinely empty inbox shows one next action and a link to it, and loads none of it. A step is confirmed only by an observation, never by a saved configuration, an installer default or a preset, so a workspace with nothing observed yet is zero of its applicable steps. The system runs its own checks: while an owner is signed in the page asks the server to observe, bounded by freshness windows. These checks are non-generative metadata, domain and DNS reads and never send mail. They distinguish saved configuration from observed sender DNS, authenticated model metadata, an inbound receipt, effective runtime ceilings, allowed origin and an authenticated widget ping; whether an article is published is not one of them (that step stays among the eight ids but is hidden and never counted). Mail to the owner is confirmed by a used emailed sign-in link, or by the provider's reported outcome for the welcome or test email; local development mail is suppressed and never confirms delivery, and provider acceptance or queueing is pending. Reading Setup performs no provider work and writes nothing. Only an explicit owner action (Create workspace, or Send me a test) may send mail, to that owner's mailbox, with durable identity; ambiguous work is never replayed. Missing provider permissions and unsupported status APIs remain unavailable. Configuration changes invalidate observations; model and DNS validation expire after 15 minutes and every observation shows its time. The owner can skip an owner-only step (the widget, the AI service, the sending domain) for now, and undo it. A skip is stored on the server for the workspace, can be made by an owner or admin only, makes no provider request, and moves the step out of Needs you and out of the confirmed count and its total; a skipped step is never shown as confirmed. An observation always wins: a skipped step that is later observed is confirmed and counted, and a rejected provider key stays under Needs you whether or not it was skipped. Provider keys and their fingerprints never enter API responses or browser storage. Details are in [the support protocol guide](docs/contract/support-protocols.md).

**Acceptance.**
1. Read Setup without side effects, observe fresh/expired/rejected configuration and explicit provider outcomes, skip/undo owner steps and reload.
2. A skip or preset never counts as confirmation; local suppression never proves delivery; keys/fingerprints remain server-only and uncertain explicit test/welcome mail is never replayed.

#### AI-001 — Configured model execution

**Requirement.** Retain Ensemble model selection, context/tools, streamed events, normalization, raw per-round provider usage, attribution, bounded suggestions and reply lifecycle. Missing providers fail explicitly when AI is asked for, and a default assistant whose provider has no key is simply not assigned to new conversations; uncertain provider attempts remain uncertain and are not replayed automatically. Usage is diagnostic/provider accounting data, not an active payment, balance or debit system. Visitor-caused model work carries the classes of its eventual action, and the company’s policy sets its project and installation AI spending limits; a skipped reply is recorded as terminal and never replayed. Each workspace's AI reply mode is auto (the default), draft or off: in draft AI writes only drafts its team sends themselves, in off AI generates nothing, no AI-authored message reaches a customer in draft or off by any path (a local computer agent's reply becomes a draft its operator sends themselves, and a visitor whose assistant will not answer is handled as one without an assistant), in draft or off a conversation whose visitor has written since its assistant last answered is listed in the team's normal views as one without an assistant, and switching back to auto releases nothing queued, written or due during that time.

**Acceptance.**
1. Request configured suggestions/replies through native routes; inspect normalized streaming events, per-round usage, context/tool and budget bounds, explicit missing-provider errors and durable daily-cap skips; crash/ambiguous attempts must not automatically replay.

#### KNOWLEDGE-001 — Published knowledge

**Requirement.** Dataset ingestion/crawl, retained corpus, lexical/selected semantic retrieval, citations and article/category authoring maintain project scope and publication state. A failed refresh cannot replace the last usable published corpus. Public pages exclude drafts/deleted projects and preserve original canonical article/search routes.

**Acceptance.**
1. Publish and search articles/categories through authoring and public help-center doors; deny draft/deleted/cross-project access, verify citations and canonical links and retain the last usable published corpus after a failed refresh.

#### CONTEXT-001 — Attributed customer context

**Requirement.** Profiles, monitoring, insights and context packets preserve evidence attribution, source bounds, consent and project ownership. Provider output must satisfy the selected schemas before becoming usable customer context.

**Acceptance.**
1. Generate/read profile, monitoring, insight and context packets through native routes; reject ungrounded/schema-invalid or cross-project content, preserve attributed evidence and respect consent/source bounds.

#### DELEGATION-001 — Explicit local authority

**Requirement.** Pairing, devices/grants, revocation, tool context and work/result states preserve investigation, resolve and advance-authorized resolve-and-reply distinctions. Revocation withdraws authority and never asserts that a local process stopped: started work becomes terminal with an unconfirmed outcome, and only the device may report cancellation. Local processes remain in the optional connector, never an implicit Worker capability. Agent calls use the company’s policy for their computed classes; any approval or review in this journey is under the held company policy.

**Acceptance.**

## Target clauses

### Complete support operations

#### DESK-001 — The shared support desk

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001, BASE-INPUT-003

**Requirement.** A visitor starts website live chat, identifies themselves under the workspace policy, sends files and returns to their history. Humans see one durable shared inbox with customer history, scoped retained-history search with words, quoted phrases and literal customer-identity matching, open/closed/mine/unassigned/AI/tag filters and saved replies that insert into the composer without silently sending. Ticket status follows the STATUS-001 lifecycle and saved replies extend to MACRO-001 action macros. Replies, attachment downloads and errors are visible on both sides; privacy/collector controls remain effective.

1. Through the installed widget and operator inbox, exchange messages and real attachment bytes, search/filter the resulting queue, insert and edit a saved reply, reload both sides and deny another tenant the same records.

#### WIDGET-001 — Availability-aware messenger and proactive messages

*Tier:* Core

**Requirement.** The messenger shows team availability from business-hour schedules (SLA-001) and live agent presence. When no human or permitted AI assistant is available it says so with the expected reply time, captures the visitor's email (or, where consented, SMS/WhatsApp under CHANNELS-001) so the answer reaches them, and creates the ticket instead of leaving the visitor waiting. Leads configure proactive messages triggered by page URL, time on page, scroll depth, exit intent, visitor attributes, returning visit or cart value, with audience, brand, frequency caps and quiet hours. Each proactive message shows a clear sender identity and an easy dismiss, respects consent and collector settings, and never starts a conversation that sends personal data on the visitor's behalf. Impressions, opens, dismissals and resulting conversations and resolutions are reported. This clause backs the homepage hero's "Before they ask".

**Acceptance.**
1. Outside configured hours, open the installed widget, see the offline message and expected reply time, leave an email and verify the ticket and the emailed answer.
2. During hours with no agent online verify the same; with an available AI assistant verify it answers and discloses itself.
3. Configure a proactive message on a checkout URL after 20 seconds with a once-per-day cap; verify it appears once, dismisses, stays silent under a declined collector setting and appears in reports with its impressions and conversations.

#### MAIL-001 — Complete support email

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-MAIL-001, BASE-OPS-003 · *Register:* R-2

**Requirement.** Connect inbound forwarding, an IMAP/SMTP mailbox, Gmail/Google Workspace or Microsoft 365/Outlook using scoped credentials/OAuth. New mail creates tickets and replies thread by stable Message-ID/In-Reply-To/References with deliberate handling of changed subject, aliases and multiple recipients. Operators manage CC/BCC, attachments, signatures and branded sender/reply addresses. Duplicate/redelivered mail, bounces, spam and auto-responders cannot create loops or send twice, and mail classified as spam or failing sender checks goes to the reviewable Suspended view of MAIL-002; reconnect/backfill has a visible cursor and errors, and removal stops new intake without deleting history.

**Acceptance.**
1. For each of forwarding, IMAP, Gmail and Microsoft 365, use the connection UI and provider sandboxes or official-schema fakes to receive a new thread, reply from the inbox, receive its follow-up and attachment, disconnect/reconnect with redelivery and observe bounce/permission failure.
2. Verify no duplicate ticket/reply or machine-mail AI loop; keep provider-protocol tests separate from live acceptance.
3. Spam and failing-sender mail reaches the MAIL-002 Suspended view, not a ticket.

#### MAIL-002 — Reviewable suspended and spam mail

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-MAIL-001, BASE-DATA-002, BASE-ROLE-001, BASE-AUDIT-001

**Requirement.** Inbound mail that is spam-scored, fails DMARC/SPF/DKIM or alignment, comes from a blocked sender or domain, forges a verified customer's address, exceeds size limits or is a detected mail loop is never silently dropped. It lands in a Suspended view with its reason, authentication results, headers and safely previewed attachments, and creates no ticket, AI work, acknowledgment or notification. Permitted operators recover a false positive into a normal ticket that threads correctly (into the existing ticket when its references match) without retroactively triggering acknowledgments or AI unless they choose to; delete true spam; and block or allow a sender or domain. Recovery, deletion and list changes are audited. Suspended mail is kept for a stated retention period (default 14 days) and then explicitly deleted with an audit record; the view shows counts and the oldest age so nothing ages out unseen. Allow/block lists and suspension reasons are reportable.

**Acceptance.**
1. Through the application’s inbound doors deliver a spam-scored message, a DMARC-failing message, mail from a blocked sender and a forged From of a known customer; verify each appears in Suspended with its reason and creates no ticket, AI request or outbound mail.
2. Recover the DMARC-failing message into a new ticket and another into its existing thread, delete the spam, allow-list a sender and redeliver.
3. Advance the clock past retention at the runtime edge and verify explicit, audited deletion; refuse every action to a role without permission.

#### STATUS-001 — Ticket status lifecycle

*Tier:* Core · *Cites:* BASE-ROLE-001

**Requirement.** Every ticket has one status from a lifecycle the lead can extend: New, Open, Pending (waiting on the customer), On-hold (waiting on an internal team or third party), Solved and Closed, plus workspace custom statuses that each map to one of those categories. A customer reply to a Pending or On-hold ticket returns it to Open and wakes its owner. On-hold and every internal status label are never shown to the customer, who sees an open request in the widget, portal and email. A customer reply to a Solved ticket reopens it. After a lead-configured period (default 4 days) a durable time-based automation (AUTOMATION-002) moves Solved to Closed, and Closed is final: a customer reply to a Closed ticket creates a new follow-up ticket linked to it that carries the requester, CCs, tags and fields. Status filters, sorts, views, bulk edits (QUEUE-002), SLA pausing (SLA-001), resolution cycles (OUTCOMES-001) and reports all use this lifecycle, and every change records its actor, time and source (person, rule, automation or customer reply).
