Leasing staff read version dates, signers, references and obligation kind/date/source metadata without charge or HAP amounts or original downloads. Other roles cannot download signed sources; every source download is audited and no-store. SAFE-004 lease retention and legal holds preserve sources until eligible erasure, which removes originals and version text, remembers erased hashes and fences older archives; SAFE-005’s readable export contains original PDFs with hashes and restores full versions and terms. PORT-007 inherits broader searchable/versioned document custody, LEASE-012 approved renewal activation writes a versioned schedule, PAY-013 inherits HAP version/source links, and ACCT-003 inherits the versioned deposit obligation before those capabilities ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Enter a lease with a concession and pet charge, approve a mid-month amendment, and reconcile previewed charges and source clauses to the resident ledger while retaining the signed prior version.

- **PORT-006 — Complete move-in transfers and move-out.** Use checklists for keys, meters, condition, prorated charges, deposits, forwarding address and possession. Roommate changes and unit transfers close and reopen the appropriate obligations; move-out produces the deposit disposition and make-ready work without deleting the lease. Staff record separate move-in and move-out operational checklists on each lease: keys, meter identifiers/readings with their stated units, condition references, possession and forwarding details. Each item is pending, recorded by staff with details, or not applicable with a reason; corrections append a dated revision with actor and source. Move-in is dated to the lease start; a recorded move-out uses its ended-on day. Changed lease/checklist versions refuse stale writes, and a changed move-out day marks an earlier checklist for review. A transfer starts with no destination checklist, so source keys or readings are never claimed for the new unit. Existing ROLE-001 move-out responsibilities and portfolio scope apply. SAFE-002 history, SAFE-004 lease retention/erasure and SAFE-005 readable backup/restore cover all revisions. These operational records alone neither post money nor assert deposit disposition or a reconciled final balance. **Acceptance evidence:** Move a household in mid-month, transfer units and move out; verify prorations, distinct deposits, final balances, keys checklist and linked turnover tasks.

- **PORT-007 — Store searchable operating documents.** Attach and version leases, applications, notices, screening reports and tax documents on their tenancy records; inspection photos/video, work documents and invoices attach to their own records under PORT-009 (ct, 22 October 2026). Search authorized content and metadata; restrict screening and tax documents, screen uploads and preserve download history and retention classes; the malware-verdict leg of “scan uploads” is PORT-010. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: document search and downloads return only records on tenancies in the searcher’s portfolios and role. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload an amended lease and restricted screening PDF; find the current version from its unit, recover the prior lease and deny a vendor and unrelated resident access. A scoped staff user’s search and direct document download return nothing from another portfolio (404). SAFE-005 applies before this ships: each stored document appears in the readable export as its original file with its SHA-256 and restores with the backup. PORT-005 signed originals, versions, source clauses and retention remain intact when broader document search and custody ship. Exact semantics (ct ruling 22 October 2026 18:00Z): a tenancy document is a lease or amendment, an application, a notice, a screening report or a tax document on one tenancy, at most 5 MB, in PDF, JPEG, PNG, plain text, CSV or .eml; a new version appends and the earlier one stays readable, each with its original bytes and SHA-256. The upload check is a static screen, never a malware verdict and never “scanned clean”: it refuses scripts, markup, executables, PDF actions, launches and embedded files, encryption and anything it cannot read, and a pass means only that the screen found no active content. Restricted kinds, always under ROLE-001 portfolio scope with 404 outside it: screening reports for the owner and portfolio managers; application documents also for leasing staff; tax documents also for accountants, who find, open and download them and no other document and never upload or revise one. A reader without a kind’s right finds no trace of it (404, like a missing record), and API credentials never reach restricted kinds. Every download is recorded in History and listed in the document’s version and download history. Retention classes follow the kind: leases stay with the lease (7 years after it ends), applications and screening reports 2 years after the last upload (LEASE-009 inherits decision-based periods), notices 3 years after the last upload (PORTAL-005 and PORTAL-006 inherit communication-based periods) and tax documents with accounting (7 years after their fiscal year); erasure removes the eligible classes and keeps each file’s hash as a re-upload fence. Documents stored before this ruling as inspection, work, invoice or other stay readable to holders of document.read; new ones attach to their own records under PORT-009.

- **PORT-008 — Apply named state landlord-tenant rule packs.** Terrace ships a versioned, counsel-reviewed rule pack for each of the 50 states and the District of Columbia, plus local overlays where a city or county adds deposit, late-fee, notice or rent rules (first: Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York City, Chicago and Seattle). Packs activate in this order: California, Texas and Florida; then New York, Georgia, North Carolina, Arizona, Illinois, Washington and Colorado; then every remaining state and DC. Each pack states, with statute citation, effective date, version and reviewer: security-deposit cap; separate-account, bank-disclosure and receipt requirements; deposit interest rate and payment schedule; refund and itemization deadlines; required disposition delivery method and address rule (personal delivery, first-class mail, certified mail); late-fee cap, fee basis and grace period; partial-payment effects on notices; pay-or-quit and lease-violation notice periods and permitted service methods; rent-increase notice periods and nonrenewal or termination notice periods; statewide rent caps and just-cause termination requirements (for example Cal. Civ. Code §1947.12 and §1946.2), with local overlays where a city adds its own; entry-notice period; required lease disclosures; and record-retention periods. A property whose state or overlay pack is not active, or whose pack lacks a field an action needs, is held from that deposit, late-fee, notice or lease action with a visible setup gap; no default value is ever substituted. Rule changes are new dated versions, and past decisions keep the version they used. Authority (ct 22 Oct): the owner alone publishes, activates and records counsel review. Every operator in a property's portfolio scope reads that property's active pack values, citations, versions and held reasons. A portfolio manager may propose a property's jurisdiction, and it takes effect only on owner confirmation. Content: Terrace authors, under a counsel engagement recorded with reviewer, firm and date, the 19 fields plus state lease disclosures and addenda and notice templates (pay-or-quit, violation, entry, nonrenewal, deposit disposition) for every pack. Each ships inactive until Terrace's counsel review is recorded. An owner may instead activate their own counsel-reviewed pack or template, recorded as theirs. Terrace-researched drafts carry citations and a verified-on date, and they never drive an action while inactive. Missing/inactive fields hold dependent previews without substitution; a preview changes no operational record and sends or moves nothing. A recorded reviewer is an owner attestation, not verification by Terrace. No active counsel-reviewed values ship; see [the rule-pack guide](docs/state-rule-packs.md). Existing operating commands do not yet enforce these previews, so this remains partial. ACCT-003/004, PAY-006, LEASE-010/012, PORTAL-009, SAFE-004 and BOUND-002 inherit reviewed, version-bound, missing-field gates before their pack-dependent actions ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Run the same move-out with a $1,800 deposit in a California, a Texas and a Florida property: California returns an itemized statement due in 21 days by personal delivery or first-class mail (Cal. Civ. Code §1950.5(g)); Texas a refund due in 30 days after surrender (Tex. Prop. Code §92.103); Florida a certified-mail notice of claim due in 30 days, or a refund in 15 days with no claim (Fla. Stat. §83.49(3)). Compute a late fee in the Texas property only after rent stays unpaid two full days and within the 12% presumption for a structure of four or fewer units (Tex. Prop. Code §92.019). In a California property, propose a renewal increase above the §1947.12 cap and show it held with the cap calculation, and show a nonrenewal of a resident in occupancy for 12 months held until a §1946.2 just cause is recorded. List all 51 packs with version and review state, remove one field from a pack and show the dependent action blocked, then publish a new pack version and show an earlier disposition keeps its original version.

- **PORT-009 — Attach inspection media, work documents and invoices to their records.** Carved from PORT-007 by ct on 22 October 2026, which keeps leases, applications and notices; this clause carries the original sentence verbatim for inspection photos/video, work documents and invoices: “Attach and version leases, applications, notices, inspection photos/video, work documents and invoices on their records.” Inspection photos and video attach to their inspection, work documents to their work order and invoices to their vendor invoice, with their own bounds: photos and video exceed 5 MB and upload in resumable chunks, and each stored file keeps its original bytes and SHA-256. ROLE-001 scope and ROLE-002 vendor rights apply to every read. Exact storage semantics: photo/video originals up to 25 MB and other accepted documents up to 5 MB use 256 KB resumable chunks; finalization verifies the full SHA-256 and publishes one immutable version, keeping prior originals readable. Inspection media belongs to an inspection, work documents to a work order, and supporting invoice attachments to a vendor bill; supporting evidence never revises approved payable terms. Staff use existing work or bill rights, checked again on each request. A live vendor grant reads only current approved/sent assigned work and its own invoices at `/portal/record-media`, never inspection media; revoked sessions stop immediately. Originals are downloaded privately with a sandbox and no malware verdict or byte egress. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload a video to an inspection. SAFE-005 applies before this ships: each stored photo or video appears in the readable export as its original file with its SHA-256 and restores with the backup.

- **PORT-010 — Scan uploads with the owner’s scanner.** Carved from PORT-007 by ct on 22 October 2026: the malware-verdict leg of “scan uploads”; PORT-007 keeps its static screen. Scanner custody follows ct’s ruling of 22 October 2026 15:46Z: a verdict comes only from a scanner processor the owner configures for the installation (a self-hosted or owner-contracted scanning endpoint behind a Base adapter, with a server-held secret, audited configure, rotate and revoke, and recorded owner consent naming the processor); no document bytes leave the installation by default; bytes go only to that processor, over TLS, never logged, and Terrace keeps only the hash, verdict, scanner id and time; a scanner outage quarantines the upload (no download, a named reason, retry) and never passes it silently. **Acceptance evidence:** Scan uploads (the original PORT-007 malware-verdict leg, moved verbatim).

- **ROLE-001 — Grant staff rights by responsibility.** Owner controls access, integrations, money authorities and cutover. Portfolio managers lease and approve property work within assigned properties and limits; leasing staff manage prospects without bank data; bookkeepers post and reconcile without managing access; accountants read/export and propose close corrections; maintenance coordinators schedule work without approving payouts. Enforce these rights on pages, APIs, exports and search. Exact semantics: each non-owner operator holds one Terrace role (portfolio manager, leasing, bookkeeper, accountant, maintenance coordinator or member) over Base’s sign-in tier (portfolio managers sign in as admin, the others as member) and covers either every portfolio or only the portfolios the owner assigns. The owner alone controls access (invitations, deactivation, roles and portfolio assignments, on Terrace’s and Base’s operator doors alike), integrations, money authorities (the PORT-001 currency confirmation; payouts when they ship) and cutover (move-in import, backup, restore and erasure). One capability table in D1 lists each role’s actions; every command, page tab, API read, download and export checks it for the signed-in operator, and every write rechecks it with the live operator and the role version inside the same D1 batch, so a role or assignment change applies from the next request (a change of sign-in tier also ends that person’s sessions). A record outside the operator’s portfolios answers 404 and never reveals that it exists; an action outside their role answers 403. A tenancy without a unit is reached only by the owner and all-portfolio staff, and installation-wide changes (the company, legal entities, operating accounts, new portfolios and tenancies without a unit) need all-portfolio scope. Portfolio managers manage tenancies, households, renewals and their approval, rent, charge terms and runs, statements, the rent roll and collections, properties and units, inspections, vendors and schedules, and approve maintenance within the owner’s per-property job limit and yearly budget (WORK-003), never access. Leasing staff manage tenancies, households, move-out, transfers, turnovers and renewal proposals, and never see ledgers, receipts, statements, collections, rent-roll money, operating accounts or EINs. Bookkeepers post charges, receipts and corrections, run lease charge terms, prepare arrears follow-ups, and read statements, collections, the rent roll, legal entities and operating accounts, never people or access. Accountants read every ledger and download every statement, rent roll and collections report, and post nothing. Maintenance coordinators run inspections, prepare, quote, reassign and hand off maintenance, record completions, assets, vendors, schedules and turnovers, and never approve spend, set owner limits, post money or change access. Members read their portfolios and prepare renewal, arrears and maintenance proposals. Admins at the upgrade became portfolio managers over every portfolio and members stayed members over every portfolio; an operator invited through Base’s own door gets that same default at first sign-in until the owner sets a role. Every role or assignment change is recorded with who made it and when. Doors not built yet inherit this before they ship: OPS-001 credentials, PORTAL-001 to PORTAL-010 staff screens, LEASE-005 prospects, ACCT-008, ACCT-010 and ACCT-018 payouts, PORT-007 and PORTAL-006 search, OPS-004 integrations, and ROLE-003 per-person approval limits and separate payment authority. **Acceptance evidence:** Exercise each role across two assigned portfolios, directly request another property’s API/download, and attempt a payout as leasing staff and an access change as bookkeeper; every unauthorized path is denied. Until payouts ship (ACCT-008, ACCT-010, ACCT-018 carry the leasing refusal), leasing staff attempt to post money (an external receipt and the charge run) and are refused.

- **ROLE-002 — Isolate residents owners and vendors.** Residents see only their authorized lease/household accounts; owners see only properties and periods they own; vendors see assigned work and their invoices. Invitations, delegated contacts, ownership changes and revocation update rights immediately without exposing other households, owners, screening or bank details. **Acceptance evidence:** Invite a resident, joint owner and vendor, change an assignment and ownership date, then crawl portal pages, direct downloads and APIs before and after revocation. Exact semantics (ct ruling 22 October 2026 18:00Z, approved as adopted with riders): staff invite portal people (residents, delegated contacts, owners, vendors) with the fresh email-link proof, and owner and vendor grants need every-portfolio scope. Invitations and sign-in links are single-use and expire within 7 days. A session lasts 12 hours, and every request re-reads the live session, person and grant. A revocation, an ownership-date change (a new share set) and a work or invoice assignment change take effect on the next request and end the open sessions of the people they touch (the person revoked, the owners on either side of the change, the former and the new vendor), who sign in again by a fresh link. A delegated contact sees the lease’s balance and charges only, never screening, bank details, other households or documents, and the resident on the lease revokes them from their own portal page, recorded in history as theirs. An owner sees only the dated periods they own; after a sale they keep reading statements for the periods they owned, and nothing after. A vendor sees only approved or sent work assigned to them and their own invoices and originals. Portal people, grants, links and sessions are never archived: a restore carries no portal session or credential, and staff invite each person again. PORTAL-001, PORTAL-002 and PORTAL-003 inherit this door and add their own actions.

- **ROLE-003 — Apply dual control and spending limits.** Set owner-approved per-property repair limits, quote requirements, reserves and separate preparation/approval/payment authorities. Agents and preparers cannot approve their own work. Changed amount, payee, bank details or terms invalidate approval; bank-detail changes, including an ACH notification of change (ACCT-018), use independent verification and a separate audit event. SAFE-001 applies before this ships: a bank-detail change needs the changer’s fresh email-link proof. Exact semantics: the owner’s per-job limit and yearly budget (WORK-003) and, beside them, an optional quote requirement (2 to 10 quotes when a job’s estimate is above a set amount) are recorded per property by the owner or a portfolio manager, labeled “recorded by staff for the owner”; the reserve requirement is the management agreement’s (PORT-003). Preparation, approval and payment are separate capabilities in ROLE-001’s table: members, coordinators and agents prepare; portfolio managers and the owner approve; nobody pays yet. Whoever prepared a maintenance job, renewal or arrears proposal never approves it, the owner included, and whoever revises a job’s terms, selects a quote or reassigns its vendor becomes a preparer of those terms; the approval answers 403. The one exception is an installation where no other active operator who did not prepare the terms holds the approval capability: the preparer’s approval is then kept labeled “self-approved: no second person”, rechecked inside the approval’s D1 batch. A job above the quote requirement cannot be approved with fewer quotes recorded. Any change of amount, payee (vendor), scope, title, due date or quote after approval makes a new version that must be approved again (with the owner’s decision again when over the limit or budget) before the packet or handoff (WORK-003). Payments, owner distributions, payee bank details and notifications of change are carried by ACCT-008, ACCT-010 and ACCT-018 (with SAFE-001’s step-up), which apply these rules before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare an over-limit repair and owner distribution, change the payee after approval, and show approval escalation and execution refusal until an independently authorized person approves the exact new inputs. A bank-detail change without a fresh email-link proof is refused (403).

### Leasing acquisition and execution

- **LEASE-001 — Publish property marketing and vacancies.** Publish accessible property/unit pages with accurate availability, rent, fees, deposits, amenities, photos, floorplans and enquiry/application actions. Vacancies come from unit and lease status; managers preview changes and withdraw occupied units. One listing record is the source for every channel: the same unit publishes to the manager’s own site page and, through LEASE-002 and LEASE-003, to Zillow and Apartments.com, and a later edit or withdrawal reaches all three. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish two vacant units, submit an enquiry on mobile, lease one and confirm its vacancy is withdrawn while the other remains available with the approved price and fees. Edit the rent once and show the own-site page, the Zillow submission and the Apartments.com submission each carrying the new rent with its own channel status. LEASE-005 applies before this ships: an enquiry from the own-site page creates a LEASE-005 prospect with source “own site listing”, held for duplicate review like any other lead. REPORT-003 applies before this ships: its real listing publication, channel status and freshness become dated source events in the leasing-performance report; a ready unit never implies a fresh listing.

- **LEASE-002 — Syndicate listings to Zillow.** Connect authorized Zillow rental distribution, map required fields and media, submit approved listings and retain marketplace IDs, rejection details, updates and removals. Publication is confirmed from provider status; one submission is not proof that a listing is live. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish through the provider test boundary, correct a rejected fee field, change rent and withdraw the listing; show acknowledgments and the same external listing identity without duplicates. LEASE-005 applies before this ships: each Zillow lead creates a LEASE-005 prospect with source “marketplace listing” and the lead reference, held for duplicate review like any other lead. REPORT-003 applies before this ships: its real listing publication, channel status and freshness become dated source events in the leasing-performance report; a ready unit never implies a fresh listing.

- **LEASE-003 — Syndicate listings to Apartments.com.** Distribute approved vacancy, price, fee and photo data to Apartments.com using its supported partner path and account permissions. Reconcile accepted, rejected, updated and removed listings independently of Zillow. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit the same unit to Apartments.com, process a rejection and later success, update availability and remove it after lease execution; trace each provider result to the unit. LEASE-005 applies before this ships: each Apartments.com lead creates a LEASE-005 prospect with source “marketplace listing” and the lead reference, held for duplicate review like any other lead. REPORT-003 applies before this ships: its real listing publication, channel status and freshness become dated source events in the leasing-performance report; a ready unit never implies a fresh listing.

- **LEASE-004 — Extend listing reach with Zumper and RentCafe.** Offer separate authorized adapters for Zumper and the RentCafe ecosystem, with explicit entitlement and field mappings. Show per-channel freshness and errors and consolidate channel-attributed enquiries; an unavailable entitlement leaves a visible setup requirement. **Acceptance evidence:** Enable each adapter in its supported environment, publish and withdraw a unit, receive an enquiry and demonstrate that an unentitled account cannot appear connected or published. LEASE-005 applies before this ships: each Zumper or RentCafe lead creates a LEASE-005 prospect with source “marketplace listing” and the lead reference, held for duplicate review like any other lead.

- **LEASE-005 — Work prospect records and enquiries.** Capture web, marketplace, email and phone leads, deduplicate with review, retain household preferences, source, consent, assigned leasing staff and activity history. Track enquiry to showing, application, offer and lost reason without importing general sales CRM scope. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: leasing staff work prospects in their portfolios and never see bank data. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive a listing enquiry and duplicate email, review the match, assign a leasing person, respond and follow that prospect through showing and application with source attribution intact. Leasing staff work a prospect in their portfolio and get 404 for another portfolio’s prospect. Exact semantics (19 October 2026): the owner, portfolio managers and leasing staff record each lead on a property in their portfolios with its source (own site listing, marketplace listing, email, phone, walk-in, referral) and the listing, message or call reference; a public enquiry form is LEASE-001’s door and creates the same prospect with source “own site listing”. A lead whose email (case-insensitive) or phone (digits, a leading US 1 dropped) matches an open, unmerged prospect in the same portfolio is held as a possible duplicate and cannot be worked until a person merges it (both histories and sources kept, the first contact’s source and reference fixed, per-channel consent the most restrictive of the two) or keeps it separate; nothing merges by itself. Household preferences are bedrooms, occupants, move-in date, monthly budget in exact cents, pets and notes; consent is granted, refused or unknown per channel (email, phone, text) with its time and source, and a response on a refused channel is refused. Staff email a prospect from the record through the installation’s mail provider only while email consent is granted (an opt-out records it refused and stops sending): the written message is kept in the history before sending and the provider’s own outcome beside it (accepted by the provider with delivery not confirmed, rejected, rate-limited, uncertain, unreachable, suppressed in development or demo, or no provider configured), replies going to the sender’s own email; phone and text responses are logged as “recorded by staff; Terrace did not contact the prospect” until PORTAL-005 (ct ruling 19:01Z). One assigned person (an active owner, portfolio manager or leasing staff member in that portfolio). Stages move forward only: enquiry, showing scheduled, shown, applied, offer, leased; or lost, with a reason (chose another home, price, unit no longer available, did not qualify, stopped responding, other with a note). Showings and applications are staff-recorded stages with a date and reference until LEASE-006 and LEASE-007 carry them. Members read prospects; bookkeepers, accountants and maintenance coordinators get 403; another portfolio’s prospect is 404; prospects hold no bank data. Prospect records are kept 3 years after their last activity (SAFE-004 communications) and the owner erases one on request, history keeping only an opaque alias.

- **LEASE-006 — Coordinate tours and showing access.** Offer resident-safe showing slots, conflict checks, reminders, cancellations and no-show follow-up; honor notice/access rules and occupancy. Integrate Tenant Turner and Showings Coordinator and sync appointments with Google Calendar and Microsoft 365 without revealing resident private data. **Acceptance evidence:** Book competing tours, reschedule through the prospect link, cancel one and process a no-show; verify each connected scheduler/calendar and the permitted access window agree.

- **LEASE-007 — Take complete online applications.** Applicants submit mobile applications for each adult/co-applicant with identity, income, rental history, references, required disclosures, attachments and provider-collected application fees. Save progress, request missing evidence and prevent staff from silently changing submitted answers. **Acceptance evidence:** Two co-applicants save and resume, upload income evidence and submit; manager requests one missing document and sees revisions and fee outcome without card data in Terrace.

- **LEASE-008 — Order consented TransUnion screening.** Use TransUnion’s authorized screening service for credit, background and eviction data after explicit applicant consent and provider onboarding. Restrict report access, show coverage, pending/error states and provider references, and retain consent and retrieval provenance. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a consented application to the provider sandbox, receive a delayed report and duplicate callback, deny an unauthorized report download and show provider errors without fabricating a screening result.

- **LEASE-009 — Review applicants and adverse actions.** Managers apply disclosed criteria consistently, inspect source reports and record the human decision. Provide approved adverse-action packages, dispute/provider contacts and delivery evidence; accommodation and contested findings route to authorized staff or counsel. Agents never rank protected traits or choose a tenant. Criteria include the manager’s disclosed income rule (for example monthly income of at least a stated multiple of rent), evaluated against verified income and shown with its result beside the screening report; an approval or decline notice reaches the applicant only after the manager’s explicit decision. **Acceptance evidence:** Review two applications, flag a disputed report, require a manager decision and send an explicitly approved adverse-action package with the correct provider reference and recorded delivery. Apply an income-multiple rule to both applications, show the calculation beside the report, approve one and decline the other, and show each applicant’s notice sent only after that decision with its delivery record. SAFE-002 applies before this ships: a screening file export is a history row with outcome “exported”.

- **LEASE-010 — Compose jurisdiction-reviewed lease templates.** Maintain property/jurisdiction template versions with the required disclosures and addenda listed in the property's PORT-008 state and local pack, merge reviewed application and approved terms and compare deviations. Missing mandatory inputs block issue; managers or counsel approve legal wording rather than receiving an AI claim of legal validity. **Acceptance evidence:** Generate a lease with co-signers, pet addendum and local disclosure, detect a missing required input and approve a changed term while preserving the template version and redline.

- **LEASE-011 — Collect legally evidenced electronic signatures.** Send leases and renewals to every required resident, guarantor and manager with consent, signing order, identity evidence, reminders, expiry and declined/void states. Integrate Inkwell or DocuSign; only the completed artifact and certificate activate the lease, and changed terms require a new envelope. **Acceptance evidence:** Send a multi-signer lease, process one decline and a replacement envelope, complete all signatures, replay its callback and attach exactly one executed PDF/certificate to the activated tenancy. PORT-005 applies before this ships: the executed original and certificate establish a retained signed version and its source-linked charge schedule, rather than overwriting a prior signed version. LEASE-012 applies before this ships: renewals sent for electronic signature replace the staff-recorded signed renewal original, and only the completed artifact and certificate activate the renewal once.

- **LEASE-012 — Run renewal and retention campaigns.** Schedule renewal work from lease-end dates, compare proposed terms with current rent and vacancy assumptions, deliver approved offers, track replies and deadlines and collect signatures. Acceptance activates future terms once; nonresponse, nonrenewal and month-to-month conversion create named next actions. The comparison shows the proposed rent’s change from current rent in dollars and percent, a dated market-rent assumption and an estimated turnover cost (vacant days at the unit’s rent plus make-ready and leasing costs), each with its source. Exact semantics (20 October 2026, ct ruling): anyone holding `renewal.prepare` schedules an inclusive window of at most 367 days of lease end dates (optionally one property) within their portfolios, creating one renewal per current, not-ended tenancy and lease end, never twice; a scheduled lease end can no longer take TER-003’s direct recorded renewal, which remains labelled recorded terms for leases without campaign work. An offer names the proposed end and rent per the tenancy’s cadence, a reply deadline from today through the current lease end, a dated market rent (an assumption, with its source), expected vacant days (0–365) and make-ready and leasing costs, each with its source; its recipients are frozen as the household’s current PORT-004 notice recipients who have an email address. The comparison, frozen with the offer, is the change from current rent in cents and in basis points of current rent, the difference from the market rent in cents and basis points of the market rent (both rounded half away from zero to 0.01%), and turnover cost = vacant days × current rent × periods per year (12, 26 or 52) ÷ 365, rounded half up once to the cent, plus make-ready and leasing costs. An owner or portfolio manager approves the exact offer under `proposal.approve` with ROLE-003 independence (sole-operator label); approval changes no lease. Owner, portfolio manager or leasing staff send an approved offer explicitly through the installation mail provider, with reply-to the sending staff mailbox; each recipient’s attempt is recorded before sending and the provider’s answer after it; “accepted” means the provider accepted the email, never delivery; an accepted or uncertain attempt is never sent again; demo and development mail are suppressed and labelled not sent. Replies (accepted, declined, counteroffer, unclear) and outcomes (no response, only after the deadline; nonrenewal; month-to-month) are staff-recorded with their date and source, never inbox-synced; a counteroffer reopens the offer. Each state names its next action, and every renewal stays in the follow-up queue until its renewed terms activate; nonrenewal and month-to-month send no legal notice and convert nothing automatically. After an accepted reply, an owner or portfolio manager records the signed renewal as a PORT-005 lease version effective the day after the current end, through the offer’s end, whose rent equals the accepted offer; it is labelled “signature recorded by staff, not verified by an e-signature provider”. Another person approves its PAY-001 preview; that approval, once only, retains the prior term in history, extends the tenancy and activates the versioned schedule atomically, and the renewal fee (ACCT-009) is earned on that day. LEASE-011 inherits electronic signature of renewals by name before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a renewal window with accepted, declined and unanswered offers; trace approved delivery and executed future terms, and verify the unresolved household remains in the follow-up queue. Before approving a 12-month renewal, show its percentage increase against the dated market rent and the estimated turnover cost. SAFE-005 applies before this ships: its signed renewal documents appear in the readable export and come back with a restore into a fresh installation. PORT-005 applies before this ships: approved executed renewal terms activate a reviewed versioned charge schedule with its signed source and prior versions retained. REPORT-007 applies before this ships: actual approved renewals source its cash/vacancy comparison with dated terms, while proposed alternatives remain labeled assumptions. REPORT-003 applies before this ships: campaign, reply and executed-renewal outcomes replace the report’s recorded-term limitation with dated sources and no inferred signature or delivery.

### Rent collection and receivables

- **PAY-001 — Post recurring rent and lease charges.** Generate recurring rent, utilities, pet/parking charges, concessions and move-in/out prorations from effective lease terms in USD. Preview a run, surface missing terms and prevent duplicate posting across retries, amendments and month boundaries. Exact semantics: lease charge terms (rent, utility, pet, parking or concession) hold an amount per billing period in the tenancy’s stored currency (USD for new tenancies, PORT-001) and an effective start and optional end. A monthly tenancy bills calendar months; a weekly or fortnightly tenancy bills 7- or 14-day periods counted from its lease start; a month’s run covers the periods that start in that month, so a period crossing a month boundary belongs to one run. A term covers the days of a period inside both the lease (its move-in and move-out dates) and the term; a partly covered period is prorated as amount × covered days ÷ period days, rounded half up to the cent, and falls due on its first covered day. A concession posts as a reduction of the same period’s effective rent and never exceeds it. If one concession spans multiple rent segments, its covered-period total is prorated and rounded once as above, then split by the segments’ covered days: floor each share and give remainder cents to the longest segment, earliest on a tie. Uncovered, overlapping or excessive concession allocations hold posting rather than omit the concession; zero-cent shares need no posting. A preview lists every line as new or posted and each period with no rent term as missing; posting requires the preview’s fingerprint, and each line’s reference (term and period start) is unique, so a retried or replayed run posts nothing twice. A term is amended from an effective date after its last posted period; posted charges never change. An owner or admin previews and posts. A renewal approval (TER-003) does not change terms; PORT-005 and LEASE-012 make a lease amendment or renewal write its terms here before they ship, and PAY-006 late fees and PAY-013 voucher splits post through the same run. **Acceptance evidence:** Preview and post rent for leases with a concession and mid-month move-in, replay the run and amend future rent; verify each period posts once and posted history is preserved.

- **PAY-002 — Collect rent through ACH.** Connect the manager’s authorized Stripe ACH account or contracted rent processor using hosted bank authorization and required onboarding. Residents see USD fees and authorization before paying; pending, submitted and settled states remain distinct and each attempt has one provider identity. Each receipt type settles to the bank account ACCT-002 maps it to, using a separate processor connected account per receiving bank account where the processor pays out to one account, so an online security deposit never lands in the rent-trust account. **Acceptance evidence:** Pay a resident balance through ACH sandbox authorization, restart after provider submission and reconcile pending then settled callbacks without a second debit or exposing bank credentials. In a property whose deposit and rent-trust accounts differ, pay a security deposit and the first month's rent online and show the deposit payout settling to the deposit bank account and the rent payout to the trust account. DEMO-001 applies before this ships: its demo flow retains the effect guard and adds a public-door no-egress assertion; no real payment, message or webhook is sent from a demo.

- **PAY-003 — Collect rent by card.** Use Stripe-hosted card entry or an approved rent processor with tokenized payment methods. Disclose permitted payer fees, accept supported debit/credit cards, handle required authentication and retain payment references without storing PAN or security codes. Card receipts settle to the bank account ACCT-002 maps their charge type to, as for PAY-002. **Acceptance evidence:** Pay a partial balance with a test card requiring authentication, inspect the disclosed fee, complete payment and confirm one resident receipt and matching provider reference. Pay a security deposit by card in a property with separate deposit and trust accounts and show it settling to the deposit account. DEMO-001 applies before this ships: its demo flow retains the effect guard and adds a public-door no-egress assertion; no real payment, message or webhook is sent from a demo.

- **PAY-004 — Manage resident autopay mandates.** Residents authorize fixed amount or outstanding-balance autopay, start/end dates, limits and advance notifications; managers control eligibility without inventing authorization. A person approves each mandate, which supplies standing authority for scheduled debits within its exact limits. Cancellation stops unsent attempts. **Acceptance evidence:** Authorize capped balance autopay, change the bill above its cap, then cancel before the next run; verify the permitted debit, held exception, notice and canceled attempt. DEMO-001 applies before this ships: its demo flow retains the effect guard and adds a public-door no-egress assertion; no real payment, message or webhook is sent from a demo.

- **PAY-005 — Enforce partial and split payment policies.** Configure partial-payment rules by lease and delinquency stage within the property's PORT-008 pack, distinguish pending from settled funds, support co-tenant split payments and resident/housing-authority split rent (PAY-013), and allocate receipts by explicit charge priority. Reject overpayment or hold it as separately identified credit according to approved policy. **Current semantics:** Owner-recorded lease policies order explicit charge ids and define increasing days-past-due stages. Admission uses property-local today and the oldest outstanding charge; both lease and every active PORT-008 partialPayments stage must allow a partial amount or credit. Missing/inactive packs hold admission. Pending external funds reserve charge capacity atomically without reducing receivables; settlement uses the frozen allocation once, failure releases it. Settled excess is separately identified unapplied credit, excluded from charge receipts and owner income; no credit is automatically spent. Policy snapshots retain exact pack versions. PAY-002/003/004 and PAY-013 inherit the same admission/reservation gate before their new collection doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Two co-tenants pay concurrently while one ACH is pending; show allocation, remaining balance and permitted credit, and refuse a partial payment under a reviewed stage-specific block.

- **PAY-006 — Calculate late fees and grace periods.** Apply the grace period, cap and fee basis from the property's PORT-008 state and local pack, with weekend/holiday rules and lease terms that may only be stricter than the pack; show the calculation and permit authorized waivers with reasons. Reversals and delayed settlements recalculate only as the approved policy allows, with no compounding surprise. **Current semantics:** The operational calculator accepts confirmed USD monthly-rent charges explicitly identified in owner-recorded lease fee terms. Each active state/local pack must state its monthly-rent basis, cap, full unpaid grace days, weekendRule (calendar or next_business_day), explicit holidays, pendingPolicy (exclude_timely or count_pending) and reversalPolicy (hold or recalculate_once). Missing values hold execution. The lease may only lower the requested fee/cap, extend grace, move charging to the next business day or protect timely pending funds. The first fee day follows the full unpaid days after the due day, shifted by the explicit calendar; all applicable packs must allow it. Eligibility reconstructs unpaid principal on the first fee day (or the earlier schedule day), so later principal settlement does not erase an earned fee. Timely pending means initiated before that first fee day; later successful settlement retains that protection, and a failed timely pending payment follows the explicit reversal policy. A human reviews the exact fingerprint before posting. One source rent charge receives at most one fee; later recalculation under its original frozen policy may only reduce an unpaid, unreserved fee, never increase or compound it. A paid/reserved reduction is held for reviewed refund/reallocation; a waiver records its actor, day and reason. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a late-fee schedule across a weekend, record a timely pending payment that settles later and waive one fee; inspect charge basis, policy version and auditable waiver. Charge the same late rent in a Texas and a California property and show each pack's grace period, cap and citation on the calculation.

- **PAY-007 — Offer cash-at-retail and offline payment options.** Provide PayNearMe or a contracted retail-cash network with resident payment codes, fees, receipt references and settlement tracking. Record check, money-order and external ACH/check-scan deposits, allocating each once and distinguishing receipt from bank clearance. **Acceptance evidence:** Generate a cash code, receive and replay its retail transaction, clear a check and return another; reconcile resident balances to settlement batches without treating a printed code as collected rent. SAFE-002 applies before this ships: a returned or reversed payment is a new history row and a new posting, never an edit of the receipt.

- **PAY-008 — Resolve failed payments returns and disputes.** Handle ACH returns, NSF fees, card disputes, chargebacks and canceled attempts with processor evidence, resident communication and reopened receivables. Retries follow approved mandates and contact rules; suspended methods cannot be charged again silently. **Acceptance evidence:** Return a previously settled ACH and dispute a card payment, inspect reversal entries and restored balances, submit approved evidence and verify a revoked mandate prevents another attempt. SAFE-002 applies before this ships: an ACH return is a new history row and a reversing posting, never an edit of the receipt. REPORT-002 applies before this ships: add returned/reversed ACH and pending/attempted collection outcomes, including its returned-ACH delinquency acceptance to the as-of report with dated source drills and no inferred settlement or resolution.

- **PAY-009 — Authorize refunds credits and write-offs.** Prepare refunds to the original method, by ACH (ACCT-018), or by printed or mailed check to a forwarding address (ACCT-017), and reasoned credits/write-offs with before/after resident and owner effects. Human approval names payee, amount and source; limits and independent execution checks prevent duplicate or excessive refunds and preserve original receipts. **Current external-record semantics:** Refunds, credits and write-offs have immutable full revisions with exact payee, amount, source, day and reason, before/after resident charge balance and owner ledger effects. Owner or in-scope portfolio manager prepares; ROLE-003 independence approves, with the sole-operator label only when no other active approver exists. A source, balance, allocation, reservation or authority change requires new review. Recording execution requires fresh email-link proof and explicit RECORDED confirmation of the external fact. Partial refunds reopen only the refunded receipt amount and reverse cash to its original frozen owners, proportionally to their remaining original receipt allocations in exact cents (floor each share, remainder in descending remaining allocation, owner id on a tie, capped at each owner’s remaining amount); originals remain unchanged. Credits/write-offs use the existing adjustment journal at the posting day ownership, reducing lease income or tax liability rather than claiming a cash refund. Check preparation records an approved numbered non-negotiable forwarding-address draft; external issuance is a staff-entered fact, never a print/mail, bank-clearance or provider-verification claim. No payment instruction is sent by these commands. ACCT-017/018 inherit the exact revision, live approval, limits and once-only source gate when their rails ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare and approve a refund, change its source after approval and refuse it; execute an unchanged refund twice and reconcile one provider refund, one ledger reversal and the correct owner effect; issue a former resident's refund by check to a forwarding address and see it in the check register.

- **PAY-010 — Issue resident statements and receipts.** Deliver itemized USD rent statements/invoices and payment receipts with due dates, lease charges, pending funds, fees, credits and current balance. Residents can download accessible PDF/CSV and inspect the source transaction; delivery failures create a follow-up. **Acceptance evidence:** Generate a monthly statement, pay part of it, receive a delivered receipt, fail the statement email and inspect the resident portal’s matching balance and delivery task.

- **PAY-011 — Work delinquencies to a recorded outcome.** Use aging by property/owner/resident, contact consent, approved message sequences, promises-to-pay, payment plans and actual receipts. Stop obsolete messages after payment, honor disputes/holds and escalate broken promises; notices, concessions, write-offs and eviction require authorized people. Pay-or-quit and lease-violation notices use the pack's notice period and are served and evidenced through PORTAL-009. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a sequence for three late households, receive a reply and payment plan, settle one balance and break another promise; verify stopped messages, next actions and human notice approval, and serve the approved pay-or-quit notice with recorded posting evidence and its expiry date computed from service. REPORT-002 applies before this ships: add active and broken payment plans, notices and collection outcomes, including its active-plan delinquency acceptance to the as-of report with dated source drills and no inferred settlement or resolution.

- **PAY-012 — Reconcile processor fees and settlements.** Match gross receipts, processing fees, refunds, reserves, payout batches and housing-authority HAP deposits (PAY-013) to bank deposits and the owner/property/tenant ledger. Replay or reorder callbacks safely; unexplained settlement differences remain exceptions and never become fabricated cash. **Acceptance evidence:** Collect several rents into one net payout with a refund and fee, import its bank line and reconcile gross-to-net; replay callbacks and leave an intentionally short payout unresolved. Reconcile an online deposit payout against the deposit bank account and the rent payout against the trust account separately.

- **PAY-013 — Split voucher rent between resident and housing authority.** For market-rate leases with Housing Choice Voucher (Section 8) or other tenant-based rental assistance, record the HAP contract and the public housing authority (PHA) as a separate payer with its own receivable, and the tenant and HAP portions with effective dates. Each rent run posts both charges; one PHA ACH or check covering many households is allocated across leases, properties and owners from the PHA remittance detail, with any unmatched remainder held as an exception. A recertification that changes the split posts retroactive adjustments to both receivables from its effective date with the PHA notice attached. HAP abatement after a failed inspection suspends or reverses the PHA charge for the abated period and never shifts it to the resident. Resident, owner and delinquency views show tenant and PHA balances separately, and a late HAP payment never triggers a resident late fee. **Acceptance evidence:** Set up two voucher leases under different owners, post tenant and HAP portions, receive one PHA ACH covering both and allocate it, apply a HAP change effective three months back and one month's abatement; show tenant, PHA and owner balances, a delinquency report separating tenant arrears from PHA arrears and no late fee on PHA arrears. PORT-005 applies before this ships: each HAP contract, split and effective revision names its signed version and source clauses, with reviewed amendments before posting. REPORT-007 applies before this ships: actual tenant/PHA portions and payer outcomes source cash forecasts separately without shifting HAP arrears to residents. REPORT-002 applies before this ships: add tenant versus housing-authority arrears, including its unpaid-HAP delinquency acceptance to the as-of report with dated source drills and no inferred settlement or resolution.

### Trust accounting and owner finance

- **ACCT-001 — Maintain a balanced property ledger.** Provide a double-entry USD general ledger and owner, property, tenant, vendor and security-deposit subledgers with a configurable chart of accounts, opening balances and source links. Each posting balances, each correction reverses rather than rewrites, and no owner’s funds cover another owner’s obligations. A duplicate receipt is corrected by a reversing entry, and its resident, property and owner subledger postings trace together to that reversal. Exact accounting semantics: [the property-ledger guide](docs/property-ledger.md) states the implemented chart, exact-cent source entries, immutable reversals, per-owner/property/fund cash fence, dated-owner allocation, legacy opaque beneficiary keys, USD boundary, role/scope, month-close snapshots and retention. This records external facts and never moves funds. A reversing receipt retains the original received-date owner allocation and agreement; its fee-run correction reverses the recorded fee and tax, including prior overrides, with exact inverse cent rounding. ACCT-002/003/004/008/010/012/013/018 and PAY-002/003/004/007/008/009/012/013 inherit balanced source entries, reversal tracing and beneficiary/fund isolation before their money actions ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Post rent, deposit, vendor expense and owner contribution across two properties, attempt an unbalanced entry and inspect the trial balance and each subledger back to source. Post a receipt twice, reverse the duplicate and trace its resident, property and owner ledger entries to the reversal with the original entry left in place.

- **ACCT-002 — Separate operating trust and deposit accounts.** Map legal entities and properties to authorized operating, rent-trust and deposit bank accounts. Enforce designated-fund separation, beneficiary balances, allowed transfers and reserves, with human approval and bank references for any transfer. Every outbound ACH file or provider batch (ACCT-018) and every check run (ACCT-017) draws on exactly one bank account. Trace commingling exceptions before money can move. Exact custody semantics: [the trust-account guide](docs/trust-accounts.md) describes USD bank references, legal-entity/property authorizations, immutable designated purposes, per-bank/property/beneficiary cash, journal-to-custody reconciliation, historical unassigned exceptions and reserve-checked same-beneficiary transfers. This records external bank facts, never initiates money movement or claims bank-statement verification. ACCT-003/004/008/010/017/018 and PAY-002/003/007/008/009/012/013 inherit authorized account/fund/beneficiary isolation and source tracing before their money actions ship; ACCT-017/018 must enforce exactly one paying bank account per check run/file/provider batch. The conservative authorization default adopted this round is owner-only bank configuration and historical assignment with fresh email-link proof; scoped bookkeeper/portfolio-manager preparation and external recording; portfolio-manager/owner human approval under ROLE-003, with fresh proof for approval/recording and live authority/reserve rechecks. Ct approval of that default is pending. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive rent and deposits into distinct accounts, attempt an owner payout from deposit funds and an inter-owner transfer, and verify blocked execution and separately reconciled beneficiary balances.

- **ACCT-003 — Receive hold and accrue security deposits.** Track deposit obligations, collections, permitted installment plans, bank custody, per-resident ownership, deposit caps, separate-account and receipt rules and applicable interest from the property's PORT-008 state and local pack. Give required receipts and records; deposits remain liabilities rather than rent income and owner transfers preserve custody obligations. Where the management agreement and the pack allow it, a deposit can be recorded as owner-held: Terrace tracks the liability, receipt, holder, any pack-required disclosure and the disposition deadline with no manager bank custody, and the ACCT-004 disposition directs the owner to refund the balance or records the owner funding the refund through the manager. **Acceptance evidence:** Collect a deposit in installments, accrue reviewed interest and transfer ownership; inspect bank, beneficiary and tenant balances and receipts without recognizing rent revenue. Record a second deposit as owner-held and show its liability and deadline tracked with no balance in the manager's deposit account, then complete its disposition with the owner's refund recorded. PORT-005 applies before this ships: deposit obligations and amendments retain the signed version, effective dates and source clauses. REPORT-007 applies before this ships: deposit actuals replace explicitly labeled held/receipt/refund assumptions without mixing liabilities with operating cash.

- **ACCT-004 — Complete deposit disposition and refunds.** At move-out, compare entry/exit condition and unpaid obligations, prepare evidenced itemized deductions and a balance refund, and track the PORT-008 pack's deadline and required delivery method. The disposition goes out through PORTAL-009 mail, certified mail or recorded service (or electronic delivery only where the pack allows it), and the refund pays by ACH (ACCT-018) or by check to the forwarding address (ACCT-017). Managers approve deductions and money movement separately; disputes retain original evidence and unresolved liability. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a move-out with damage and normal wear, approve only supported deductions, deliver the disposition and execute the approved refund; verify deadline, proof and remaining deposit liability. In a Florida property send the claim notice by certified mail and show the 30-day deadline met against the mailing date, then refund the balance by printed check to the forwarding address.

- **ACCT-005 — Connect Plaid bank feeds.** Connect US bank accounts through Plaid-authorized consent, map each feed to the correct books, import stable transactions and surface pending-to-posted changes, missing periods and reauthorization. No bank password lives in Terrace; manual statement import remains a first-class documented input. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect two bank accounts through the provider boundary, import duplicate and pending-to-posted lines, expire consent and reconnect; verify no duplicate bank transaction and a visible freshness gap.

- **ACCT-006 — Match statements and perform three-way reconciliation.** Import bank CSV, OFX/QFX and statement PDFs with reviewed extracted lines, match settlements and ledger entries, match cleared checks by number and amount (ACCT-017), match transmitted ACH files and entries by trace number, batch total or entry amount (ACCT-018), record outstanding checks/deposits and prove bank balance equals adjusted book balance and beneficiary subledger totals. Unmatched amounts block a clean close. **Acceptance evidence:** Reconcile a month with batched rent, fee, outstanding check, a cleared owner ACH batch and missing deposit; resolve one exception and show the remaining difference prevents a balanced three-way sign-off.

- **ACCT-007 — Capture and approve vendor bills.** Capture PDF/image/email invoices, supplier, invoice number, date, coding, line items, tax and attachments. Check duplicates, allocate shared costs to properties/owners and require approval against work, budgets and management authority before payment. Recurring payables (owner mortgages, HOA dues, insurance premiums, utilities) are set up once with payee, amount, schedule, end date and property/owner allocation; each period generates one bill under the same approval rules, and a changed template amount or payee needs new approval. A residential owner’s HOA dues are such a recurring payable, with the association as payee, never association dues or association accounting (BOUND-004). Exact semantics (ct 19 October 13:49Z): the owner, portfolio managers and bookkeepers capture an original PDF, JPEG, PNG or .eml email up to 5 MB privately and enter its supplier from the vendor directory, invoice number/date, USD line descriptions, expense codes, pre-tax amounts and tax in exact cents; Terrace does not extract or validate the invoice with a provider. Attachments download only for those roles and accountants reaching every current and historical allocated property; out-of-scope records are 404, other roles 403. Supplier plus case-folded invoice number (including prior revisions), and the exact bytes of an original, prevent duplicates. Property allocations including tax must equal the bill total. Approval needs dated owner shares and a management agreement for every property; a linked work order must belong to that property, have the same supplier and currency and approved terms. Per-job limits, annual budgets, approved work amounts and cumulative work-linked invoices are checked; the budget uses the larger of each reserved approved estimate or its approved actual invoices, plus unlinked payables, rather than counting linked work twice. Missing source/authority is held. A manager or owner records the owner’s exact source-backed decision for an over-limit, over-budget or over-estimate bill, labeled recorded by staff for the owner, then a different owner or portfolio manager approves its exact revision under ROLE-003 (sole operator approval is explicitly labeled). Approval records an unpaid payable, splits each property’s cost using PORT-003 shares effective on the invoice date, and records the dated agreement’s markup and tax on markup, half up after the owner split. The owner allocation statement shows these expenses, fees and agreement references and subtracts them from available USD cash with the reserve share in force at period end (property ids identify reserves, even when names repeat). Changing terms, payee or attachments makes a pending revision and reverses prior markup with new lines; earlier snapshots stay and the changed obligation needs fresh approval. Monthly recurring templates carry payee, amount/lines, allocations, first/last bill date and day of month; days 29–31 clamp to the month’s last day, and a run is allowed only when that date has arrived at every allocated property. Exact template approval and each period bill’s separate approval are required; edits reopen template approval without changing bills already generated, and a unique template/month key makes replay safe. Closed months refuse new or changed bills and markup. ACCT-008 and ACCT-018 carry payment execution; no money moves here. SAFE-004 applies: work-linked subject references survive work deletion, accounting periods and either resident’s hold retain shared originals (the other subject’s hold is explained without identity or reason); once eligible, originals and personal revision/decision/audit text are erased/redacted under the erasure gate while amounts, dates, allocations and original fingerprints stay. A minimal erased-file hash suppresses reupload and the archive journal blocks restoration of older copies. Resident access lists their shared accounting source ids without another party’s invoice text or amounts. SAFE-005 archives private originals, revisions and owner expense rows; ACCT-012 expands full owner statements and WORK-009 adds invoice extraction/matching before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload the same invoice twice, split an approved landscaping bill across properties, exceed an owner’s limit and inspect the held bill, approval route and resulting payable. Set up a monthly HOA-dues recurring bill for a residential owner, generate two months and replay the run, and show exactly one bill per month, each posted as a payable to the association and not as association dues (BOUND-004). PORT-003 applies before this ships: each approved bill on a property is allocated to its owners by the share set in force on the bill date, so an expense before a transfer stays with the seller.

- **ACCT-008 — Pay vendors and reconcile payment outcomes.** Prepare vendor ACH payments executed through ACCT-018 (a NACHA file per paying bank account at the manager’s bank, or the Modern Treasury payment-order API), or checks that Terrace prints or sends through Lob (ACCT-017), validate verified payees and available owner funds, and execute only human-approved batches. Track sent, settled, failed, returned and voided results with bank/check references and cleared payables. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: only the owner and roles the capability table grants payment preparation reach these doors, within their portfolios; leasing staff, maintenance coordinators, accountants and members are refused (403). **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a vendor batch, change one bank destination and hold it, execute the unchanged items in the paying account’s ACCT-018 NACHA file and import an R01 return from the bank’s return file; show one payment per bill, a remittance notice per vendor and the reopened returned payable. Pay a check-only vendor in the same batch by printed check and show its register entry. Leasing staff attempting this payout are refused (403), and a bookkeeper outside the paying property’s portfolios gets 404. ROLE-003 applies before this ships: the person who prepared a vendor payment never approves it (a sole operator’s approval is labeled “self-approved: no second person”), and a changed amount or payee after approval needs a new approval of the exact inputs before execution.

- **ACCT-009 — Calculate management fees and owner reserves.** Configure effective management fees, leasing/renewal fees, minimums, markups, tax treatment and reserve floors by agreement. Show each calculation’s source, prevent charging twice and respect available owner cash before distributions; overrides need explicit authority. Exact semantics: fee terms belong to PORT-003’s dated management agreement, the one in force on each fee’s day: the management fee percent of collected rent, a flat leasing fee per new lease, a flat renewal fee, a monthly minimum management fee, a tax rate on fees and a markup percent for vendor bills, all in USD; the reserve floor is the agreement’s reserve requirement. A property’s fee run for a month (this month or earlier, property-local; the owner, portfolio managers and bookkeepers in its portfolio) records one line per owner and source: the management fee on each owner’s share of every confirmed-USD receipt received that month (receipts on ACCT-016 tax charges excepted) (share split and fee rounding as PORT-003: floor per share, remainder cents to the largest share, fee half up to the cent; receipts in another or an unconfirmed currency are listed as skipped), the leasing fee on each lease starting that month on one of its units (a unit transfer is not a new lease), the renewal fee on each renewal approved that month (its property-local approval day), and, once the month has ended, the top-up that brings that month’s management fees to the monthly minimum; flat fees are split by the shares in force on their day. Tax on each line is the agreement’s rate of the fee, half up to the cent, as recorded; Terrace files and remits no tax. Each line names its source (receipt reference, lease, renewal or minimum), base, rate, agreement and run. A rerun posts only the difference between what the records now call for and what is recorded, so nothing is charged twice, and two runs at once cannot both post; fee lines are never edited or deleted, and a run or override for a month closed under ACCT-011 is refused until it is reopened. Only the owner overrides a fee (ROLE-001 money authority): the override is a new line setting that owner’s fee for that source to the stated amount with a reason, and later runs leave that source alone. The PORT-003 owner allocation statement lists each owner’s recorded fee lines with their agreement reference and the owner’s USD cash available: their share of receipts less recorded fees, tax on fees and their reserve floor share in force at the period end; ACCT-010 distributions never exceed it before they ship, ACCT-007 vendor bills now apply the agreement markup and carry approved expenses into it; ACCT-012 full owner statements inherit these lines before shipping. **Acceptance evidence:** Post rent and a lease renewal under a dated fee schedule, calculate fees/reserve, replay the run and inspect the owner statement with the exact agreement references.

- **ACCT-010 — Disburse owner funds by ACH or check.** Prepare distributions from cleared beneficiary cash less reserves, unpaid obligations and approved fees; handle ownership shares and contributions. Owners choose ACH, executed through ACCT-018 (a NACHA file per trust bank account, or the Modern Treasury payment-order API), or check (printed or mailed through ACCT-017); each owner receives a remittance notice with the distribution statement. A human approves exact bank destination or check payee/address and amount before execution; pending receipts never fund an owner payout. Reconcile returns and replacements without duplicate distributions. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: only the owner and roles the capability table grants payment preparation reach these doors, within their portfolios; leasing staff, maintenance coordinators, accountants and members are refused (403). **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare a joint-owner distribution with a pending ACH receipt and unpaid repair, approve cleared funds only, execute it in the trust account’s ACCT-018 NACHA file and import an R01 return for one share from the bank’s return file; show corrected cash and one replacement requiring new approval. Leasing staff attempting this payout are refused (403), and a bookkeeper outside the paying property’s portfolios gets 404. ROLE-003 applies before this ships: the person who prepared a owner distribution never approves it (a sole operator’s approval is labeled “self-approved: no second person”), and a changed amount or payee after approval needs a new approval of the exact inputs before execution. REPORT-007 applies before this ships: actual distributions and returns source its forecasts without treating a planned payout as executed.

- **ACCT-011 — Close periods without rewriting history.** Use month-end checklists, reconciliation sign-offs, exception queues and locked accounting periods. Authorized accountants propose adjustments; reopening a period requires owner/bookkeeper authority, a reason and a new close version, with affected statements marked superseded. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: accountants propose close corrections as prepared proposals that an authorized bookkeeper or manager approves; accountants post nothing. Exact semantics: a period is a calendar month of the recorded rent ledger, installation-wide; a posting belongs to the month of its date (a charge’s due date, a receipt’s received date, a charge reduction’s property-local day of recording). Only a month that has ended in the office time zone (PORT-001) can be signed off or closed, and only by the owner or an all-portfolio bookkeeper (ROLE-001). The month-end checklist has three sign-offs, each kept with who signed, when and an optional note: every receipt for the month is recorded; recorded receipts agree with the bank deposits, labeled as checked by staff because Terrace has not matched a bank statement (ACCT-006 adds statement matching and makes this item a matched reconciliation before it ships); and open receivables and charge reductions are reviewed. The exception queue lists the month’s charges still unpaid and its pending close corrections; a month closes only with all three sign-offs and no pending correction. A close is a numbered version that keeps a statement of every posting dated in the month, totaled per currency (charges, receipts, reductions and net change, never converted); while a month has a close that is not superseded, the database refuses any charge due or receipt received in it, and any ACCT-009 fee line or override for it (409 `period_closed`). The owner or a bookkeeper reopens a closed month with a reason: that version is marked superseded with the reason, who reopened it and when, and is never edited or deleted; new sign-offs are needed and the next close is the next version, shown beside the earlier ones with the entries added and removed since the version before (earlier entries stay as recorded). A close correction is a missed charge or a missed receipt in an ended month, prepared by an accountant, bookkeeper or portfolio manager with a reason; it posts nothing until another bookkeeper, portfolio manager or the owner approves the exact prepared entry (ROLE-003: the preparer never approves, except “self-approved: no second person”), and approval is refused while its month is closed. A month’s statement of record is its close version: today’s ledger, owner and allocation statements are generated from the live ledger, and ACCT-012 published owner statements mark those covering a reopened month superseded before they ship; ACCT-001 double-entry postings and ACCT-007 vendor bills are refused in closed months the same way before they ship. Sign-offs, closes, reopenings and corrections are history rows (SAFE-002), and close statement downloads are recorded reads. **Acceptance evidence:** Close a reconciled month, attempt a backdated posting, approve a period reopening and adjustment, then compare old/new statements with the reopening reason and unchanged original entries. An accountant’s close correction stays a proposal until an authorized person approves it. SAFE-002 applies before this ships: each close, lock and controlled reopening is a history row with its approver and reason.

- **ACCT-012 — Publish complete owner statements.** Produce owner/property statements showing opening cash, income, expenses, management fees, deposits separately, reserves, contributions, distributions, liabilities and closing cash. Drill to bills, settlement and bank reconciliation; publish corrected versions explicitly and deliver on schedule. Each statement itemizes the management fee, repairs and other expenses, reserve movement and net to owner, and is delivered with its source receipts and bills attached. **Acceptance evidence:** Publish a monthly owner statement with rent, a paid bill and distribution, reconcile its closing cash to books/bank and download the source invoice from the owner portal. Confirm the delivered statement shows the management fee, a repair, other expenses, the reserve and net to owner, and carries the receipt and invoice attachments for its lines. PORT-003 applies before this ships: income, expenses, fees and reserve shares on each side of a dated ownership transfer appear on the seller’s and the buyer’s statements respectively. REPORT-007 applies before this ships: statement actuals source its rent, payable, fee, reserve and distribution comparisons, keeping forecasts distinct.

- **ACCT-013 — Report cash and accrual financials.** Exact implemented basis timing, opening treatment, tax liabilities, inclusive dates, oldest-first aging and unassigned entity semantics are stated in [the financial-report guide](docs/financial-reports.md); REPORT-006 inherits those rules. Offer cash- and accrual-basis income statements, balance sheet, trial balance, general ledger, receivables and payables aging and cash flow by property, owner and entity. Every total drills to postings; changing basis never modifies the underlying ledger. **Acceptance evidence:** Record earned unpaid rent and an unpaid bill, compare cash and accrual P&L and balance sheet, and drill each difference to its original transaction.

- **ACCT-014 — Prepare and file owner and vendor 1099s.** Collect restricted W-9/TIN information, validate payer/payee classifications and thresholds for the applicable tax year, reconcile reportable payments, including migrated year-to-date balance-forwards (MOVE-010) so a mid-year switch files one form per payee for the whole year, and support corrected forms. Integrate Nelco for human-reviewed 1099-MISC/NEC e-filing, recipient delivery and acceptance/rejection tracking; tax advice remains with the buyer’s accountant. The prior tax year’s payee set, reportable totals and exceptions are complete and ready for accountant review in the first week of January, before the year’s earliest filing deadline. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare owner/vendor forms from reconciled payments, correct an invalid TIN, approve a Nelco submission and process accepted/rejected/corrected outcomes without duplicate filings. On the first business day of January show the prior year’s owner and vendor 1099 data complete, reconciled to payments, with exceptions listed.

- **ACCT-015 — Sync QuickBooks Online without losing trust truth.** Connect QuickBooks Online via authorized OAuth, map accounts, tax codes and entities and sync approved journals/bills/payments with stable identities and conflict reports. Terrace retains residential beneficiary/deposit detail; an aggregate accounting export never counts as subledger reconciliation. **Acceptance evidence:** Sync a property close to a QuickBooks sandbox, replay it, change an account mapping and reconcile resulting totals and a visible conflict back to Terrace’s owner/deposit subledgers.

- **ACCT-016 — Account for utility recoveries and ancillary income.** Allocate actual utility bills, RUBS/submeter readings and lease-authorized reimbursements with reviewed formulas, caps and source invoices; handle sales/use tax where applicable through configured accountant-reviewed rules. Include parking, storage and other permitted charges in resident and owner books. Exact semantics: a utility bill (water, sewer, trash, gas or electric) is recorded per property with its vendor, source invoice reference, service period, resident due date, amount, recoverable share (default 100%, half up to the cent), formula and optional per-lease cap, by the owner, a portfolio manager or a bookkeeper. Its recoverable amount is split over everyone who occupied the property’s units in the service period, inclusive of both days: occupant-days (the primary tenant plus co-tenants and occupants, each for the days they were on the lease; guarantors and contacts do not count), bedroom-days (a studio counts as one bedroom), unit-days, or submeter reading × days; under the unit-weighted formulas a unit’s vacant days take their share. Each party’s share is the floor of its part, with remainder cents to the largest basis. A lease is charged its share only when a recorded clause of that lease authorizes recovery of that utility, and at most the cap; vacancy, unauthorized leases and capped excess stay unrecovered (the owner’s cost).
