The allocation is reviewed: another person with approval authority approves the exact allocation shown (ROLE-003 independence; a changed allocation must be reviewed again), and approval posts one charge per charged lease, referenced by invoice and unit and describing the invoice, period, formula and basis, so the posted charges total the approved recoverable amount. Parking, storage and other permitted charges post one-off to a lease, and parking and utility charges also recur through PAY-001 terms. A tax rule names a property, a charge kind (utility, parking, storage or other), a rate and its start; it applies only once an accountant or the owner has reviewed it, and the reviewed rule in force on a charge’s due date adds a separate tax charge, half up to the cent, naming the rule. Terrace computes tax as configured and files or remits nothing. Every such charge is in the resident’s ledger; receipts on recoveries and ancillary charges are owner income in PORT-003 allocation and ACCT-009 fees, and receipts on tax charges never are. ACCT-007 records the utility bill as the owner’s payable and ACCT-012 owner statements show the bill beside its recoveries, and PORT-007 attaches the source invoice document, before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Allocate one water invoice by a reviewed occupancy formula, post parking and taxable ancillary charges and verify source-linked tenant allocations equal the approved recoverable total.

- **ACCT-017 — Print mail and register trust checks.** Print MICR checks on blank check stock from the paying operating, trust or deposit bank account (routing, account and check number in E-13B MICR), or send them through Lob’s check print-and-mail service with tracking, for vendor bills, owner distributions and deposit or credit refunds. Each bank account keeps an unbroken check-number register in which every number is issued, voided or spoiled, never skipped or reused, and a duplicate number is refused. A void reverses the payment and reopens the payable or refund; a reissue needs new approval and a new number. Checks outstanding past the owner-set stale date (default 180 days) create a follow-up and, if unclaimed, an unclaimed-property review. Positive-pay issue files export in the bank’s format with acknowledgments recorded, and cleared checks match from the bank feed (ACCT-006). **Acceptance evidence:** Print a deposit-refund check from the deposit bank account and a vendor check batch from the operating trust account, void and reissue one check with new approval, refuse a duplicate check number and export positive-pay for the batch; clear one check against the bank feed and leave one outstanding past its stale date with a follow-up.

- **ACCT-018 — Originate trust ACH payments through NACHA files.** Terrace executes approved owner distributions (ACCT-010), vendor payments (ACCT-008) and ACH refunds (PAY-009, ACCT-004) over a named outbound rail chosen per bank account. **Bank file rail (default):** the manager’s own bank is the originating bank. For each approved batch Terrace generates one NACHA-format file per paying operating, trust or deposit bank account, never mixing accounts: PPD entries for individual payees, CCD entries with a remittance addenda record for business payees; immediate destination and origin, company ID, company entry description and file ID modifier from the bank’s ACH settings; a balanced offset entry to the paying account or an unbalanced file, per the bank setting; 94-character records blocked to multiples of ten; batch and file control records with entry and addenda counts, entry hash and debit and credit totals; and an effective entry date from the approved pay date and the bank’s cutoff. File, batch and trace numbers derive from the approved batch, so regenerating returns the same file and never a second batch. The person who uploads the file to the bank portal, or the configured bank SFTP transmission, records the bank’s upload or confirmation reference; entries stay `transmitted`, not `settled`, until the bank feed shows them. **Provider API rail (optional):** Modern Treasury payment orders on the manager’s connected bank account for same-day or next-day ACH, under the same one-account-per-batch, idempotency and approval rules, with provider webhooks for sent, returned and reversed states. **Payees:** a new or changed payee bank account is verified by a zero-dollar prenote or provider micro-deposits (or Plaid Auth when the payee links an account) before its first live entry, and a bank-detail change follows ROLE-003 independent verification. **Returns and notifications of change:** Terrace imports the bank’s ACH return and notification-of-change (NOC) files, or the provider’s webhooks. A return (R01, R02, R03, R04 and the other R codes) reverses the entry, reopens the payable, distribution or refund for new approval and suspends the payee method. A NOC (C01 to C07) proposes the corrected account, routing or account-type detail, which is held for ROLE-003 independent verification before use, and its correction deadline is tracked. Every payee gets a remittance notice by email and portal listing the bills, distribution statement or refund the entry pays. Settled entries clear against the bank feed (ACCT-005) and three-way reconciliation (ACCT-006) by trace number, batch total or entry amount. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: only the owner and roles the capability table grants payment preparation reach these doors, within their portfolios; leasing staff, maintenance coordinators, accountants and members are refused (403). SAFE-001 applies before this ships: adding or changing a payee bank account or applying a notification of change needs the fresh email-link proof as well as ROLE-003’s independent verification. **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a 90-owner distribution drawn on one trust account and a vendor batch drawn on a second trust account. Generate one NACHA file per account, pass both through a NACHA format validator (record lengths, blocking, batch and file control totals, entry hash), and match each entry's amount and destination to the approved batch exactly. Regenerate both and get the same file IDs and trace numbers with no second batch. Record the bank upload reference. Send a prenote for a new vendor and hold its first live payment until the prenote window passes. Import an R01 return on one owner's entry and a C01 NOC on another: the returned distribution reopens for new approval, the NOC's account change is held for independent verification, and the settled entries clear against imported bank-feed lines in the three-way reconciliation. Pay one vendor through the Modern Treasury sandbox and process its return webhook once. Leasing staff attempting this payout are refused (403), and a bookkeeper outside the paying property’s portfolios gets 404. A payee bank change without a fresh email-link proof is refused (403). SAFE-002 applies before this ships: each generated file, upload reference and bank instruction is a history row with its approver.

### Resident owner and vendor service portals

- **PORTAL-001 — Give residents a complete account portal.** Residents see current and future charges, settled/pending payments, deposits, lease documents, receipts and household obligations, can authorize/pay rent and update allowed contact preferences. Accessible responsive views keep private guarantor, screening and other household data protected. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). SAFE-001 applies before this ships: a staff change to a resident’s bank details needs the fresh email-link proof. **Acceptance evidence:** Sign in as a resident with two leases, inspect an itemized balance, pay rent, download a receipt and update contact preferences; direct access to an unrelated household is denied. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors. A staff bank-detail change without a fresh email-link proof is refused (403).

- **PORTAL-002 — Give owners their financial and property portal.** Owners see owned-property occupancy, rent, maintenance approvals, reserves, statements, source bills, distribution status and documents for authorized ownership periods. They can contribute funds, approve requested spend and communicate without gaining resident screening or other owners’ records. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). SAFE-001 applies before this ships: a staff change to an owner’s distribution bank details needs the fresh email-link proof. **Acceptance evidence:** Joint owners inspect different ownership periods, approve an over-limit repair, contribute funds and download a statement/invoice; access another owner’s report and screening file is denied. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors. A staff bank-detail change without a fresh email-link proof is refused (403).

- **PORTAL-003 — Give vendors a work and invoice portal.** Vendors accept/decline assigned work, verify qualifications, propose appointments, submit estimates, completion photos and invoices and see their payment status. Access codes and resident contact details are limited to approved jobs and time windows. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). SAFE-001 applies before this ships: a staff change to a vendor’s bank details needs the fresh email-link proof. **Acceptance evidence:** Invite a plumber to one job, accept an appointment, upload evidence/invoice and read payment state; after reassignment revoke the access details and deny every other vendor job. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors. A staff bank-detail change without a fresh email-link proof is refused (403).

- **PORTAL-004 — Receive resident maintenance requests.** Residents report unit issues with photos/video, category, access consent, pets, preferred times and urgency from web or mobile. Give a tracking number, safe acknowledgment and visible status; duplicate reports can be linked without losing each resident’s original concern. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a leaking-tap request with photo and access restrictions, add another household report and follow the tracking link through scheduled work and resident-confirmed resolution. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors. WORK-001 applies before this ships: a resident’s safety or emergency report opens the same WORK-001 case, shows the resident the approved guidance version and alerts on call as staff intake does.

- **PORTAL-005 — Deliver two-way email and SMS.** Use Resend for authorized email and Twilio for SMS with verified sender setup, consent, opt-out and quiet-hours handling. Route replies to the right property/household/job, retain delivery/failure evidence and prevent duplicate messages; unsent drafts remain visibly unsent. Recipients without email or SMS consent, and notices whose pack requires mail, use PORTAL-009 postal delivery in the same thread. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a repair message, deliver email/SMS at provider boundaries, receive a reply and opt-out, replay callbacks and show failed delivery and suppressed future SMS in the shared thread. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors. SAFE-005 applies before this ships: its sent and received messages with their delivery records appear in the readable export and come back with a restore into a fresh installation. DEMO-001 applies before this ships: its demo flow retains the effect guard and adds a public-door no-egress assertion; no real payment, message or webhook is sent from a demo. WORK-001 applies before this ships: its SMS/voice door pages the on-call person and backup of an open emergency with timed automatic escalation, records each provider outcome without claiming a person was reached, and keeps the email alert.

- **PORTAL-006 — Keep shared threads and notices accountable.** Provide searchable staff/resident/owner/vendor conversations, assignments, internal notes, attachments, unread state and service deadlines. Bulk announcements scope recipients by property and retain each result; legal notices require exact human approval and named service evidence recorded through PORTAL-009 or the delivering provider. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). Search returns only threads and notices on tenancies in the searcher’s portfolios. **Acceptance evidence:** Assign a resident conversation, add a private note, broadcast a water shutoff to one building and inspect delivered/failed recipients; verify the resident cannot see the note or another building’s messages. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors. A search by a scoped staff user returns nothing from another portfolio. SAFE-005 applies before this ships: its threads, notices and their service records appear in the readable export and come back with a restore into a fresh installation.

- **PORTAL-007 — Track requests documents and approvals to completion.** Owners and residents sign, upload requested documents, acknowledge permitted notices and approve quotes through scoped expiring links. Staff see missing items, reminders, expiry and who completed each action; an opened email never substitutes for approval or signature. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). **Acceptance evidence:** Request insurance evidence and owner quote approval, expire one link and complete a replacement; show reminders stop only after validated completion and the exact signer/approver is recorded. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors.

- **PORTAL-008 — Support mobile and accessible everyday work.** Provide WCAG 2.2 AA journeys at desktop and phone sizes, keyboard/screen-reader access, clear validation and safe resume after connectivity loss. Native iOS/Android apps support resident payments/requests and staff field work with permissioned push notifications and device session revocation. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). **Acceptance evidence:** Use 1440- and 390-pixel screens and assistive navigation to pay, submit a request and approve work; suspend/resume native sessions and revoke a lost device without exposing cached private data. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors.

- **PORTAL-009 — Print mail and record service of notices.** Merge approved letters and notices (pay-or-quit, lease violation, entry, nonrenewal, deposit disposition, owner letters) into a batch PDF for office printing, or send them through Lob with first-class, certified and certified return-receipt options. Retain the exact approved PDF, provider IDs, USPS tracking numbers and delivery events (mailed, in transit, delivered, returned). Staff record physical service (posted on the door, hand-delivered, mailed by the office with a certified tracking number) with server, date and time, method and photo. Deadlines from the PORT-008 pack run from the recorded service or mailing date, including any mailing extension the pack declares; a draft or a printed page never counts as service. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). **Acceptance evidence:** Approve a Florida deposit-claim notice and send it certified through the Lob test boundary, or record a certified tracking number for office mail; show the 30-day deadline met against the mailing date and a late mailing flagged as missed; serve a pay-or-quit notice by posting with recorded photo and server; return one mailed letter as undeliverable and see a follow-up. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors. SAFE-002 applies before this ships: each notice merged, mailed and recorded as served is a history row with its source.

- **PORTAL-010 — Tell owners what was fixed, at what cost, with photos.** When a repair on an owner’s property is confirmed complete by the resident, or closed by authorized staff with a recorded reason (WORK-008), the owner for that ownership period receives a notice by email and in the owner portal naming the unit and the repair, the final matched cost (WORK-009) and the actual completion photos, and pointing to the statement period in which the cost appears (ACCT-012). A job that is only vendor-closed, or whose resident has reported it unresolved, produces no “fixed” notice; owners of other properties and prior ownership periods receive nothing; a replay never sends a second notice and a failed delivery creates a follow-up. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: its staff screens and doors check the capability table and portfolio scope (out of scope 404, out of role 403). **Acceptance evidence:** Complete a repair as a vendor and have the resident report it still leaking: no owner notice is sent. After a return visit and resident confirmation, show one owner email and portal notice with the matched cost and two completion photos, find the same job and cost on that month’s owner statement, replay the event for no second notice, bounce the email for a follow-up, and show a second owner and a former owner of the property receive nothing. A staff user outside the property’s portfolios gets 404, and one whose ROLE-001 role lacks the action gets 403, on this clause’s staff screens and doors.

### Maintenance from request to reconciled bill

- **WORK-001 — Triage safety and emergency requests.** Classify intake by property, asset, habitability risk and emergency policy, give approved safe guidance and alert the human on-call service with acknowledged escalation. Tell residents when to call 911 or utilities for immediate danger; no agent diagnoses safety or closes an emergency by inference. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a gas-smell request outside office hours, show approved emergency guidance and escalate to an acknowledged human; an unanswered alert remains urgent and open. REPORT-004 applies before this ships: the service report counts open emergencies and their age until a human acknowledges and resolves them. Exact semantics (19 October 2026, ct ruling 16:58Z): staff (owner, portfolio manager, maintenance coordinator in the property’s portfolios) record a safety report on a tenancy placed on a unit, with the risk (gas, fire, electric, water, habitability, other), how it arrived (phone, email, in person, observed by staff), who reported it, what was reported, an optional in-service asset, the reported-at instant (an ISO time with a UTC offset, never in the future; blank is now) and their own explicit emergency yes/no; gas, fire and electrical hazards, and any risk whose current guidance is marked immediate danger, are recorded only as emergencies. The owner or a portfolio manager over every portfolio approves numbered guidance versions per risk; immediate-danger guidance must carry a when-to-call instruction naming 911 (and the utility where it applies); each case keeps the exact text of the version it was given, and a risk with no approved guidance records that none was given. The owner or a portfolio manager in scope names one on-call person and one backup per portfolio (an active owner, or staff whose role may acknowledge emergencies there); the latest assignment applies to new cases. Terrace keeps no office hours: on call applies at every hour. Recording an emergency emails the on-call person a sign-in link to the case with no case details through the installation’s mail provider, and the case history records the provider’s own outcome (accepted by the mail provider, failed, uncertain, not sent because development or demo mail is suppressed, or not sent because no provider is configured); “accepted” never claims a person was reached. A portfolio with no on-call person records the case and says no alert was sent. Escalation is a recorded human action by those staff, with a reason, re-sending the alert to the backup or the on-call person; nothing escalates on a timer. Only the on-call person or backup named on the case acknowledges it, in Terrace, saying what they are doing; an acknowledged case stays open. Only the owner or a portfolio manager resolves, after acknowledgement, with field-work evidence and the resident’s follow-up, labeled “resident follow-up recorded by staff; Terrace did not contact the resident”. Members and preparers cannot record, acknowledge or resolve, and no agent or automatic path classifies or closes a case. REPORT-004 counts each emergency in scope as open, with its age in hours (one decimal) from the reported-at instant, until it is resolved. Case records are erased with their tenancy as maintenance jobs are (SAFE-004) and are in the backup and readable export (SAFE-005). Not yet: SMS/voice paging of on-call and backup with timed automatic escalation (PORTAL-005), and resident self-report (PORTAL-004).

- **WORK-002 — Maintain property asset and warranty history.** Track installed equipment, model/serial, location, service history, warranties, manuals and replacement plans. Link requests and costs to assets, flag warranty coverage and keep old assets after replacement for historical cost and failure analysis. Exact semantics: an asset is recorded under a tenancy and, when that tenancy is on a unit (PORT-002), under the unit too, so it shows and takes repairs on every tenancy of that unit; erasing the tenancy it was recorded under erases it. Its manual is recorded as a link or the place it is kept; PORT-007 adds stored manual files. A replacement is recorded as a new asset installed on the replacement date; the old asset is marked replaced on that date, linked both ways, and keeps its service history. A repair request (a maintenance job) links to one in-service asset of the same tenancy; a replaced asset takes no new requests. A linked repair is attributed to the warranty when its due date falls on or after the installed date and on or before the warranty end (inclusive), otherwise to the property owner; Terrace flags coverage and never files or confirms a warranty claim. Costs are approved estimates in the tenancy’s currency (a prepared, unapproved job is listed but not counted); WORK-009 links matched invoices and REPORT-004 the failure analytics, and PORTAL-004 resident requests inherit the asset link before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Add an HVAC asset and warranty, open a repair, replace the asset and inspect both service histories with warranty and owner-cost attribution.

- **WORK-003 — Estimate work and obtain owner approval.** Collect comparable vendor quotes, scope, availability, tax and proposed spend against owner limits and property budgets. A manager approves within authority; over-limit work needs the owner’s exact approval. Scope, vendor or price changes reopen authorization. Exact semantics: any operator who prepares work records quotes on a job (a directory vendor or a named unlisted one, quoted scope, available-from date, price before tax and tax, in the job’s currency) and compares them by total, price plus tax, lowest first; selecting a quote makes its vendor, scope and total the job’s terms. An owner or admin records the property owner’s per-job spending limit and optional yearly maintenance budget, labeled “recorded by staff for the owner”, for the property when the tenancy is on a unit (PORT-002), otherwise for the tenancy. With no limit recorded a manager’s approval stands for any amount. A job needs the owner’s decision when its estimate is above the limit, or when the estimates of approved and handed-off jobs in the same scope due in the same calendar year as this job, plus this estimate, are above the budget. Until the owner portal exists (PORTAL-002), an owner or admin records that decision (approved or declined) with its source (email, document or call) and where it is recorded, labeled “recorded by staff for the owner”; Terrace never claims it asked or notified the owner, and members and agents cannot record it. The decision covers the exact terms of one job version (title, scope, vendor, due date, estimate and quote, by SHA-256); approval of a job that needs it requires an approved decision on those exact terms, and the approval snapshot and handoff packet name it. Any change of scope, title, estimate, due date or selected quote, before or after approval, makes a new version that is prepared again (WORK-004 qualification is rechecked): the earlier approval and owner decision no longer apply, the packet cannot be downloaded and the handoff cannot be recorded until the new terms are approved. PORTAL-002 makes owners decide in the portal, and WORK-005, WORK-006, WORK-009 and ROLE-003’s per-person approval limits inherit these terms before they ship (ROLE-001 portfolio managers approve within the owner’s limit and budget recorded here). **Acceptance evidence:** Compare two repair quotes, request an owner decision above the spending limit, then change the approved scope and verify dispatch remains blocked until the new terms are approved.

- **WORK-004 — Qualify and assign vendors.** Maintain vendor specialties, service areas, W-9 status, insurance/license expirations, availability, rates and preferred/blocked status. Assign only qualified vendors for the job and expose qualification exceptions to authorized staff. Exact semantics: a vendor qualifies for a job when it is in the directory and not blocked, lists the job’s trade as a specialty, names a service area (a ZIP code or city) that appears as a whole word in the property address, has a received W-9, and has insurance, and any recorded license, expiring on or after the job’s due date. The W-9 status, insurance and license dates are what a manager records; Terrace does not verify them with the vendor, insurer or licensing board. Qualification is checked when work is prepared or reassigned and again at approval and at the recorded handoff, against the vendor’s current record. Work assigned to an unqualified or unlisted vendor is prepared and shown with its issues but held: approval and handoff are refused until an owner or admin records a documented exception (a reason, kept unedited) for exactly those issues; a changed issue needs a new exception. Every operator sees holds, exceptions and assignment history on Inspections & maintenance. Only prepared, unapproved work is reassigned. Availability is recorded as text; WORK-005 adds booked appointments, and WORK-006, PORTAL-003 and every later dispatch door inherit the same qualification hold before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Select a plumber by area and insurance status, expire their coverage and attempt reassignment; verify qualification hold and a documented human exception rather than silent dispatch.

- **WORK-005 — Book appointments and resident access.** Coordinate vendor availability with resident permission, entry notice, keys/access windows and staff calendars. Confirm both parties, handle cancellations/no-shows, timezones and reassignment, and record the next appointment instead of treating a due date as a booking. The resident receives an arrival-window message by SMS or email with a simple reply (for example Y) that confirms the visit, and the reply is routed to the appointment. Current staff-recorded slice (ct 19 October 12:55Z): after approval of the current WORK-003 terms, a portfolio manager or maintenance coordinator (or the owner) records an arrival window inside the resident’s permitted access window, vendor availability, permission/restrictions, externally served entry-notice or documented exception reference and time, key/access instructions and the responsible staff calendar. Times carry explicit offsets matching the property’s IANA zone; skipped daylight-saving times and wrong seasonal offsets are refused, and either repeated autumn time can be selected by offset. Historical external appointments may be backfilled; all recording and confirmation timestamps remain the actual entry time in Terrace. Active proposed and confirmed windows reserve staff, vendor and unit calendars, and overlaps are refused atomically without revealing another property’s details. Both parties’ confirmations are recorded separately from external evidence, labeled “confirmed by staff, resident not contacted by Terrace”; no response stays unconfirmed. Cancellation/no-show, superseded windows, new permission, replies and reassignment are kept in history. Rescheduling makes a new appointment needing both confirmations; a vendor reassignment after cancellation/no-show makes a pending work version requiring fresh spend approval and any required exact owner decision before booking or handoff. WORK-004 qualification is rechecked at booking and confirmation. REPORT-004 measures actual preparation-to-first-dual-confirmation entry time, even if later canceled or rescheduled. Terrace sends no notice or arrival-window message and receives no resident reply in this slice: PORTAL-005 supplies email/SMS and Y-reply routing and notifications, PORTAL-003 supplies vendor-portal cancellation; WORK-005 stays partial with those gaps. **Acceptance evidence:** Book a repair, receive resident confirmation, cancel from the vendor portal and reschedule with a new permitted access window; notify both parties and preserve appointment history. Send an arrival-window text, reply Y and show the appointment confirmed by that reply; an unanswered window stays unconfirmed. REPORT-004 applies before this ships: the service report shows booking time from preparation to the first confirmed appointment.

- **WORK-006 — Dispatch and track technician progress.** Deliver approved work orders to vendors or in-house technicians with task checklist, scope, authorized spend, permitted contacts and due/appointment times. Capture acceptance, en route, started, blocked, parts needed and completion states, with human escalation for missed service commitments.  Exact semantics: the approved checklist (one task per line, up to 20) and scope, authorized spend, due date and approving staff contact are frozen in the work approval. An explicit staff send dispatches them through the installation mail provider to the assigned vendor or in-house technician mailbox, with the current approval’s recorded arrival window when one exists. No resident contact or key instructions are added to that packet. Provider acceptance, rejection, suppressed/unconfigured mail and uncertain outcomes are labeled as such; acceptance never claims delivery or a technician’s reply. One durable claim per approval prevents concurrent/replayed sends; after an uncertain attempt staff reconcile with the provider before arranging another handoff. Staff record sourced technician replies (accepted, en route, started, blocked, parts needed, completed) and checked approved tasks; completion requires the whole checklist, and never resolves the resident issue without WORK-008’s separate check. A missed arrival window or past property-local due date stays visibly escalated until the issue is resolved or closed; staff record whom they contacted and the next action. WORK-005 no-show/reassignment reopens exact approval, keeps the first dispatch and replies, and requires fresh approval before sending the replacement. PORTAL-003 inherits direct vendor responses; WORK-007 inherits field evidence; their absent doors are not claimed by staff-recorded progress. Dispatch snapshots and replies inherit SAFE-002 history, SAFE-004 work-evidence retention/erasure and SAFE-005 export/restore before shipping. **Acceptance evidence:** Dispatch an approved order, receive vendor acceptance and a parts hold, miss its appointment and reassign it; inspect notifications, state history and a still-open resident issue.

- **WORK-007 — Capture field labor materials and completion evidence.** Technicians record labor/time, parts, notes, before/after photos/video, resident access outcome and checklist completion on mobile. Support offline capture with conflict review and original evidence provenance; a closed vendor status alone cannot prove repair. Current conservative direct-capture semantics pending ct approval: a signed-in owner or portfolio manager records their own technician evidence, attributed to that operator; this introduces no vendor authentication or grant. Private device drafts keep only explicitly consented capture fields and original files, never credentials, and sync only on a person’s explicit request. Successful sync or explicit device deletion removes the draft. Changed field scope reopens exact work approval, retains old approvals/dispatch/evidence, and requires fresh authorization and handoff before manual reconciliation of the original draft. Direct reports require every current approved task, whole-minute labor (zero allowed), explicit materials/none, notes, access outcome and distinct before/after originals (photo or video); client replay cannot create another completion. They leave the resident resolution check open. Staff-recorded completion attachments currently retain whole-minute labor time (zero allowed), parts/material notes (explicit none when absent), access outcome, every approved checklist task and distinct before/after inspection originals with hashes, dates and the exact approval/scope snapshot. They are labeled sourced staff records, never direct technician submissions, and do not resolve the resident issue. A changed job version or approval requires staff to reload and review the evidence against the current work before submission. SAFE-002 history, SAFE-004 work-evidence retention/erasure and SAFE-005 backup/restore apply to these attachments. **Acceptance evidence:** Lose connectivity during work, capture time and photos, reconnect with a conflicting scope change and reconcile the conflict before submitting complete evidence for review.

- **WORK-008 — Verify repair with the resident.** Ask the resident whether the original issue is resolved after evidence submission, distinguish no response from confirmation and reopen recurring or incomplete work. Track warranty callbacks, satisfaction and unresolved safety concerns; only authorized staff can close without resident confirmation with a recorded reason. Exact semantics: after the external handoff, any operator records the vendor’s completion report (completed date, what the vendor reports and where their evidence is), labeled as recorded by staff, because there is no vendor portal yet (PORTAL-003). The work then awaits the resident’s check, and staff record the resident’s answer to whether the original issue is resolved: “confirmed” counts only labeled “confirmed by staff, resident not contacted by Terrace”, “not resolved” (with what is still wrong) and “no response” carry the same “recorded by staff, resident not contacted by Terrace” wording, and Terrace never claims it asked the resident (PORTAL-005 delivers the question before it ships). No response keeps the work open and is never a confirmation. Not resolved reopens the work; a report that a resolved or closed issue recurred reopens it too. A reopened job takes a return visit: a further completion report that is a callback to the vendor, marked warranty (no charge) or billable, and then a new check. A confirmation may record satisfaction from 1 to 5; any answer may record a safety concern, which stays listed as unresolved until a later confirmation on the same job. Only an owner or admin closes open completed work without the resident’s confirmation, with a recorded reason. Reports, answers and closures are append-only, so every attempt and the final resolution stay on the job. PORTAL-003 (vendor submission), PORTAL-004 (resident status), PORTAL-005 (asking by message), PORTAL-010 (owner notice) and REPORT-004 (callback and satisfaction analytics) build on these records before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Vendor submits completion, resident reports the tap still leaks and the job reopens; after a return visit obtain confirmation and retain both attempts and the final resolution.

- **WORK-009 — Match invoice work and owner charge.** Extract invoice lines with source locations, match vendor, approved estimate, labor/materials, completion and duplicate history, then propose an owner/property allocation. Differences, unapproved extras and incomplete work hold the bill; human approval posts it and links the later settlement. **Acceptance evidence:** Submit a completed repair invoice exceeding its quote, flag the unmatched line, approve a corrected invoice and trace work, payable, payment and owner statement without double entry. REPORT-004 applies before this ships: the service report’s asset cost and budget variance use the matched invoice amount once a job’s invoice is approved, labeled as invoiced.

- **WORK-010 — Schedule preventive and recurring maintenance.** Generate dated work from asset intervals, seasonal tasks and inspection findings, with budgets, owner permissions, vendor schedules and recurrence history. Track missed occurrences and equipment changes without creating duplicate work orders on scheduler replay. Exact semantics: a schedule belongs to a tenancy, names a directory vendor (WORK-004 qualification applies to every order), a trade, a budget per occurrence in the tenancy’s currency, an interval of 1 to 60 months from its first due date (the same day of the month, or the month’s last day when shorter; a seasonal task is an annual schedule anchored in its season’s month) and 0 to 90 lead days, and may follow an asset (WORK-002) or come from a completed inspection’s finding. A scheduler run, started by an owner or admin, creates one pending order for the budget for each occurrence whose effective due date (its deferred date, if deferred) is on or before the property-local today plus the lead days; a unique occurrence key means a replayed or concurrent run never creates a second order. An order is work an owner or admin must approve, as for any maintenance. An occurrence can be deferred, with a reason, only before it has an order. An occurrence past its effective due date whose order has not been handed off is listed as overdue. When a followed asset is replaced the schedule follows the replacement, and each occurrence keeps the asset it was ordered for. OPS-003 adds an unattended timed run, and WORK-005 vendor calendars, before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule annual HVAC service and quarterly safety work, replay a scheduler run, defer one occurrence and replace an asset; inspect exactly one order per due occurrence and an explicit overdue exception.

- **WORK-011 — Complete mobile move-in and move-out inspections.** Use configurable room/asset checklists, dated original photos/video, notes, readings and resident acknowledgment. Current conservative semantics pending ct approval: new structured capture/configuration/acknowledgement/proposal doors are owner or portfolio-manager only; no new portal grant or resident authentication is introduced. Offline evidence is an explicit-consent private device draft, never an automatically submitted report; successful synchronization deletes the device draft, and a separate explicit control deletes it without sending. A changed checklist requires manual review and reconciliation, retaining the original values in the synchronized record. Resident acknowledgement is entered by staff with the resident’s words and a source, never presented as a resident signature or a Terrace contact. Entry/exit comparisons use stable room/asset keys and retain original hashes. Every proposal is held for human review; unsupported damage cannot be approved, and no inspection decision posts money, creates work or sends a message. Existing ROLE-003 independence applies to approval (including its labeled sole-operator exception). Compare entry and exit condition side by side, retain disagreements and propose evidenced work or deposit deductions for a person to approve. **Acceptance evidence:** Inspect on a phone offline, sync photos, compare move-out damage to the entry record and reject an unsupported deduction while retaining the resident’s disputed finding.

- **WORK-012 — Integrate HappyCo inspection evidence.** Connect authorized HappyCo accounts, map properties/units and import inspection findings, media, timestamps and author identity through supported interfaces or reviewed provider exports. Preserve source IDs and compare versions; a vendor closed status does not overwrite resident resolution. **Acceptance evidence:** Bring a HappyCo inspection into the correct unit, replay it and update one finding, then create approved repair work with original media/provenance and a visible unmapped-unit exception.

- **WORK-013 — Run make-ready and turnover boards.** From notice/vacancy create dependent inspection, deposit, cleaning, repair, utility and listing tasks with owners, durations, quotes and target ready date. Show blockers and vacancy-day impact; a unit becomes ready only after authorized completion checks, not merely after task submission. Exact semantics: an owner or admin opens a make-ready board for a unit (PORT-002) from a move-out date, on notice or after vacancy, when no lease occupies the unit the day after; it creates the standard tasks: move-out inspection and utility transfer first, deposit disposition and repairs after the inspection, cleaning after repairs and the listing after cleaning, each with an assignee, a duration in whole days, an optional delay and quote. A task starts the day after its last dependency ends (the first tasks the day after move-out) plus its delay; the planned ready date is the day after the last task ends, and vacancy days count from the day after move-out to it. Any operator submits a task; only an owner or admin checks it, and only after the tasks it depends on are checked; a task whose dependencies are unchecked is shown as blocked. Publishing needs every task checked and sets the unit’s available date to the later of the planned ready date and the day after the last check, in the property’s time zone. The deposit task prepares a decision only (ACCT-004 disposes the money) and the listing task prepares one (LEASE-001 publishes it); PORT-006 move-out opens the board automatically before it ships. **Acceptance evidence:** Move out a resident, delay a repair dependent on inspection, revise the ready date and show cleaning/listing effects; complete checks and publish the true available date.

- **WORK-014 — Control maintenance budgets inventory and chargebacks.** Track property/asset spend versus approved operating/capital budgets, in-house stock use and purchasing, and authorized resident/owner/insurance chargebacks. Record approvals and tax treatment so a cost is never recovered twice or assigned to the wrong beneficiary. **Acceptance evidence:** Consume a stocked part on a repair, cross a budget limit, propose a resident chargeback and approve one allocation; reconcile stock, payable, receivable and owner cost.

### Reports and portfolio performance

- **REPORT-001 — Explain the complete rent roll.** Report every unit, resident, lease dates, market/contract rent, concessions, recurring charges, deposit obligations and occupancy state as of a chosen date, including vacant and future leases. Totals drill to effective terms and export to CSV/XLSX/PDF. A collection view of the same rent roll for a period shows, per unit and in total, rent collected against rent billed, the share of leases paid in full and each lease’s payment state (paid by ACH, card or cash, partial or unpaid) from settled receipts, with pending funds shown separately. Exact semantics: the rent roll lists every unit (PORT-002) and every lease without a unit record that is in effect, as of the chosen date in the property’s calendar. A unit is occupied when a lease covers that day (its start to its move-out day or end date), otherwise vacant, naming any future lease. Contract rent on the day is the rent of the lease period covering it: a renewal’s earlier terms until that period ends, then the renewed rent (TER-003). Market rent is the unit’s recorded market rent. Recurring charges and concessions are the PAY-001 terms in effect that day, linked by term to the lease they drill to. Totals count units, occupied and vacant units, and sum contract and market rent per currency, never across currencies. Filters by property and occupancy apply to the page and to the CSV, XLSX and PDF downloads alike. The collection view for a month takes the charges due in that month: billed is their amount, collected is the recorded external receipts against them, a lease is paid in full when nothing remains after receipts and reductions, and its payment state is paid by the recorded method (ACH, card, cash, check or other; “method not recorded” for receipts entered before this rule), partial or unpaid. The method is what a manager records; Terrace has not processed or verified it. Pending funds are reported as none because Terrace holds none; PAY-002, PAY-003 and PAY-007 add processor receipts and pending funds, and ACCT-003 adds deposit obligations to the roll (shown as not recorded until then), before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Run an as-of rent roll before and after a scheduled renewal and move-in, reconcile occupied/vacant unit counts and effective rents and download the same filtered data. For one month, show collected of billed and leases paid for the portfolio and, per unit, the ACH, card, cash, partial and unpaid states, reconciling every total to resident-ledger receipts.

- **REPORT-002 — Report delinquency and collection performance.** Show current/past-due aging with tenant arrears separate from housing-authority arrears (PAY-013), pending payments, broken promises, payment plans, notices and collection outcomes by household/property/owner. Separate settled cash from attempted collection and permit authorized drilldown/export without exposing screening reports. Exact semantics (20 October 2026, ct ruling): done for current recorded capabilities; PAY-008 inherits returned/reversed ACH and pending/attempted-collection outcomes, PAY-011 inherits active/broken plans, notices and resolved outcomes, and PAY-013 inherits tenant/HAP separation and the corresponding acceptance cases before shipping. The as-of date is an inclusive property-local day no later than today. Each due charge’s outstanding is exact charge cents minus external receipts received through that day minus reductions on their explicit approved posting day, or property-local recorded day when absent; future-due charges and their allocations are excluded. This reconstructs effective dates from records known now, not what staff knew then. Due today is current; earlier balances age by calendar days into 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 and over 90. Paid lines remain drillable; one household shares one balance, never multiplied by co-tenants. USD, AUD and currency-unconfirmed balances remain separate. Property/household filters apply existing reports.read portfolio scope. Owner filters select the ownership set effective on asOf; a matching owner selects the full household balance once, not a percentage allocation, and missing ownership remains unknown. Staff see dated charge, receipt, reduction and ownership sources and export the same filtered CSV without screening data. External receipts are not settled-bank proof; PAY-005 manually recorded pending funds are dated separately and never deducted from receivables. Linked negative receipts include only source-limited recorded refunds/reversals. Processor pending payments, returned ACH, plans, broken promises, delivered notices, collection outcomes and HAP splits remain not recorded, never inferred zero or resolved. Owner/portfolio-manager/bookkeeper in the household’s portfolio assigns an active owner/portfolio-manager/bookkeeper as operational follow-up owner, without send or collect authority; absent or revoked/out-of-scope/restored assignees read “unassigned — assign follow-up owner”. Assignment changes are versioned and audited with commit-time live actor/target scope checks. With an eligible assignee and a latest approved arrears draft, the next action is “review and send externally; Terrace has not sent it”; otherwise prepare and review a proposal. Assignment history and approved drafts are dated through asOf, while eligibility is checked live. SAFE-004 treats assignment references/events as accounting follow-up evidence: seven-year fiscal retention from their property-local recorded day and accounting holds; personal redaction deletes those references/events while preserving financial amounts under the opaque alias. Resident access includes the subject’s assignment dates/references without staff identity. SAFE-005 archives/exports/restores the history with opaque source staff IDs, which grant no destination authority; import undo is held after an assignment as later native work. **Acceptance evidence:** Filter delinquency to one owner, include a returned ACH, an active plan and a voucher lease with unpaid HAP, reconcile aging to resident balances and show follow-up owner and next permitted action for each overdue household.

- **REPORT-003 — Measure vacancy leasing and renewal performance.** Show occupancy, economic vacancy, days vacant, days to lease, lead source conversion, showing/application drop-off and renewal retention with explicit date windows and formulas. Distinguish stale listings from ready units and explain forecast assumptions separately from actuals. Exact semantics (20 October 2026, ct ruling): current capabilities conform now; LEASE-001, LEASE-002 and LEASE-003 add actual listing publication/freshness before they ship, and LEASE-012 adds campaign, reply and executed-renewal outcomes before it ships. The report uses inclusive property-local windows of at most 732 days ending no later than each selected property’s today, and inventory begins on its recorded creation day. Occupancy is occupied rentable unit-days divided by rentable unit-days; leases cover start through move-out or end inclusive. Current rentable status is a snapshot, not reconstructed historical inventory. Vacancy spells retain their recorded beginning and are clipped to the window; days to lease is the nonnegative local-day difference from vacancy start to the next tenancy’s recorded creation, never move-in or signature evidence. Future move-ins and current make-ready ready dates are separately labeled schedules/forecasts; a published available date is a recorded actual. Listing status says “listing not recorded (LEASE-001); freshness unknown”, never zero stale listings. Economic vacancy is (estimated potential rent minus recorded external rent receipts received in the window) divided by estimated potential rent, and may be negative. Potential uses the current USD monthly market-rent snapshot, explicitly an assumption taken at report time, divided by each calendar month’s actual days and summed as exact rational cents, rounded half up once across the unit or report. Missing-market units are excluded from both potential and receipts. Only confirmed USD receipts on term-classified rent charges count; unlinked manual receipts, unconfirmed/other currencies and missing market rents are separate coverage gaps, never inferred zero or converted. A receipt is not bank settlement. First-contact lead cohorts exclude merged/held duplicate rows, keep reviewed-separate contacts, and count only dated staff stage events effective and recorded by the window end; skipped stages are never inferred. Source conversion is leased divided by leads; showing/application drop-off is the number with a shown/applied event lacking an applied/leased event, divided by the corresponding actual stage count. Renewal retention is approved recorded renewals divided by original lease-term expiries in the window, preserving prior ends through renewal history and separating pending, rejected and nonrenewed cases; a LEASE-012 campaign offer counts as renewed only once its signed renewal activated by the window end, its scheduling, send results, replies and outcomes are dated sources, and a declined, nonrenewal, no-response or month-to-month outcome counts as nonrenewed. It never claims delivery or electronic signatures; a signature is reported as staff-recorded. Zero denominators are not measurable. Existing reports.read holders read scoped aggregates and unit/lease/receipt sources; only those who also hold prospect.read receive prospect drill IDs, events and references. **Acceptance evidence:** Follow a vacant unit through showing, lease and move-in, compare source conversion and vacancy days and drill the metric to dated source events.

- **REPORT-004 — Report maintenance service and cost.** Report request age, response/booking/resolution time, repeat repairs, open emergencies, vendor performance, asset cost and budget variance. Use confirmed outcomes and disclose missing timestamps; vendor closure alone cannot improve resolution metrics. Exact semantics: the report covers maintenance jobs on tenancies in the reader’s portfolios (ROLE-001: owner, portfolio managers, maintenance coordinators, bookkeepers and accountants), filtered by the property-local date the job was prepared (inclusive), property and status (all, unresolved, or one status). Each job shows its status (waiting for approval, approved, handed off, completion reported and not confirmed, reopened, resolved with the resident’s confirmation, or closed without it), request age in whole days from preparation to the office’s today while open, response time in hours from preparation to the first approval, handoff time to the recorded external handoff, and resolution time to the resident’s confirmation only while that confirmation is the job’s current outcome; a vendor’s completion report, a reopened job or a closure without confirmation has no resolution time. Repeat repairs are jobs with a warranty or billable return visit (WORK-008). Vendor performance counts each vendor’s jobs, resolved, reopened, return visits and average resolution hours. Asset cost sums the estimates of each asset’s jobs whose current terms are approved or handed off; budget variance compares each owner yearly budget (WORK-003) with the approved and handed-off estimates due that year, as WORK-003 counts them. Costs are labeled approved estimates, not invoices (WORK-009 carries invoiced cost). Missing timestamps are listed per job (no approval, no handoff, no completion report), and booking time is preparation to the first appointment confirmed by both parties externally and recorded by staff (WORK-005), or explicitly missing; open emergencies remain not recorded until WORK-001 (emergency triage), which inherits this report before it ships. The filtered list downloads as CSV. **Acceptance evidence:** Run a service report for a reopened repair and an unconfirmed completion, trace durations and owner cost to evidence and export the filtered unresolved queue.

- **REPORT-005 — Build governed custom reports and fields.** Managers define typed custom fields, validated values, document merge fields and saved reports with formulas, grouping and role-aware filters. Show source lineage and schema changes; templates cannot leak hidden fields or silently change prior generated documents. Exact semantics: fields and definitions are portfolio-scoped on units, properties or owners, using existing ROLE-001 rights; chosen read roles restrict those rights. Fields support text, finite decimal number, boolean, date and select values, with required/range/choice validation and dated source/version history. Numeric formulas use add/subtract/multiply/divide with IEEE-754 arithmetic and no monetary rounding; missing operands yield null, numeric aggregates ignore null and division by zero is refused. Reports group selected columns, filter typed source fields and retain schema pins; a changed source schema requires explicit definition revision (409). Templates merge custom field keys into plain text. Generated documents freeze text and template/schema/value/source versions; later edits create new versions, while downloads recheck current and historical field access. **Acceptance evidence:** Add a unit inspection field, use it in a saved report and document template, hide a sensitive owner field from leasing staff and verify their export/merge cannot reveal it.

- **REPORT-006 — Schedule delivered operating reports.** Ct approved delivery and installation-only snapshot custody on 24 October 2026: explicit installation-owner approval for each send; existing owner portal fields only, with no new recipient data fields; live recipient grants checked at send; source-verified frozen statements; snapshots excluded from archives; no unattended sends; uncertain outcomes are visible and never retried automatically. Retention default ADOPTED: snapshots remain until the owner explicitly deletes them through an audited path; legal and accountant holds block deletion until released. [Generation and reviewed delivery semantics](docs/report-schedules.md) state the implemented timezone, close and custody rules. Schedule rent roll, delinquency, vacancy, maintenance and owner and financial reports by recipient scope, timezone and close status, completing the full owner batch within the SAFE-009 bound. Retain generation version, secure delivery link, delivery failures and next action; retry transport safely without emailing duplicates or stale permissions. **Acceptance evidence:** Schedule an owner report across a timezone boundary, revoke an owner before delivery and bounce another recipient; verify scope recheck, one authorized delivery and a failed-delivery task.

- **REPORT-007 — Expose cash and vacancy trade-offs.** Project rent, renewals, deposits held, payables, capital work, reserves and owner distributions under explicit scenarios. Show confidence, assumptions and vacancy-day/cash differences; projections never post ledger entries or approve lease pricing on their own. Exact semantics: on a property-linked tenancy the owner or a staff role holding the existing reports.read capability compares two read-only plans: repair before listing and immediate marketing with a concession. Both require an explicit inclusive property-local horizon, dated source reference and confidence/uncertainty note, plus source-backed rent per tenancy cadence, optional assumed renewal date and new rent, make-ready days, letting days, total concession, opening operating cash, deposits already held/new receipts/refunds, capital or additional costs, planned distributions and collection percent. Zero is entered explicitly; missing cash or deposit history is never invented. The comparison sources the tenancy’s recorded rent/cadence/version, the current approved unpaid vendor-bill allocation for that property once per current bill revision, and dated management agreements; it names each invoice/revision and agreement. The reserve is the requirement in force at horizon end, never a claim that cash is held; the earlier dated reserve schedule is retained in the result. Confirmed USD is required because reserves and payables are USD; historical amounts are never relabeled or converted. Without the property or an agreement effective by horizon start the report shows a source gap. Repairs run make-ready then letting, so vacant days are their sum; immediate marketing runs them concurrently, so vacant days are their maximum. The ready date is the horizon start plus vacant days and is the first assumed rent day; vacancy within the horizon is capped at its inclusive day count. Daily rent uses each calendar month’s actual days for monthly cadence, seven for weekly and fourteen for fortnightly; an assumed renewal changes rent from its stated day, and forecasts explicitly continue rent over the horizon as an assumption rather than extending the actual lease. Exact rational daily rent is summed and rounded half up once to cents; expected collected rent applies the user’s 0–100% estimate to the exact gross before that rounding. The full concession, current payables once (regardless of their invoice dates), capital/additional costs and final reserve floor reduce opening operating cash plus collected rent; distributions reduce the result and a negative result shows a potential shortfall, never payment authority. A current payable is not repeated in capital assumptions. Deposits are separately shown as opening held plus new expected less refunds and never become operating cash or owner distributions; collection percent does not discount deposits. Other expected fees, taxes or operating costs need an explicit additional-cost assumption; no bank balance, arrears or reconciliation is inferred. Changing assumptions recalculates cash and ready dates without storing scenarios, changing approvals, posting ledger entries or approving rent. Existing role and portfolio read scope apply on the page and API. LEASE-012, PAY-013 and ACCT-003/010/012 inherit sourcing their renewal, payer, deposit, distribution and statement actuals into this comparison before those records ship; until then all those forecast categories remain explicit user assumptions. **Acceptance evidence:** Compare repairing before listing versus immediate marketing with a rent concession, change the vacancy assumption and inspect the recalculated cash/ready dates while actual books remain unchanged.

### Integrations and persistent operating automation

- **OPS-001 — Expose a scoped property operations API.** Provide documented versioned APIs for properties, households, leases, resident and owner ledgers, documents, work and reports with scoped revocable credentials, pagination, validation and idempotent writes. Agents receive read and prepare scopes and cannot turn a credential into human approval. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: each credential acts with one staff role’s capabilities and portfolios, rechecked in D1 on every call; out-of-scope records answer 404 and out-of-role actions 403. SAFE-001 applies before this ships: minting, rotating or revoking a credential needs the fresh email-link proof, and a credential never satisfies a second factor for a person. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a read-only accountant and prepare-only agent, traverse paginated records, retry an idempotent work proposal and refuse approval, payout or cross-property reads outside each credential’s scope. Each credential is also refused (403) any action its ROLE-001 role lacks and answers 404 for records outside its portfolios. Minting a credential without a fresh email-link proof is refused (403). **Exact semantics (done 21 October 2026):** a credential belongs to one staff role and a fixed set of portfolios (or all) and has scope `read` (GET only) or `prepare` (GET plus the listed proposal commands: maintenance.prepare/revise, quote.add, renewal.prepare, arrears.prepare, correction.prepare, charges.preview, agent.execute); any command not on that list, and every approval, owner decision, period or access command, is refused (403 `credential_cannot_approve` or `credential_scope`) so a future approval, payout, send or connection door is closed to credentials until it is deliberately listed with its own acceptance; a role the credential's role lacks answers 403 `forbidden`. Tokens (`ttk_…`) are shown once, stored only as a SHA-256, never archived or exported, and the owner mints, rotates (the old token stops at once) and revokes them under the fresh email-link proof; credentials carry no session, so they never pass a second factor and never open a page, backup or readable export. Version 1 lists (`/api/v1/{properties,leases,households,ledgers,owner-ledgers,documents,work,reports}`) are scoped before paging, sorted by id, with `limit` 1 to 200 (default 50) and an opaque `cursor`; an out-of-scope record is 404. Every credential write needs an `Idempotency-Key` (8 to 100 characters): the same key and body replays the stored response once (`idempotent-replay: true`), the same key with another body is 422, and a key whose first attempt never reported back stays pending (409) rather than being run again. Any error after the key is claimed retains it as pending, including failure to persist the response after a domain commit; restart never releases it. History names the credential, its role version and scope. Each future resource (PORT-007 documents, ACCT-012 statements, PORTAL-010 notices) and command door joins `/api/v1` with the same scoping before it ships.

- **OPS-002 — Publish dependable events and automation hooks.** Emit signed versioned events for lease, payment, work, document and ledger changes with delivery history, deduplication, replay and disabled-subscription controls. Connect Zapier and Crank without granting them broader rights than their credentials. **Acceptance evidence:** Subscribe to work completion and rent settlement, fail then replay delivery, process a duplicate and revoke the subscription; show exactly one downstream effect and no later delivery. DEMO-001 applies before this ships: its demo flow retains the effect guard and adds a public-door no-egress assertion; no real payment, message or webhook is sent from a demo.

- **OPS-003 — Run persistent workflow templates.** Configure leasing, renewals, rent, delinquency and unit-turn workflows with triggers, conditions, steps, assignees, due times and escalation. Preserve the next action, attempt, reply, external reference and completion evidence through restarts; pause on stale authority, contact limits or uncertain results. **Acceptance evidence:** Start a renewal and unit-turn workflow, restart between steps, receive a reply and exhaust a contact limit; inspect durable next actions and a human escalation rather than a false completed state. **Exact semantics (ct 22 October 2026; hourly sweep and send recording built in the OPS-003 fix round):** a template version (kind leasing, renewal, rent, delinquency or unit turn) holds a kind-specific trigger (renewal: days before the lease ends; leasing: days an enquiry has had no activity; rent: 1–30 days past due; delinquency: 31+ days past due; unit turn: an open make-ready board), optional conditions (one property; a minimum overdue amount), 1–12 steps (task, contact or gate; each with a due-day offset and an optional assignee), one contact limit for the whole run (1–10 attempts), and the owner or portfolio manager an escalation goes to. Only the owner and every-portfolio managers configure; a change appends a version and runs keep the version they started under. A run starts for one record only when it matches the trigger and conditions inside the person's portfolios and holds the existing action for that kind of record (leasing: prospect.respond; renewal: renewal.reply; rent and delinquency: arrears.prepare; unit turn: turnover.task.update); a person starts it, or a sweep starts the runs the triggers call for, once per record and template. The sweep runs unattended every hour (a Cron Trigger) and on demand (Run now, by the owner or an every-portfolio manager). The unattended tick acts as `scheduler:workflows`, attributed to the person who saved the template version, with no session. It is fenced on that person still being the owner or an every-portfolio manager; a template that fails the fence starts nothing and is listed as needing a configurer, and its running or paused runs escalate to the owner with a durable next action. A tick only starts runs, escalates overdue steps and runs WORK-010's maintenance scheduler (its orders still await owner or admin approval). It never records an attempt, reply, evidence, resumption or closure. Each tick is recorded (time, runs started, steps escalated, templates skipped), and a replayed or concurrent tick starts or escalates nothing twice. Every transition appends a sequenced event and rewrites the run's durable next action in D1, so a restart loses nothing. Task steps finish with an evidence reference; contact steps record each attempt (channel, outcome, external reference) and then the reply; gate steps finish only when Terrace already holds the fact (the make-ready board is published ready, the renewal is executed, the prospect is leased, the overdue balance is cleared). A run completes only when its last step has recorded evidence. A run pauses, writing nothing else, when the starter's or last resumer's role changed or ended, its assignee may no longer work it, its record changed or already reached its outcome, or a contact attempt's result is uncertain; a manager reviews and resumes (an uncertain result needs a stated delivered or not-delivered). A run escalates to the named person (the owner if that person no longer reaches the portfolio) when a step passes its due day (found by the sweep), when the contact limit is used up without an agreed reply, or when a reply is declined or unclear; an escalated run takes no further step and a person closes it (closed, never completed) or records the agreeing reply. Contact (ct, 22 October 2026): the workflow engine sends nothing itself, and staff record attempts and replies. A LEASE-005 prospect email, or a LEASE-012 approved renewal-offer send, made while a matching run is live for that record is recorded on the run as its next attempt. The email event is the external reference and the provider's answer is the outcome: accepted counts as sent and awaiting a reply; an uncertain answer for any recipient pauses the run; rejected, rate-limited, unreachable, suppressed or unconfigured is listed but does not count toward the limit. A send while the run is paused or escalated is listed on the run for the reviewing person and changes nothing else; a prospect's refused contact channel (LEASE-005) refuses the attempt; run labels carry no resident names; API credentials cannot run any workflow command. Future clauses inheriting this: WORK-010 (the unattended maintenance scheduler), PORTAL-005, COM-001 and NOTIFY clauses (a Terrace-sent contact must use a contact step, its consent and the same limit), OPS-002 (events for run transitions), AUTO-001 agents (prepare-only, never a step).

- **OPS-004 — Operate integrations with visible health and cost.** Show each provider’s configured permissions, entitlements, last successful exchange, freshness, failures and billable operation estimate. Validate setup with real provider checks; bounded transient retries never conceal missing credentials, denied access or semantic errors. ROLE-001 applies before this ships: only the owner configures integrations. **Acceptance evidence:** Connect a valid provider and one with denied scope, expire a token and simulate transport failure; inspect distinct actionable states, bounded retries and cost/usage records with secrets redacted. A non-owner operator’s integration change is refused (403). SAFE-005 applies before this ships: each connected provider appears in the readable export’s reconnect list, and a restore imports no provider session or token.

- **OPS-005 — Link insurance coverage through MSI.** Use MSI or an authorized insurance partner for renter quotes/enrollment, policy proof, effective dates, expirations and claims handoff; also record externally purchased coverage. Show coverage gaps without inventing approval or acting as insurer, and restrict policy details. **Acceptance evidence:** Resident submits external proof and another enrolls through the partner boundary; expire a policy, request renewed evidence and hand a claim to the insurer with status/reference retained.

- **OPS-006 — Connect finance signing and trade siblings.** Use Pantry for company-level accounting handoff, Inkwell for signature envelopes, Glove for a contractor’s field-service job and Gasket for an owner’s maintenance asset system where selected. Explicit mappings join external IDs and outcomes without merging their separate products into Terrace. **Acceptance evidence:** Send an approved repair to a Glove boundary, receive completion and invoice references, sign a lease through Inkwell and reconcile a Pantry journal; verify each external identity and permission remains distinct. SAFE-005 applies before this ships: its signed envelopes and their signed files appear in the readable export and come back with a restore into a fresh installation.

- **OPS-007 — Respect adjacent property product boundaries.** Terrace owns long-term residential operations and its full trust ledger. Cabin owns vacation-rental reservations/channel management; general business file sync belongs to Chest and sales CRM to Orbit. Link records through permissioned APIs instead of building booking engines, generic drives or sales pipelines here. Exact semantics (20 October 2026, ct ruling): the sibling decides access for the person. The installation owner alone enters each sibling product’s https origin (a host name; never an address literal, localhost, credentials, path, query or fragment). An owner or portfolio manager within the property’s portfolio links a property to a record address on that configured origin with a label; anyone who reads the property (existing scope) sees its links, and others get not-found. Terrace stores only the origin and the record’s address and label, never guest, booking, reservation, file or pipeline data; following a link opens the sibling, where the person’s own Cabin or Chest sign-in and grants decide access, and Terrace adds no credential and never vouches for the person. Each link is labelled as unchecked. An owner-configured installation credential may later confirm only that the record exists and show its title/status label (never exported), but owner-entered origins are outbound destinations under the egress rule, so that confirmation waits on Base’s egress door. Links change no residential ledger, statement or export record. **Acceptance evidence:** Link a mixed owner’s residential property to its Cabin record and a Chest document, navigate the authorized references and confirm residential ledger exports remain complete without short-stay reservation duplication.

- **OPS-008 — Handle commercial CAM and specialist housing through adapters.** For mixed portfolios, integrate specialist systems for commercial CAM recoveries and project-based affordable compliance regimes (HUD project-based Section 8 certifications, LIHTC compliance and their regulatory reporting) with explicit source-of-truth mappings and reconciled residential impacts. Tenant-based vouchers on ordinary leases are core receivables in PAY-013, not adapter work. Specialist regimes remain separate; missing provider agreements are tracked implementation work. **Acceptance evidence:** Import a specialist CAM allocation and a project-based subsidy receipt through authorized provider boundaries, reconcile the residential owner/tenant effects and expose unsupported mappings as held exceptions for a person.

Repeats and apply replays write nothing and never re-create reversed records; re-importing a reversed source row needs a new reviewed approval. Erasure redacts the reason and evidence and keeps the disposition. An import that cannot be fenced this way, including every import created with strict reversal, is refused (409) and left unchanged until a reviewed reversal-policy conversion exists.
