### Security privacy ownership and recovery

- **SAFE-001 — Enforce authenticated least-privilege doors.** Check live identity, organization, property and action permissions before every page, API, file, export and agent operation. Use CSRF protection, expiring sessions and secure cookies; require step-up authentication for bank/access changes and support SSO/MFA for staff. No client-supplied role or hidden route grants authority. Exact semantics: every page, API read, download, export and command reads the live Base session and operator, then ROLE-001’s capability table and portfolio scope; agents use member accounts through the same doors. Commands need Origin equal to the installation and are refused cross-site. Changes to bank references and legal entities (entity.add, account.add) and to access (operator invite, role, status, the second-factor requirement and authenticator resets) need Base’s fresh email-link proof: the sign-in link that created the session or a completed step-up link, within 10 minutes; without it the command answers 403 and writes nothing. Terrace’s own second factor is a time-based one-time password (RFC 6238: HMAC-SHA1, 30-second steps, 6 digits, one step either side) with ten single-use recovery codes stored only as hashes; a code is never accepted twice, and five wrong codes in 15 minutes lock verification for 15 minutes. Once a person confirms an authenticator, each new sign-in of theirs must pass it before any other door, Base’s own account and access doors included (pages show only the two-step page; API calls answer 403). The owner, after passing their own, may require a second factor for everyone who signs in by email link; un-enrolled staff then enroll before anything else. Staff signing in through the organization’s identity provider (OIDC) count as satisfied, under that provider’s MFA policy. Only the owner resets someone’s authenticator. Secrets are sealed with AES-GCM under a key derived from the installation’s session secret and, with recovery codes and passed sessions, are never archived, so people enroll again after a restore elsewhere. Doors not built yet inherit this before they ship: OPS-001 credentials, ACCT-018 and ROLE-003 payee bank details and notifications of change, and PORTAL-001, PORTAL-002 and PORTAL-003 bank details. **Acceptance evidence:** Crawl all private doors signed out and with each restricted role, replay a revoked session and attempt a cross-site payout or bank change without step-up; deny all unauthorized reads and writes.

- **SAFE-002 — Keep attributable immutable operating history.** Retain who prepared, approved, changed and executed each lease, notice, payment, bank instruction, work order, import and close, with original source, timestamps, policy version and outcome. Audit reads/exports of sensitive records; authorized users can search/export history without rewriting it. Exact semantics: every Terrace command that changes a lease, household, rent charge, receipt, correction, maintenance job, approval, owner record, role or setting writes one history row in the same D1 batch as the change, with the actor, the time (UTC), their role and its version at that moment (the policy they acted under; the owner’s is “owner”), the tenancy it concerns, the source they gave (a lease reference, receipt or handoff reference, or reason) and the outcome; move-in applies and undos, restores and operator activation or deactivation, which Base carries out, add a row once they succeed (Base’s own /auth doors, open only to the owner, keep Base’s records). Sensitive reads add a row with outcome “read” (owner statements, owner allocation statements, rent roll and collections reads, photo and handoff packet downloads, ACCT-011 close statement downloads) and exports one with outcome “exported” (backup, readable export, history export). The owner reads and exports all history; portfolio managers read, and accountants read and export, history about tenancies in their portfolios, and history with no tenancy only with all portfolios; others are refused (403). History rows and accounting amounts are never deleted. Restrict and redact TIN, screening and identity data; scan attachments and show access scope. **Acceptance evidence:** Upload a restricted report, inspect its private download headers and expiry, request it with a revoked role and inspect logs/export/browser output for secrets, PAN and TIN leakage.

Explain retained statutory records, delete eligible copies/search/media/provider artifacts and preserve a minimal non-resurrecting fence; never erase ledger evidence merely to hide a discrepancy. Exact semantics (ct 19 October 12:55Z): the reviewed default periods are lease records 7 calendar years after lease end, accounting identity 7 years after its fiscal year (the calendar year in today’s books), screening 2 years after decision or 5 for adverse action, and communications 3 years after communication. The anniversary is the last retained day, inclusive in the property time zone, with 29 February clamped to 28 February; a PORT-008 pack may only lengthen a default before it ships. The installation owner records a resident access or erasure request with its external reference (no resident contact by Terrace), downloads that tenancy’s primary-resident access file without other household or owner contacts, and reviews retained classes, dates and reasons. Only the owner places or releases a class or all-record legal hold, with a reason. Erasure requires that request’s current review fingerprint and exact resident email; changed holds or terms require a new review. A lease period or lease/all hold prevents deletion of lease evidence. Once eligible, its originals, photos, work and import copies/search provenance are removed atomically with the restore fence; accounting identity stays while its period or hold applies. After both expire or are released, the tenancy’s personal fields and financial free-text references, fee labels, close references and resident-linked audit source text become an opaque alias/record id; amounts, currencies, dates, financial links, close rows and attributable audit events are kept, and an ordinary update still cannot alter them. The erased tenancy disappears from operational reads; retained accounting remains in exports. Restore to an independent installation with referential integrity and destination identities; list provider secrets/mandates that must be reconnected. Exact semantics: the owner downloads two exports. The backup (.rer, Base’s documented portability format) holds every table except platform bookkeeping, Base sign-in records and the named secrets (the capability table, authenticators, recovery codes, passed sessions and failed attempts); it restores only into an empty installation, keeping identifiers and references, and never brings sessions or operator accounts across. The readable export (.zip) is built from that same archive: one CSV per table with a header row (money in whole cents beside its currency, ISO dates, UTC timestamps), every stored file as its original bytes under files/ with its SHA-256 in the CSV cell that held it, a manifest of tables, row counts, columns, file checksums and what was left out, and a README listing what to reconnect after a restore: mail delivery, people and their roles, authenticators, any identity provider, and that Terrace moves no money so a restore repeats no payment. Every record table a later clause adds is archived and exported the same way unless it is a named secret; PORT-007 adds its stored documents and media as original files, PORTAL-005 and PORTAL-006 their communications, OPS-006 and LEASE-012 their signed files, and OPS-004 each connected provider to the reconnect list, before they ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Export a complete leased/paid/repaired property, restore to a fresh installation and compare balances, signed files, communications and work evidence; reconnect providers without importing sessions or repeating money movement.

### Service boundaries and specialist partners

- **BOUND-001 — Use regulated rails without becoming the custodian.** Terrace owns the complete residential ledger and orchestrates collection, trust-account reconciliation, approved vendor/owner payments and deposit refunds through contracted banks and processors. Banks hold funds; providers perform payment-network functions, identity verification and required onboarding. For outbound ACH the manager’s bank remains the originating bank: Terrace prepares and reconciles the NACHA files (ACCT-018) and never holds funds. This boundary does not exclude online collection or trust accounting. **Acceptance evidence:** Onboard a manager’s processor and bank account, collect rent, reconcile trust subledgers and execute an approved payout; show funds remain at the bank/provider and Terrace records authoritative reconciled outcomes.

- **BOUND-002 — Keep housing legal tax and insurance decisions human.** TransUnion supplies reports; a manager decides applicants. Counsel approves jurisdiction-specific lease/notice/deposit rule packs and eviction/service actions; accountants review taxes and filings; MSI/other insurers issue policies. Track all referrals and responses in Terrace without claiming to be a bureau, lawyer, CPA or insurer. **Acceptance evidence:** Hold a disputed screening result, uncertain notice rule and rejected tax filing; refer each to its authorized professional, record the response and resume only the explicitly approved action.

- **BOUND-003 — Coordinate emergency and physical work with people.** Local licensed vendors, the manager’s on-call service, emergency responders and utilities perform field work and emergency response. Terrace delivers urgent instructions/escalations, acknowledges handoff and checks subsequent resolution; it never presents an unattended bot or successful notification as physical emergency assistance. **Acceptance evidence:** Receive a safety request, provide reviewed 911/utility guidance, obtain a human on-call acknowledgment and keep the case open until authorized resolution evidence and resident follow-up are recorded. Exact semantics: WORK-001’s safety cases carry this boundary. Terrace delivers the approved guidance to staff who read it to the caller, alerts people by the installation’s email (a sign-in link, labeled with the provider’s outcome) and an urgent queue, takes acknowledgement only from the named on-call person or backup, and keeps the case open until the owner or a portfolio manager records field-work evidence and the resident’s follow-up; an email the provider accepted is never shown as a person reached or as emergency assistance. Escalation reaches people by the installation’s email and the in-app urgent queue; timed SMS/voice paging is WORK-001’s and PORTAL-005’s (ct ruling 18:50Z).

- **BOUND-004 — Stay residential: no commercial leases, CAM or HOA dues.** Terrace manages residential rentals only. It has no commercial lease type, no CAM reconciliation and no homeowners’-association dues, assessments or association accounting, and says so in setup (the app’s first-run portfolio setup, which is the empty Tenancies page after Finish setup, and the Move in screen), the documentation and its public pages, so a buyer with commercial or association work learns the limit before importing. Commercial CAM recoveries and project-based affordable housing remain with specialist systems through OPS-008, and a residential owner’s own HOA dues remain an ordinary recurring vendor bill (ACCT-007), not association accounting; ACCT-007 carries that acceptance, because vendor bills ship with it. An import that carries commercial lease records holds them as exceptions rather than loading them as residential tenancies. In Terrace tenancy CSV v1 the optional `lease_type` column marks a row: empty or `residential` (any letter case) imports, and any other value is held as a rejected exception naming that value, so the reviewed file cannot be approved and nothing from it loads until the row is removed. Each incumbent importer (MOVE-002 through MOVE-007) inherits this hold for the lease or property type its source carries before it ships (MOVE-001). **Acceptance evidence:** Search the app, API and setup for any commercial-lease, CAM or association-dues feature and find none; read the stated limit in setup and the docs; import a source file containing a commercial lease and show it held as an exception.

### Open source and hosted demo

- **OPEN-001 — Free and open source under the MIT license, run by one command.** Terrace is free and open source under the MIT license: the repository’s LICENSE and rer-project.json declare MIT, and anyone may run, modify and redistribute it. Every capability in this contract ships in the open-source product with no license key, unit, seat or owner cap, per-payment fee, paid gate or upgrade prompt from Terrace’s authors. Paid third-party services a manager connects (payment processors, banks, Plaid, TransUnion, Zillow and Apartments.com, Lob, Twilio, Resend, Nelco, MSI and hosting) bill their own fees, and Terrace names the provider and links its pricing before the connection is enabled (SAFE-008). The run site and README show the one command `npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-terrace`, which starts a local, empty installation owned by the person who ran it, with no telemetry (SAFE-007). All capabilities that exist today conform; each future capability inherits the open-source/no-author-gate obligation before shipping. LEASE-002/003/004/006/008/011, PAY-002/003/004/007/012, ACCT-005/008/010/014/015/017/018, PORTAL-005/009, WORK-012, OPS-002/004/005/006/007 and SAFE-008 inherit provider naming/pricing before enabling their connection. Today the deployment door names Cloudflare hosting/storage and Resend email and their pricing before calling the deployment or secret-change hook; README names them before credential setup. The one-command acceptance runs the published npm/repository command in a fresh directory; registry/Git/dependency acquisition is expected, while the installed app contacts no telemetry or license service. Terrace replaces AppFolio, Buildium and Rent Manager through MOVE-002 through MOVE-004 and MOVE-011 and is not affiliated with them. **Acceptance evidence:** Read LICENSE and the project metadata and find MIT; build the run site and read the command on /run; run that command in a clean directory and reach setup with an empty portfolio and no outbound telemetry; search the installed source and app for license keys, caps and upgrade prompts and find none; start a provider connection and see its provider and pricing named before it is enabled.

- **DEMO-001 — Hosted demo portfolio that sends nothing.** The homepage’s “Try the demo” link opens a hosted demo of the current release at https://demo.run-terrace.com/, built from this repository’s main branch in Base demo mode. It holds a lived-in sample portfolio seeded once after its owner exists: tenancies, rent history, renewal and arrears proposals awaiting a person, photographed inspections and maintenance in each state. A visitor signs in with one click to an isolated demo as owner, manager or preparer and can approve the prepared drafts; email, SMS, payments, webhooks and other provider writes return simulated success, so no request reaches a real provider or person and no mail is delivered. As target journeys ship they appear in the demo with the same rule. Demo data and simulated providers exist only under demo mode: a production build or deploy refuses `RER_DEMO`, and an ordinary installation starts empty. Hosted interactive acceptance uses the same commit on the isolated `demo.test.run-terrace.com` host with Turnstile’s published test keys and the private measurement credential, alongside the real production homepage/link and signed-out landing readback. Production keeps real Turnstile; no production CAPTCHA completion is claimed. The acceptance run ends both visitor copies and deletes its test host. PAY-002/PAY-003/PAY-004, PORTAL-005 and OPS-002 inherit demo suppression and corresponding no-egress journeys before their payment, SMS, delivery or webhook doors ship. **Acceptance evidence:** Open the homepage link and reach the hosted demo signed out; sign in as the owner and as a preparer in separate browsers and approve a renewal and a maintenance handoff in one; confirm the other visitor sees none of those changes; observe that no outbound email, SMS or payment request leaves the demo; run a production build with `RER_DEMO` set and see it refused; start a fresh installation and find it empty.

## Push further — accountable portfolio agents

These agents serve the same residential job on real operating records. Authority, human decisions, completion evidence and safe stopping conditions are part of each journey.

- **AGENT-001 — Run repair intake through owner-statement resolution.** A portfolio agent joins resident intake, asset history, access constraints, vendor qualifications, quotes, approved spend, appointment, completion evidence, resident reply, invoice and owner ledger. It books within human-approved authority, chases blocked work and confirms repair with the resident, then matches the bill and reconciles its statement effect. People approve vendors, spend changes and payments; emergencies escalate immediately. **Acceptance evidence:** Give the agent a leaking tap, approved vendor/spend envelope and resident availability; interrupt booking, change the invoice and receive a failed completion check. It resumes safely, reopens the repair, holds the mismatch and closes only after confirmed repair and reconciled owner cost.

- **AGENT-002 — Plan vacancy recovery with cash trade-offs.** An agent combines lease ends, condition evidence, make-ready dependencies, vendor quotes, lead funnel and explicitly dated market assumptions to compare repair, listing and offer plans by vacancy days and cash impact. It follows the approved plan to signed lease and move-in, revising forecasts as facts change. Managers approve capital work, pricing, offers, legal terms and applicant decisions. **Acceptance evidence:** Present two turnover plans with source-linked cost/vacancy assumptions, approve one, delay a vendor and recalculate; follow the revised authorized plan to a human-approved applicant and executed lease, comparing actual vacancy/cash with forecast.

- **AGENT-003 — Investigate deposit and close exceptions.** An agent joins lease deposit obligations, processor settlements, bank feeds and beneficiary subledgers to find missing deposits, duplicates, owner misallocations and stale outstanding items. It assembles source-linked correction proposals and pursues missing evidence before close. Bookkeepers approve corrections; deposit deductions, transfers and payouts retain separate human approvals. **Acceptance evidence:** Introduce a duplicate receipt, missing deposit and repair charged to the wrong owner; have the agent explain each difference from source evidence, propose corrections and reconcile only approved entries while unresolved differences block close.

- **AGENT-004 — Pursue arrears to a permitted resolution.** An agent tracks consented attempts, replies, promised payments, plans and actual settled receipts, proposes the next permitted contact and follows through until paid, a plan is met or an accountable professional accepts handoff. It pauses on dispute, accommodation, contact limits or changed balance. Managers approve concessions/notices/money movement; counsel controls legal escalation. **Acceptance evidence:** Work late rent with a promise that fails, a later returned payment and a disputed fee; show permitted next actions and holds, obtain human approvals, then verify settled resolution rather than treating a promise or submitted debit as payment.

- **AGENT-005 — Steward renewals through executed future rent.** An agent reads lease dates, current terms, communication history, condition and approved vacancy/cash assumptions, prepares sourced renewal alternatives and follows approved offers, replies, signatures and future charge setup. It surfaces retention/concession trade-offs and pauses if terms or authority change; people approve pricing, legal terms and notices. **Acceptance evidence:** Prepare renewal options, approve one, receive a counteroffer and require new approval; collect all signatures, verify future charges match the executed terms and escalate an unanswered offer before the deadline.

- **AGENT-006 — Compare inspection evidence without inventing damage.** An agent compares dated original entry/exit/repair photos, video, checklist notes and asset history to highlight possible changes with exact source locations and uncertainty. It proposes inspection follow-up, repair or deposit-review items; a qualified person decides condition, wear, liability and deductions. Insufficient or contradictory evidence remains visible. **Acceptance evidence:** Compare an unchanged fixture, documented damage and ambiguous low-light image; inspect source-linked findings, reject an unsupported deduction and carry a human-approved repair into work with original media retained.

- **AGENT-007 — Learn operating risks from verified outcomes.** An agent analyzes vacancy, repeat repairs, resident-confirmed outcomes, collections, cash, reconciliation exceptions and vendor reliability to suggest preventive tasks, staffing and workflow changes. It separates hypotheses from measured outcomes and forecasts cost/benefit. Managers review the proposal and authority before any changed vendor, budget, fee, contact or workflow is activated. **Acceptance evidence:** Detect repeated HVAC callbacks and a leasing bottleneck, show source cases and quantified assumptions, approve one preventive plan and compare later actual outcomes without silently modifying the other workflow.

- **AGENT-008 — Keep agent authority and evidence inspectable.** Every agent workload exposes purpose, permitted data/actions, human approvals, next step, due time, attempts, replies, costs and outcome evidence. People can pause, cancel or reassign; revocation stops queued execution. Untrusted resident/vendor documents cannot expand authority or instruct payments, and the agent cannot approve its own proposal. **Acceptance evidence:** Embed a payment instruction in an invoice, revoke the agent during a queued booking and cancel a follow-up. Show ignored document instructions, stopped execution and a complete human-readable action history with no self-approval.

- **AGENT-009 — Weigh each arrears case in cash and vacant days.** For each delinquent household an agent compares a payment plan with a pay-or-quit notice (and waiting) by expected cash and vacant days: rent at risk, plan receipts by date weighted by the household’s payment history, the notice period and eventual turnover timeline from the property’s PORT-008 pack, expected vacant days at the unit’s rent, make-ready and leasing cost, and the resulting expected loss for each option. It shows its dated assumptions, sources and confidence, drafts the preferred plan or notice, and stops for a person to approve and send it (PAY-011, PORTAL-009). It never sends, serves or posts ledger entries itself, pauses on dispute, accommodation or contact limits (AGENT-004) and later compares the chosen option’s actual cash and vacancy with its forecast. **Acceptance evidence:** Take one household with a plausible plan and one that has missed a plan; show each case’s plan-versus-notice comparison in cash and vacant days with its assumptions, change the vacancy assumption and watch the recommendation recalculate, approve and send the plan for one and the notice for the other as a person, and show nothing was sent before approval and the forecast compared with the actual outcome afterwards.

OPS-003 send grouping and recovery semantics: one explicitly requested renewal-offer send is one attempt across its recipient emails; every email event and per-recipient provider outcome is kept, and any uncertain recipient pauses the run. A slot is reserved in the same transaction as the source send event, preventing overlapping sends from bypassing the limit. Known non-sends release that reservation without consuming a contact. If a process ends before the provider result is recorded, the reservation survives and further workflow work is refused until a manager reviews the source and records delivered/not delivered through Review and resume; that unresolved attempt consumes its reserved slot. A later provider answer is still kept, never counted twice, and a contradictory answer pauses the run for review. The sweep's property-local date comes from its scheduled instant; Cron receipt identity is that UTC instant. The active installation owner authorizes WORK-010's unattended orders, prepared as `scheduler:workflows`, with no approval or dispatch.

PORTAL-001/002/003 inherit the portal door, its live per-request checks, session ending and the ownership-period statement; LEASE-009 inherits the screening retention class and restricted documents; PORTAL-005/006 inherit the notice retention class; PORT-005 signed originals appear in document search but keep their own door and rights.

Revised 23 October 2026: PORT-006 roommate and transfer obligations. A charge names the resident, co-tenants and guarantors whose membership includes its due day: a leaver is named through their leaving day, a joiner from their joining day and never on earlier charges. `tenancy.transfer` carries every member who joined before the move-in to the new lease from the move-in day (listed `stay` members remain), closing their old place the day before, atomically. The record names people; it is not a legal opinion about who owes what. Deposits, their disposition, final accounts and complete proration reconciliation stay open and wait on ACCT-003/004.

released_readme.text: # Terrace Residential property management for an independent manager or landlord. Keep tenancies, recorded rent, photographed inspections, reviewed maintenance and owner statements in your own Cloudflare account. MIT licensed. Terrace records charges and money received elsewhere. It does not yet collect rent, hold or move funds, reconcile a trust account, hold security deposits, screen applicants or publish listings. See [ACCEPTANCE.md](ACCEPTANCE.md) for the first release. ## Clone and run Install Git. RER selects the project's pinned Node 22.20.0 for project commands. Run one line to install the CLI, clone Terrace and start it: ```sh npx -y @runeditrun/rer dev just-every/run-terrace ``` Or, as [run-terrace.com/run](https://run-terrace.com/run) shows it, install rer first (it brings its own Node when you have none) and then start Terrace: ```sh curl -fsSL https://runeditrun.com/install.sh | sh rer dev just-every/run-terrace ``` To start it again later, run `cd run-terrace && rer dev`. `rer dev` installs the pinned dependencies, prepares a local D1 database and owner, applies migrations and starts the app. Allow several minutes on the first run. Open its `RER_OPEN` link privately: it signs you in as the local owner. Confirm the owner on **Finish setup**, then open Terrace. The link is a credential; do not share it publicly. Local development mail is silently suppressed and sends no external email. For an installation with your real owner mailbox, run `npx -y @runeditrun/rer install just-every/run-terrace`, then `rer setup --owner-email you@example.com` from the checkout before the first `rer dev`. The interactive `rer setup` also accepts your mailbox. Do not change an existing owner's identity by overwriting settings. Stop with `rer dev --stop` (or Ctrl-C). Rerunning `rer dev` reuses a compatible running instance. Stop dev or preview before a build or verification. If a command times out, repeat it and follow its recovery message; do not reset data to repair a startup. ## Try a disposable workspace Run `rer demo` for a fresh signed-in **Terrace Demo**, with eight tenancies, rent history, reviewed decisions, photographed inspections and maintenance. Stop it with `rer demo --stop`; each launch starts fresh. [DEMO.md](DEMO.md) describes isolation and real-read / mocked-send behavior. ## First working cycle 1. **Tenancies → Add a tenancy.** Enter the address, owner and tenant names/emails, lease dates and rent cadence. The chosen tenancy carries into its selected screen. Prepare a renewal with its source reference; approve the exact proposed terms in **Prepared decisions**. Previous terms remain in the archive. 2. **Rent & arrears.** Select the tenancy. Add a charge with a unique reference. Record an amount already received in your external system, with its date and unique bank/receipt reference. A receipt cannot exceed a charge's remaining balance. Use **Reduce an incorrect charge** for an explained correction. Prepare an arrears follow-up and approve it on **Tenancies**. No follow-up email is sent automatically. Download a period **Owner statement** CSV; its opening and closing amounts are rent receivables, not owner disbursements. 3. **Inspections & maintenance → New inspection.** Save a date and notes, upload a JPEG/PNG up to 1.5 MB, then complete the inspection. At least one photo and notes are required. Prepare maintenance with its vendor, due date and estimate. Approve the exact work and checklist, then choose **Dispatch approved work by email** to send through your installation mail provider. Record sourced technician replies and human escalation for missed commitments. Provider acceptance does not confirm delivery or resolution. You can also download the `.eml` packet, send it in your email client and record that external handoff. The approval snapshot and photo fingerprint are retained. 4. **Move in.** Paste [fixtures/terrace-tenancies.csv](fixtures/terrace-tenancies.csv), use a stable namespace, preview the rows and approve their displayed fingerprint. Inspect the journal and original, or undo the import. Undo stops if a tenancy acquired rent, inspections, maintenance or later edits. See the exact [CSV contract](docs/move-in.md). The fixture is a documented-shape example, not a verified vendor export. 5. **Data & access.** Download a backup. To restore, start a separate empty installation and upload the `.rer` file there. The owner records and reviews resident access/erasure requests and legal holds. Eligible lease evidence is deleted; accounting identity stays through its retention or hold, and financial evidence is then retained under an opaque alias. Download a new backup after erasure and provide it as the later journal when restoring any older backup. Owners control imports, backup, restore, erasure and operators. Admins are property managers: they record rent and inspections and approve proposals. Members can read the portfolio and prepare proposals only. Invite people in **Data & access**. Agents should use a member account and the [command API](API.md); a person's owner/admin account approves. ## Backup, restore and checks The browser supports archives up to 20 MB. The CLI supports larger archives: ```sh rer export --output exports/terrace.rer # In an empty destination with the same schema: rer import --input /absolute/path/terrace.rer --yes # When the source has since erased data: rer import --input /absolute/path/old.rer --journal /absolute/path/later.rer --yes rer verify ``` Archives include all product tables, original import bytes, journals and photograph BLOBs. Auth sessions, credentials, development outbox and private configuration are excluded. Restore preserves the destination owner and refuses a nonempty product destination, corrupt archives and a supplied erasure fence. Keep backups private. An offline archive cannot know about a later erasure unless you supply the later journal. `rer reset --yes` removes local data and settings; export first if they matter. Verification builds the app, typechecks it and runs the public-door product journeys, the run-site build test, plus the emitted-Worker runtime and ordinary email-link checks at the mail provider boundary. Build and deploy do not run tests. Test cap: 200. Push and PR Verify runs source/site, typecheck, product and emitted-Worker shards in parallel. Release tags (`v*`), nightly and manual Nightly journeys run the full plan; the SAFE-007 clean-install/reviewed-upgrade, OPEN-001 published command and REPORT-005 native custom-report journeys run there, outside the push wall. See [VERIFY-WORKFLOW.md](VERIFY-WORKFLOW.md) to add them without dropping checks. `rer describe`, `rer check --profile first-party` and `rer doctor` explain the declared operations and local setup. ## Deploy to your Cloudflare account Use the RunEditRun Cloudflare account for this seed's managed deployment. Your own fork can be installed into your own account. No domain is needed for a workers.dev deployment. The Worker/project/database/package identifiers in the committed declarations are stable; do not rename them during deployment. 1. Finish `rer setup` with your real owner email. Commit any intentional source/branding changes; real deploy refuses dirty tracked files. 2. Review [Cloudflare hosting pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/), [D1 storage pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/pricing/) and [Resend email pricing](https://resend.com/pricing) before connecting them: those providers bill your account. Terrace has no author license key, paid gate, unit/seat cap or per-payment fee. Both deploy and dry-run print these disclosures before the provider deployment hook runs. Configure `deploy.json`'s nonsecret `MAIL_FROM` to a sender verified with Resend. It currently uses a non-deliverable example address. Obtain a Cloudflare API token scoped to the target account and a Resend API key. Configure Cloudflare through RER's private setup; do not commit credentials. 3. Provide `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `OWNER_EMAIL`, `SESSION_SECRET`, `SETUP_TOKEN` and `MAIL_API_KEY` in the deployment process's private environment. Session/setup values must be private random secrets of at least 32 characters. RER's deploy kit names any missing inputs. Never paste secret values into command history or Git. 4. Validate and then deploy: ```sh rer deploy --dry-run rer deploy ``` The dry run builds and validates without contacting providers. Real deploy provisions declared D1 resources, applies migrations, uploads the Worker/assets and checks deployment identity and asset health. Keep the returned workers.dev address. On the new installation, claim its first owner at **Finish setup** with the configured setup token, then use the emailed sign-in link. If the provider settings are incomplete, fix them before calling the deployment ready. The static run site includes the Terrace homepage, `/run` instructions and repository Markdown guides. Build it with `rer build --site`. The public site is at https://run-terrace.com and updates automatically through GitHub Actions on pushes to `main`. Email delivery remains unverified. ## Reviewed upgrades Back up first and merge the chosen upstream commit in a separate review installation, preserving owner changes and private configuration. Follow [the upgrade and diagnostics guide](docs/upgrades.md) before changing a live installation. ## Source Foundation: `runeditrun/base` `fc0e1041efa55771142bbb57c4ab4743147e264d`. Package-mode CLI: the exact `@runeditrun/rer` devDependency in `package.json`. `base-copies.json` records the vendored runtime copies. [SOURCE.md](SOURCE.md) records the Base and sibling reuse. Terrace uses one set of tokens (lavender paper, navy ink and the violet ramp of its stepped-blocks mark): its palette in `public/fonts/fonts.css` and the `--rer-*` theme tokens Base's installer reads in `public/rer-theme.css`, and self-hosted Geist, Figtree and JetBrains Mono ([public/fonts](public/fonts/README.md)) across its run site, setup, sign-in and server-rendered app. The explicit OPS-003 installed-container cadence journey is `node tests/workflow-cadence.mjs` on a clean committed checkout. It builds the production container artifact and waits for two real hourly Cron deliveries (up to 125 minutes), without direct dispatch or a fake clock; it is deliberately outside push Verify. Its private local results name the candidate SHA. This does not measure Cloudflare hosted trigger delivery. ## Capacity readiness SAFE-009 remains partial. On a clean committed checkout, `node tests/capacity.mjs` creates a disposable local Worker and D1 with 500 units, 60 properties, 600 leases (including 50 past and 50 future leases), 150 dated owners, 1,200 residents, 250 vendors and 24 months of rent history, all through public commands. It checks the counts and measures local rent posting, as-of rent roll and delinquency, including a duplicate-run check. `CAPACITY_RESULT` selects a private receipt file outside the repository; the receipt records date, commit, counts and measured times. This journey runs separately from push Verify. These are local readiness measurements. They do not prove the required Cloudflare reference deployment, bank auto-matching, three-way reconciliation, complete owner statement batch or staff and portal p95. `node tests/capacity.mjs --require-reference` fails while those required measurements are absent. ACCT-006 and ACCT-012 still need their operating foundations before a full reference capacity receipt and setup disclosure can be claimed.
